# Titles

## At a glance

| Action | Shortest call | Inference/defaults | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `createTitle` | `createTitle({ text: "Title" })` | Top, plot-left alignment, default styles | Semantic text and concrete title graphics |
| `editTitle` | `editTitle({ position: "bottom" })` | Preserves omitted text, layout, wrapping, and style | Rematerialized title graphics |
| `removeTitle` | `removeTitle()` | Existing chart title | Title and subtitle resource removed |

## `createTitle(options)`

Creates one chart title and an optional subtitle on any Canvas edge.

Facet and concat parents support the same four edges. Their inferred Canvas reserves an outer
lane for the title and subtitle, outside retained axes, headers and shared legends.
Alignment follows the union of the child plots; left and right titles rotate with
their subtitle. Editing the title or composition layout recomputes that lane.

Top titles use the nearest retained chart content, including axis text, facet
headers, and shared legends, rather than leaving an extra gap for empty child
Canvas margins. When the reserved lane has spare space, the title/subtitle block
moves toward that content to leave 16 logical pixels. Already tighter lanes,
child sizes and margins, and explicit facet `topLane: "shared"` layouts are
preserved.

On a concat parent, omit `target` to create or edit one overall title. Use
`target: { childPath: ["main"] }` to title only the named child view. Parent and
child titles are independent; removing the parent title preserves child titles.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program.createTitle({
  text: "The trend of acceleration by year",
  subtitle: "from 1970 to 1982"
});
```

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | non-empty string | required |
| `subtitle` | non-empty string | omitted |
| `position` | `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, or `"right"` | `"top"` |
| `align` | `"left"`, `"center"`, or `"right"` | `"left"` |
| `offset` | finite number | `0` |
| `gap` | non-negative number | `8` |
| `maxWidth` | positive number | omitted; no wrapping |
| `wrap` | `"word"` or `"character"` | `"word"` when `maxWidth` is set |
| `lineHeight` | positive number | each font size × `1.2` |
| `subtitleLineHeight` | finite number ≥ subtitle font size | shared `lineHeight`, or subtitle font size × `1.2` |
| `titleStyle` | text style object | default title style |
| `subtitleStyle` | text style object | default subtitle style |

Both style objects accept `color`, `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, `fontWeight`, and
`fontStyle: "normal" | "italic"` (normal by default). Title and subtitle styles
are independent; for italic credits, pass `subtitleStyle: { fontStyle: "italic" }`.
Style edits preserve omitted fields. Measured wrapping distinguishes normal and italic fonts.
Numeric weights follow the shared [Canvas font-weight policy](./api/marks/text/#font-weights).
The defaults are:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
{
  titleStyle: {
    color: "#0f172a",
    fontSize: 22,
    fontFamily: "sans-serif",
    fontWeight: 600
  },
  subtitleStyle: {
    color: "#64748b",
    fontSize: 14,
    fontFamily: "sans-serif",
    fontWeight: "normal"
  }
}
```

## Position, alignment, and wrapping

Alignment uses the plot bounds rather than the full Canvas: left aligns with
the plot's left edge, center with its midpoint, and right with its right edge.
For a facet, the alignment span is the union of the translated child plot
bounds. Child margins, axis labels and titles, facet padding, and shared
legends do not pull the title away from the visual center of the plots.
For a left or right title, the same values mean the top, center, and bottom of
the plot edge. Left titles rotate counter-clockwise and right titles rotate
clockwise; top and bottom titles remain horizontal.

Set `maxWidth` to wrap text before edge rotation. Word wrapping prefers
whitespace and falls back to Unicode-safe character wrapping for an oversized
word. Both modes preserve whole Unicode grapheme clusters, including combining
marks, Hangul syllable sequences, and emoji sequences. A single cluster wider
than `maxWidth` stays intact on its own line. Layout uses `Intl.Segmenter`
grapheme boundaries and deterministic text metrics; Unicode boundary rules
follow the runtime's Unicode version. Renderers draw the concrete lines already in
`graphicSpec`; they do not wrap text again. Title and subtitle strings accept
explicit newline characters. Each hard line wraps independently when `maxWidth`
is set. Leading, interior, and trailing blank lines reserve vertical spacing
without creating empty painted text. Each title or subtitle must contain at
least one non-empty hard line. Font-family and color values remain single-line
strings.

Set `subtitleLineHeight` to control only the subtitle's line spacing. For example,
`subtitleStyle: { fontSize: 8 }, subtitleLineHeight: 10` keeps a larger heading
unchanged while spacing credit lines by 10 logical pixels. This option supports
explicit line breaks without `maxWidth`, and overrides shared `lineHeight` only
for the subtitle. Omitted edits retain it, including while `subtitle: false`
hides the subtitle. Its value must cover the stored subtitle font size even
while hidden; increasing that font size requires a compatible spacing in the
same edit. Removing the complete title removes the setting as well.

With `createCanvas({ plot: { width, height } })`, the title and subtitle sit
16 pixels beyond the occupied guides on the requested edge, plus `offset`.
The measured space includes Cartesian axes, parallel-coordinate dimension
titles and tick labels, polar axis text, and outside legends. Editing those
guides or resizing the Canvas recalculates the clearance; it does not accumulate
extra spacing. The plot dimensions stay fixed while insufficient outer margins
grow to contain the title.

With a fixed outer `width` and `height`, the requested margins must contain the
title and avoid same-edge guide collisions. Insufficient space is an error;
increase the margins or change the placement explicitly.

## `editTitle(options)`

Partially edits the existing title. At least one option is required.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const edited = program.editTitle({
  position: "bottom",
  align: "center",
  maxWidth: 280,
  titleStyle: { fontSize: 20 }
});
```

Omitted properties remain unchanged, and style objects merge only the supplied
leaves. `text` and string `subtitle` replace semantic text. Use
`subtitle: false` to remove the subtitle; a later string recreates it.
Wrapping and layout changes rebuild the concrete text lines without changing
unrelated chart state.

## `removeTitle()`

Remove the complete chart title resource, including subtitle text, concrete
graphics, and stored layout settings:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const untitled = program.removeTitle();
```

The action accepts no options and requires an existing title.

## Stored result

The title and subtitle strings are stored in `semanticSpec`. Alignment,
spacing, wrapping configuration, and text appearance are graphical state.
Resolved line breaks, coordinates, and rotations are concrete text graphics.
Canvas size and margin changes explicitly rematerialize their positions.

## Errors and limitations

The library supports one title and one optional subtitle. `wrap` and
`lineHeight` require `maxWidth`; explicit `lineHeight` must cover every visible
font size. Missing margin space and same-edge guide collisions are errors.
The collision check includes Cartesian axis components and every legend family,
including borders and combined categorical/size groups. Creating the title first
or last follows the same rule. Canvas and scale updates check the final positions
of dependent guides; rejected changes leave the earlier program unchanged.

## Shift a title along its edge

Use `alongOffset` in `createTitle` or `editTitle` to move the complete title/subtitle block along its selected edge. The signed finite logical-pixel value defaults to zero: positive moves top/bottom titles right and left/right titles down. It is independent of the existing outward `offset`. On facet parents, the horizontal shift uses the translated child-plot union and remains through facet layout, guide, and scale edits. Facet title and subtitle text must fit the composed Canvas. The shift remains through Canvas edits, and all occupied-bounds and guide-collision checks still apply. Set it to zero to restore the normal alignment anchor.

## Related

[Canvas](./api/canvas/) · [Guides](./api/guides/) ·
[Semantic and graphical state](./concepts/semantic-and-graphics/)

Component styles also accept `align: "left" | "center" | "right"`. For example,
`editTitle({titleStyle: {align: "center"}, subtitleStyle: {align: "right"}})`
aligns each component inside the measured block while the top-level `align`
continues positioning that block relative to the plot. Omission keeps the
existing component alignment, including on rotated left/right titles.

<!-- Source: /api/rendering/ -->

# Rendering

Render one fully materialized `ChartProgram` to Browser Canvas, a browser-safe
SVG string, a Node PNG file, or a single-page vector PDF. Choose the target
based on where the output runs and how it will be consumed.

Canvas and SVG need only `npm install ggaction`. For Node PNG and PDF, install
the optional native backend with `npm install ggaction @napi-rs/canvas`.
Importing the PNG/PDF entry works without the backend; calling it then reports
the required installation command. No dependency is installed automatically.

Canvas, PNG, and PDF keep the requested font families first and share one ordered
list of common CJK, Unicode, and emoji fallback families. The drawing host skips
unavailable families. Exact embedded font bindings use only their prepared alias.
Text and layout remain unchanged; fonts are never downloaded. Install an
appropriate font on the drawing host for the scripts you use, or specify your own
ordered font-family list. SVG uses the browser's font resolution.

## At a glance

| Target | Environment | Shortest call | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Browser Canvas | Browser | `render(program, context)` | Drawing into an existing interactive page |
| SVG | Browser or Node.js 20+ | `renderToSVG(program)` | Embedding or saving scalable markup |
| Node PNG | Node.js 20+ | `renderToPNG(program, { output })` | Producing a raster file at an explicit pixel density |
| Node PDF | Node.js 20+ | `renderToPDF(program, { output })` | Producing a selectable, single-page vector document |

Rendering consumes a completed program's `graphicSpec`. It does not read
datasets, semantic encodings, context, or trace to infer missing output.

For pointer inspection of the rendered Canvas or SVG, use an explicit
[interaction session](./api/interaction/).

## First render

Run this ES module in a bundler-based browser page containing `<canvas id="chart"></canvas>`:

> **Executable complete.** Use a browser ES module with a canvas element whose id is chart; all input rows are included.

```javascript
import { chart, render } from "ggaction/basic";
const program = chart().createCanvas({ width: 480, height: 320 })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 1, y: 2 }, { x: 2, y: 4 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: "x", y: "y" });
render(program, document.querySelector("#chart").getContext("2d"));
```

The result has two points. The output adapters below consume this same completed
program. Text measurement is an optional authoring step described after the output examples.

## Automated environment checks

CI and release qualification exercise these environments against installed
packages. The release jobs all consume the same candidate tarball.

| Environment | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Ubuntu, Node.js 20, 22, and 24 | Package installation, public entries, declarations, and consumer workflows |
| macOS and Windows, Node.js 22 | Native PNG/PDF buffers and files, image dimensions, SVG, and snapshot round trips |
| Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit supplied by the pinned Playwright dependency | Canvas and SVG clipping, gradients, text alignment, resizing, DPR 1 and 2, accessible labels, and SVG downloads |

Browser checks use a shared representative graphic scene; they do not imply
coverage of every browser release, operating system, font, or device. Native
checks use the optional Canvas backend installed on each runner.

SVG, PNG, and PDF options must be plain objects (including objects with a null
prototype). Unknown option keys are rejected before output is written; for
example, use `pixelRatio`, not `pixelratio`, for PNG density.

## Complete example program

Every rendering fragment below continues from this complete program:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const observations = [
  { displacement: 97, acceleration: 14.5, origin: "Japan" },
  { displacement: 140, acceleration: 15.5, origin: "USA" },
  { displacement: 86, acceleration: 16.4, origin: "Japan" }
];

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({
    width: 640,
    height: 400,
    margin: { top: 30, right: 130, bottom: 60, left: 70 }
  })
  .createData({ values: observations })
  .createScatterPlot({
    x: "displacement",
    y: "acceleration",
    color: "origin",
    shape: "origin"
  });
```

## Browser Canvas

In a browser page containing `<canvas id="chart"></canvas>`, render with its 2D
context:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { render } from "ggaction";

const context = document.querySelector("#chart").getContext("2d");
render(program, context);
```

The optional `pixelRatio` increases physical output density while retaining
logical chart coordinates. For an HTML Canvas, ggaction also preserves the
logical CSS width and height while enlarging the backing store:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
render(program, context, { pixelRatio: 2 });
```

Raster backing dimensions are the logical dimension multiplied by
`pixelRatio`, rounded to the nearest whole pixel with a minimum of one pixel.
This leaves fractional logical dimensions unchanged in CSS and SVG output.
Canvas and PNG preflight the complete allocation before changing the backing
store: each physical side is limited to `32767` pixels and the complete image
to `16777216` pixels.

An explicit mark `blend: "multiply"`, `"screen"`, or `"difference"` also allocates one transparent glyph source
within its visible fill and stroke bounds. It obeys the same per-surface limits, including
pixel ratio and nested clips, and is reused while painting individual items.
Unsupported custom Canvas contexts fail before resizing or clearing the chart;
ordinary drawing does not require the extra surface/compositing capabilities.

## SVG output

The browser-safe SVG entry returns a complete SVG document string without
reading the DOM or filesystem. Assign it to a trusted application container or
save the returned string with the file API available in your environment.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { renderToSVG } from "ggaction/svg";

const svg = renderToSVG(program, {
  title: "Quarterly revenue",
  description: "Revenue by quarter",
  resourceNamespace: "quarterlyRevenue"
});
```

The root `width`, `height`, and `viewBox` use the program's logical Canvas
dimensions. Optional `title` and `description` strings become escaped
`<title>` and `<desc>` children. Repeated calls with the same program and
options return the same string. Resource IDs use a deterministic hash of
`graphicSpec` by default. When multiple copies of the same chart will coexist
in one HTML document, give each call a distinct `resourceNamespace` so their
gradient and clipping IDs cannot collide. It must start with an ASCII letter
and contain only ASCII letters, numbers, `_`, or `-`.

For example, a browser application can place the generated document in an
existing output container:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
document.querySelector("#svg-output").innerHTML = svg;
```

## PNG output

The Node-only entry point writes a completed program directly to PNG.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { renderToPNG } from "ggaction/png";

const result = await renderToPNG(program, {
  output: "./output/chart.png",
  pixelRatio: 2
});
```

Missing output directories are created. A logical 640×400 chart at ratio 2
produces a 1280×800 image. The result contains the absolute `output`, physical
`width` and `height`, `pixelRatio`, and byte count.

## PNG in memory

For HTTP responses, object storage, or other host-controlled output, use the
Node-only `renderToPNGBuffer(program, { pixelRatio })` from `ggaction/png`.
Options are optional and accept only `pixelRatio` (default 1). The result is
`{ buffer, width, height, pixelRatio, bytes }`, where `buffer` is a caller-owned
`Uint8Array` and dimensions are physical pixels. Each call returns independent
bytes. The result object is frozen; its byte array remains writable.

Canvas drawing and geometry validation are synchronous. PNG encoding runs
asynchronously in the native backend; the returned Promise does not move chart
authoring or Canvas drawing off the JavaScript thread.

## PDF output

The Node-only PDF entry writes one completed chart as one vector PDF page:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { renderToPDF } from "ggaction/pdf";

const result = await renderToPDF(program, {
  output: "./output/chart.pdf",
  metadata: {
    title: "Quarterly revenue",
    author: "Example",
    subject: "Revenue by quarter",
    keywords: ["revenue", "quarterly"]
  }
});
```

Missing output directories are created. The page width and height in PDF points
use the program's logical Canvas dimensions. The native vector backend
represents page boxes as positive integers, so PDF output requires each logical
dimension to be an integer no larger than `16777216`; unsupported dimensions
are rejected before replacing the output file. The frozen result contains the
absolute `output`, logical `width` and `height`, `pages: 1`, and byte count.
Metadata is optional; it accepts only non-empty `title`, `author`, and `subject`
strings plus an array of non-empty `keywords`.

Ordinary Text remains selectable/searchable PDF text. Paths, strokes, fills, clipping,
opacity, dashes, and linear gradients remain vector output. An explicit mark
`blend: "multiply"`, `"screen"`, or `"difference"`, or explicit legend recipe-layer opacity rasterizes only
that glyph's fill-and-outline source for native PDF compositing; the rest of the
page stays vector. The adapter does not
rasterize the complete chart or accept `pixelRatio`. Nested Canvas translations apply to
text as well as shapes, so concat children with different plot margins retain
their distinct title and axis-label origins in PDF output.

The current renderers support concrete canvas, collection, circle, rect, line,
text, and `M/L/C/Z` command-path graphics. Path and line strokes may use concrete
dash arrays. They validate values with the same concrete property contract used
by `editGraphics`. The paint string `"none"` draws no fill or stroke in every backend,
including text fill and Canvas backgrounds. It never reuses an earlier drawing color.

Rect and closed-path fills may be solid strings or item-local linear-gradient
paint values. Gradient endpoints are normalized against the final fill geometry;
path stroke width does not expand that coordinate box. The renderer creates the
Canvas gradient only for the current draw call and never stores backend objects
in `graphicSpec`.

Canvas, PNG, and PDF share a native drawing backend. Before creating or changing
native output, they require every geometry and style number passed to that
backend—including path controls, nested translations, stroke/dash sizes, text
size/rotation, and resolved gradient endpoints—to have magnitude no greater
than `16777216` (`2^24`). Derived rect/circle and nested-clip extents, gradient
direction lengths, cumulative translations, and pixel-ratio-scaled values use
the same boundary. SVG remains browser-safe string serialization and preserves
the complete finite JavaScript number range.

Line curve actions resolve interpolation into those commands before rendering.
Canvas, SVG, and PDF execute `L` and cubic `C` segments but do not read curve
names or calculate control points.

## PDF in memory

The Node-only `renderToPDFBuffer(program, { metadata })` from `ggaction/pdf`
accepts the same optional metadata as file output and returns
`{ buffer, width, height, pages: 1, bytes }`. Options may be omitted. The
caller-owned `Uint8Array` contains one vector PDF page; dimensions are logical
PDF points. The result object is frozen and its bytes remain writable.

Both memory functions reject `output`; PDF also rejects `pixelRatio`. File
functions call their corresponding memory function before creating directories
or replacing files. PDF construction and encoding are synchronous even though
the public function returns a Promise. Use a host worker for expensive jobs.

## Errors and limitations

Rendering never reads `semanticSpec`. Every drawable property must already be
concrete. Canvas/PNG `pixelRatio` must be positive at native precision, no
greater than `16777216`, and produce physical dimensions within the raster
limits above. PDF is vector output and does not accept `pixelRatio`, but its
page and drawing geometry use the Canvas-backed native limits. Native numeric
range failures are rejected before Canvas mutation or PNG/PDF file replacement.
SVG uses neither native nor raster limits. PDF options and metadata use closed
key sets. SVG `resourceNamespace` follows the identifier form above, and SVG
text, attributes, titles, and descriptions reject characters that XML 1.0
cannot represent; emoji, joiners, variation selectors, and right-to-left text
remain unchanged.

## Accessible data alternatives

`exportAccessibleData(program, { target? })` from `ggaction/accessibility` works in
Browser and Node with Full or Basic editable programs. It returns a deeply frozen
`{ schemaVersion: 1, title, views }` without changing the program or its trace.
`title` is the semantic title string or `null`.

> **alternative.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resource selectors used here: `target: "sales"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";
import { exportAccessibleData } from "ggaction/accessibility";

const program = chart().createCanvas()
  .createData({ values: [
    { quarter: "Q1", revenue: 12 }, { quarter: "Q1", revenue: 18 },
    { quarter: "Q2", revenue: 20 }
  ] })
  .createBarPlot({ id: "sales", x: "quarter",
    y: { field: "revenue", aggregate: "mean" }, guides: false });
const alternative = exportAccessibleData(program, { target: "sales" });
console.log(alternative.views[0]);
```

The first quarter is one aggregated bar with endpoints 0 and 15, rather than two
source rows. The second bar has endpoints 0 and 20.

Each owner view has `ownerId`, `markType`, `columns`, `rows`, and `units`. A column
has a unique `key`, semantic channel `role`, and `component` mark ID, with `field`,
`aggregate`, and `unit` when applicable. Keys combine component ID and channel
with `:`. A row has `component`, a `series` field/value record, and `values` keyed
by those column keys. Composite owners include their owned graphical components
in the same view; rows from different components may use different columns.
Absent values remain absent. Temporal position values use UTC milliseconds and
corresponding columns declare `unit: "utc-milliseconds"`; other units are not
guessed. Area layouts can also supply `lower` and `upper` endpoint roles. Parallel
coordinate dimensions use their field names as column roles.

Omitting `target` exports every stable chart owner in semantic order. An explicit
target must name a stable owner; requesting an owned component reports its owner.
A composition returns child views in composition order, each with `ownerId`,
`kind: "composition-child"`, `title`, and nested `views`. Facet children also have
a `facet` field/value record. Grid facets contain both row and column fields;
repeats contain `repeatField` and `channel`. To select a mark within a composition,
pass the explicit child program to this function. A composition-level target is
rejected instead of choosing among repeated IDs.

Point, bar, histogram, line, area, arc, rule, tick, rect, and their supported
composite owners use final materialized data. This includes aggregate cells, bin
endpoints, ordered path points, stack endpoints, error intervals, and final mark
filters. Attached text labels repeat owner data and do not create additional views.
Standalone text marks and custom unsupported owners raise an error identifying
the owner; the function never silently returns a partial set of views. Incomplete
marks and render-only snapshots are rejected. Empty charts return an empty list.

The output describes the authored chart data, including data outside a clipped
viewport or styled with zero opacity. It does not reverse scale mappings from
pixels or infer units, prose, missing observations, or statistical explanations.
The host supplies meaningful captions, HTML tables, and ARIA relationships. Use
DOM `textContent` for user-controlled titles, column labels, and values; do not
insert them as HTML. Keep the alternative synchronized by exporting the updated
program after an edit.

## Explicit whole-glyph opacity

Concrete circle/rect/path/line/text nodes accept `blend:'normal'` as an explicit
whole-glyph source-over instruction. The renderer paints the fill and stroke or
outline together, attenuates the source once, and composites it. This marker is
emitted for explicit legend recipe-layer opacity. Omission keeps ordinary painting
unchanged. Containers and image nodes do not accept blend markers.

The same five glyph types also accept multiply, screen, and difference. The public
mark actions treat `blend:'normal'` as a semantic reset which removes the optional
concrete blend field. See [per-item blend modes](./api/appearance/mark-style/#blending-each-mark-item)
for the supported mark and facade options.

## Transition scenes

`createTransitionScene(program)` from `ggaction/scene` is a read-only extension API.
It returns a frozen, structured-cloneable version-1 scene with native `width` and
`height`, SVG `definitions`, and ordered `nodes`. Each node contains an opaque
`key`, concrete `type`, path `topology` signature, escaped SVG fragment, absolute
parent `offset`, and intersected canvas `clip` rectangle. Keys are correspondence
hints, not editable graphic addresses. Renderers still consume concrete graphics.
Compound path fill rules are retained in each SVG fragment. Path owner clips are
preserved through scoped definitions and fragment wrappers. The SVG `clip`
rectangle retains the rectangular viewport/owner intersection; path clips apply
inside the fragment so fractional edges are not clipped twice.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resource selectors used here: `data: "data"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';
import { createTransitionScene } from 'ggaction/scene';
const program = chart().createCanvas({ width: 600, height: 400 })
  .createData({ id: 'data', values: [{ x: 1, y: 2 }, { x: 2, y: 3 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ id: 'points', data: 'data', x: { field: 'x' }, y: { field: 'y' } });
const scene = createTransitionScene(program);
```

The optional `@ggaction/transition` package owns browser playback, timing,
interruption and reduced-motion behavior. Creating a scene does not append an
action or modify a program. Scene extraction shares an ordered concrete traversal; version 1 additionally serializes SVG.
Point/member correspondence survives filters, reordered rows and facet placement;
identical records receive occurrence keys. Selection resolvers supply membership
for supported aggregate and series marks. Changed membership, unsupported
selection structures and changed path topology use conservative replacement
rather than an invented data relationship. Arbitrary data-transform lineage and
many-to-one morphs are not inferred. Keys are opaque and only comparable within
a related dataset/program history, not globally persistent row identifiers.

### Canvas transition scenes

`createTransitionScene(program, { format: 'canvas' })` returns a frozen version-2
scene. It shares version-1 keys, order, topology, offsets and clips, but each node
contains concrete `properties` instead of an SVG fragment. Properties include
resolved path commands, multiline text, gradients and blend settings. It contains
no DOM, Canvas resources, semantic compilation or data tables. The default format
remains SVG/version 1; unknown formats are rejected.

Canvas nodes also retain optional `clips`: the explicit outer-to-inner clip
frames in global logical coordinates: rectangle tuples or
`{ type: "path", commands, fillRule? }` objects. The root physical viewport is implicit.
This preserves fractional-edge coverage and owner clips inside nested Canvases;
Canvas `clip` remains their intersected bounds, including path bounds. If an intermediate node omits `clips`,
its single `clip` rectangle is used. Retain the supplied frames when animating
an unchanged clipping hierarchy.

`renderTransitionScene(scene, context, { pixelRatio = 1 } = {})` paints version-2
scenes with the ordinary Canvas renderer. It uses the same primitive validation,
paint order, nested clipping and isolated blending as `render`. It sizes and clears
the target Canvas, keeping logical dimensions independent of output density.
Invalid scene versions, duplicate keys and invalid geometry are rejected.
Playback code may supply intermediate concrete properties; this function does
not perform interpolation or schedule frames. Mutable intermediate scenes are
not cached. Each intermediate node must retain a unique key and valid concrete
properties. Do not use keys as editable graphic addresses.

Browser example (with an existing `<canvas id="chart">` element):

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resource selectors used here: `data: "data"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';
import { createTransitionScene, renderTransitionScene } from 'ggaction/scene';
const program = chart().createCanvas({ width: 600, height: 400 })
  .createData({ id: 'data', values: [{ x: 1, y: 2 }, { x: 2, y: 3 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ id: 'points', data: 'data', x: { field: 'x' }, y: { field: 'y' } });
const scene = createTransitionScene(program, { format: 'canvas' });
renderTransitionScene(scene, document.querySelector('#chart').getContext('2d'), {
  pixelRatio: window.devicePixelRatio
});
```

## Measured text layout

Full charts support `applyTextMetrics({ profile })` and `removeTextMetrics()`.
These authoring actions recalculate text layout before rendering. A profile has
exactly `schemaVersion: 1`, a nonempty `id`, and a `measurements` array. Each entry
requires `text`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, and `width`, and may
include `fontStyle: "normal" | "italic"` (normal when omitted).

The host measures strings in the font it will use. Width is in logical pixels,
not output pixels multiplied by device pixel ratio. Font size must be positive;
width must be finite and nonnegative. Weight is one of 100, 200, …, 900.
Duplicate text/family/size/weight/style combinations are rejected. Empty profiles and
empty strings are valid.

This complete browser example waits for fonts and measures the full string and
word candidates that its title wrapping will use:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";

await document.fonts.ready;
const context = document.createElement("canvas").getContext("2d");
const fontFamily = "sans-serif";
const fontSize = 20;
const fontWeight = 400;
context.font = `${fontWeight} ${fontSize}px ${fontFamily}`;
const profile = {
  schemaVersion: 1,
  id: "page-fonts",
  measurements: ["Alpha Beta", "Alpha", "Beta"].map(text => ({
    text, fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight,
    width: context.measureText(text).width
  }))
};
const measured = chart()
  .applyTextMetrics({ profile })
  .createCanvas({ width: 500, height: 350, margin: 80 })
  .createTitle({
    text: "Alpha Beta", maxWidth: 100,
    titleStyle: { fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight }
  });
const estimated = measured.removeTextMetrics();
```

Matching uses the exact string, family, size, and normalized weight. Omitted
family uses `sans-serif`; omitted/`normal` weight is 400 and `bold` is 700.
Numeric weights use the renderer's rounding to 100 and clamping to 100–900;
strings `"100"` through `"900"` match those numeric values. Unmatched strings or
styles, including relative CSS weights, use the existing deterministic estimate.
Wrapping may measure partial words and candidate lines; include those strings
when exact measurements are needed for them.

Applying clones and freezes the profile and replaces any active profile. It
recalculates titles, axes, legends, labels, and composition layout without
changing typography. A composition applies the profile to its root and nested
children, adopting Basic children as Full snapshots; replacement/insertion children and retained facet/repeat edits inherit
it. Removal clears the profile throughout that composition and restores
estimates; it does not restore earlier child profiles. Removing without an active
profile is an error. Failed layout leaves the original program intact.

Later domain edits and source revisions use the stored profile. Editable
[persistence](./data-updates/#save-and-restore-snapshots) preserves and validates it. Render-only snapshots
contain the already laid-out graphics. Changing the original profile or loading
a font later does not change an existing program. Apply a new measured profile
to update layout after fonts change. Canvas, SVG, PNG, and PDF draw the resulting
text graphics; they do not rewrap or replace the authoring measurements.

### Identity across revisions

Transition scenes use the materialized item identity in `graphicSpec`. Explicit
row keys retain an item across reorderings and value edits. Generated rows retain
identity only when `reviseData` receives a `rowMap`. New independent datasets
have separate identity namespaces. A series keeps its semantic key while changed
ordered membership changes its topology fingerprint. Composition child paths
participate in identity, so moving an item to another child produces enter/exit.
SVG scene version 1 and Canvas scene version 2 keep their existing shapes.
Graphic-only snapshots retain the same scene identities.

## Embedded images

Full authoring uses `prepareImageResource(program, request, host)` followed by
`program.createImageResource({prepared, requestToken})` or
`program.replaceImageResource({prepared, requestToken})`. The host explicitly loads
bytes and reports decoded dimensions. The synchronous action requires the exact
prepared receiver and current request token. Keep the token in application state
and change it when a request is superseded. `createImageMark` and `editImageMark`
place one named image; [the image example](./tutorials/image-assets/) shows
contain, cover, fill, alignment and clipping from one retained source.

For browser Canvas, prepare embedded bytes with an application-owned decoder:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `URL`, `canvas`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
import { prepareImageRendering, render } from "ggaction";

// Fragment: program already contains materialized image graphics; canvas is an HTML canvas.
const images = await prepareImageRendering(program, {
  async decode({bytes, mimeType}) {
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([bytes], {type: mimeType}));
    try {
      const image = new Image();
      image.src = url;
      await image.decode();
      return {image, width: image.width, height: image.height, originClean: true};
    } finally {
      URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
    }
  }
});
render(program, canvas.getContext("2d"), {images});
```

`prepareImageRendering(programOrCanvasScene, {decode, signal?})` is available from
Full and Basic. The decoder returns an ephemeral Canvas image object, exact stored
width/height and `originClean:true`. A preparation holds at most 64 MiB of unique
encoded bytes and 64 MiPixels of unique decoded pixels; every hash and total is
validated before the first decoder call. One source is limited to 16 MiB and
64 MiPixels. PNG, JPEG, WebP and restricted static SVG are supported. Hash mismatches,
unsafe SVG, decode errors, tainted results, aborts and stale preparations reject
explicitly. Missing/stale preparations fail before Canvas resize or clear.

A handle belongs to the exact `graphicSpec`; prepare again after a changed program.
For a Canvas transition scene, pass that scene to `prepareImageRendering` and then
pass the handle to `renderTransitionScene(scene, context, {images})`. Changing a
mutable scene invalidates its handle. Cloned handles cannot be used.

SVG emits self-contained data URIs. Node PNG and PDF decode the same retained bytes
internally before output. They do not fetch the source URI, and other graphic nodes
remain vector in SVG/PDF. Editable and graphic-only snapshots retain image payloads
and validate them offline; decoder objects and preparation handles are never saved.
Image selection and inspection use the clipped rectangle, not pixel alpha.

## Embedded fonts

Full authoring separates font loading, text measurement, and rendering. Use
`prepareFontResource(program, request, host)`, then commit its authentic handle
with `createFontResource({prepared,requestToken})` on that exact receiver.
Replacement uses `kind:"replace"` with `target` and `replaceFontResource`.
Request tokens are application identifiers for superseded work; the explicit
action token appears in the action trace, so use a request identifier, not a secret.

The request includes `uri`, lowercase SHA256 `expectedHash`, `mimeType`, `family`,
`style:"normal"|"italic"`, numeric weight 100–900 in steps of 100, and
`metricsProviderVersion`. Optional fields are `maxBytes`, `license`, and
`attribution`. TTF, OTF, WOFF and WOFF2 use their `font/*` MIME values; the default
and maximum byte limit is 16 MiB per font. The host explicitly supplies `load`
and `decode`. Loading returns `{bytes:Uint8Array,mimeType}`. Decoding validates
the complete font and returns its exact `contentHash`, `family`, `style`, `weight`
and `metricsProviderVersion`. A decoder may not substitute a fallback font.

Next, `prepareTextMetrics(program,{id,fonts},host)` takes explicit font resource
IDs and `{requestToken,decode,measure,signal?}`. The measurement callback receives
`{asset,queries,signal?}` and returns `{contentHash,metricsProviderVersion,widths}`.
Each query has `text` and `fontSize`; `asset` supplies the exact bytes and font
descriptor. Widths must be finite, nonnegative, in query order, and measured using
that font. Apply the result with `applyTextMetrics({prepared,requestToken})`.
The helper prepares the queries required by existing text layout, including
bounded grapheme prefixes for wrapping. It never treats a missing width as zero
or an estimate. Preparation allows 64 font bindings, 64 MiB of unique bytes,
10,000 queries, 1,048,576 total UTF-16 units, and 256 layout passes.

An exact profile requires a unique resource for each family/style/weight tuple.
New labels or typography may require new measurements. Such edits fail atomically;
use `removeTextMetrics()`, make the edit, then prepare and apply the new layout.
Replacing a bound font prepares its new measurement closure before committing
the resource and all affected text, including tree, treemap, and graph labels.
These labels reuse their stored layout coordinates when typography changes. Existing schema 1 profiles retain their
documented estimate behavior for unmatched queries.

Canvas uses `prepareFontRendering(programOrCanvasScene,{register,signal?})` from
Full or Basic. The explicit `register` callback receives bytes, MIME, content hash,
a content-addressed `family` alias, original `sourceFamily`, style, weight and
provider version. It registers **that alias**, then returns
`{contentHash,family,style,weight,metricsProviderVersion,dispose}`. The identity
fields must match the request; `dispose()` releases that exact host registration.
Pass the result as `render(program,context,{fonts})` or
`renderTransitionScene(scene,context,{fonts})`, and call `fonts.dispose()` when
finished. Aborts and partial failures also release completed registrations.
Callbacks sharing an external font registry must manage their own registration
ownership; deleting another caller's face is not a valid disposal implementation.

Missing, stale, copied, aborted or disposed handles fail before Canvas clear or
resize. Any change to the prepared graphic content requires preparation again.
The rendering budget is 64 distinct font identities and 64 MiB of unique bytes.
No callbacks or handles enter a saved program. SVG embeds the bytes with the same
aliases; PNG/PDF register the bytes during output and release their native leases
after drawing. Renderers do not measure or rewrap text. Missing glyph coverage
must be addressed by the application's chosen fonts; the library does not invent
a replacement font or claim that one font covers every Unicode character.

The [complete font example](./tutorials/font-assets/) includes explicit browser
and Node host adapters, pinned Korean and monochrome emoji subsets, combining
marks, wrapping, offline snapshots and the same primitive across four renderers.

## Prepared shadows

`prepareShadowRendering(programOrCanvasScene, {createCanvas, decode?, fonts?, pixelRatio?, signal?})` is available
from `ggaction` and `ggaction/basic`. It prepares each affected glyph from actual source pixels, combines its
shadow and retains the canonical PNG in an opaque handle. Canvas and SVG then consume those same bytes.
This preparation does not change the immutable program.

Complete browser module with a destination `<canvas id="chart">`:

> **Executable complete.** Use the installed ggaction package in a browser module with a canvas element whose id is chart.

```js
import { chart, prepareShadowRendering, render } from "ggaction";
import { renderToSVG } from "ggaction/svg";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 240, height: 160, margin: 40 })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 1, y: 2 }] })
  .createPointMark({ fill: "#d2462d", shadow: {
    color: "rgba(30,60,90,.5)", offsetX: 8, offsetY: 6, blurRadius: 4
  } })
  .encodeX({ field: "x" }).encodeY({ field: "y" })
  .encodePointRadius({ value: 18 });
const context = document.querySelector("#chart").getContext("2d");
const shadows = await prepareShadowRendering(program, {
  createCanvas(width, height) {
    const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    canvas.width = width; canvas.height = height;
    return canvas;
  },
  async decode({ bytes, mimeType }) {
    const image = await createImageBitmap(new Blob([bytes], { type: mimeType }));
    return { image, width: image.width, height: image.height, originClean: true };
  }
});
try {
  render(program, context, { shadows });
  const svg = renderToSVG(program, { shadows });
  // Use svg as an inline or saved SVG document.
} finally {
  shadows.dispose();
}
```

For SVG-only output, omit `decode`. For high-density Canvas output, pass the same `pixelRatio` to preparation
and `render`. Text shadows additionally require a `fonts` handle from [font preparation](./api/rendering/#embedded-fonts)
for the exact same program or Canvas scene. Pass both `fonts` and `shadows` to Canvas rendering. The host must
provide finite actual glyph ink metrics; missing fonts or metrics are errors. The original multiline positions,
rotation, glyph holes, structured fill and outlines are preserved.

`renderToPNG`/`renderToPNGBuffer` and `renderToPDF`/`renderToPDFBuffer` prepare fonts and shadows automatically
with the installed native backend. They do not fetch resources. PDF keeps unaffected geometry vector and uses
an image only for each affected glyph. A source outside an owner clip can still cast its shadow inside that clip.

For Canvas scenes, prepare the exact scene returned by `createTransitionScene(program,{format:"canvas"})`, then
pass the handle to `renderTransitionScene`. For SVG scenes, pass a program-bound handle to
`createTransitionScene(program,{shadows})`. Scene output contains the prepared effect without adding semantic items.

Handles belong to one exact graphic identity/content and output density. After editing or restoring either
program codec, prepare again. Disposing twice is safe; missing, changed, stale, disposed or aborted preparation
fails before the destination is cleared or resized. The handle is ephemeral and cannot be serialized.

Each glyph permits at most 4096 pixels on either axis, 1,048,576 pixels and 8 MiB of numeric/RGBA output buffers.
The complete scene permits 16,777,216 output pixels, 64 MiB RGBA and 10,000,000 units of convolution/compositing work.
All glyph frames are checked before large raster allocations. Text may first allocate a 1×1 measuring surface.

# Inspect chart items

Use `createInteractionSession` from `ggaction/interaction` to inspect the logical
items under a pointer. It supports Full and Basic programs, browser Canvas and
SVG surfaces, and headless CSS-point queries. The program remains immutable.
See the [complete browser recipe](./recipes/inspect-chart/) for setup.
This is an advanced controller function, not a chainable authoring action.

## Create and mount

Continue from a rendered `program` and its Canvas or SVG root element:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { createInteractionSession } from "ggaction/interaction";
const session = createInteractionSession({ program });
const unsubscribe = session.subscribe(({ state }) => {
  console.log(state.hit?.target, state.hit?.candidates);
});
const unmount = session.mount(element);
```

The default binding inspects `pointermove` and `click`, and clears the transient
hit on `pointerleave`. Supply `bindings: []` for headless dispatch, or one
`{ type: "inspect", events: ["click"], slop: 0, hitInvisible: false }` binding.
Events must be distinct `pointermove` or `click` values. Unknown options and
binding types are rejected.

`mount(element, { rootTransform })` accepts an optional six-number
`[a,b,c,d,e,f]` affine matrix mapping chart coordinates to CSS-local coordinates.
Identity is the default. The host owns CSS layout and any additional transform;
the session does not infer them. Client coordinates subtract the current element
rectangle once. Device pixel ratio is never multiplied into hit coordinates.
Slop remains in CSS pixels under scale or rotation. Use matching logical dimensions
for the rendered chart and surface when no root matrix is supplied.

## Inspect without a DOM

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `session`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
session.dispatch({ type: "inspect", point: { x: 126, y: 182 }, pointerType: "mouse" });
const { target, candidates } = session.getState().hit;
session.dispatch({ type: "leave" });
```

`point` is CSS-local. Pointer type is `mouse` by default, or `pen` or `touch`.
Stroke slop defaults to 3 CSS pixels for mouse/pen and 6 for touch; a finite
non-negative `slop` overrides it. `hitInvisible: true` includes opacity-zero
items. Clips still apply.

A candidate contains opaque `itemKey`, `ownerId`, `role`, `childPath`, `rowKeys`,
`resourceRefs`, `screenPoint`, `localPoint`, `distance`, and `zIndex`. The first
candidate is the target. All overlapping logical items remain in `candidates`,
ordered front to back, then by distance and stable identity. A body and its label
produce one logical candidate. `localPoint` uses the owning child Canvas.

Marks retain final-item grain and exact data/resource revisions. Guides have
roles `axis-tick`, `axis-title`, `legend-item`, `facet-header`, and `chart-title`.
Renaming a label does not change its raw value identity. Facet headers belong to
their parent composition; nested marks and guides retain their child paths.

Paths honor fill holes and painted dash runs. Transparent fill differs from
`none`. Text targets its concrete per-line metric rectangles, including rotation
and outline extent; images target their clipped viewport. Shadows do not enlarge
hit geometry. Path approximation is bounded by 0.25 CSS pixels.

## Replace a program or sampled frame

Call `session.updateProgram(nextProgram)` after an authoring edit. Replacement is
atomic and clears transient hits. It increments both `frameVersion` and
`generation`; mounted listeners stay active.

An animation host may supply a sampled version-2 Canvas scene whose node keys,
types and topology belong to the current program. Render the accepted snapshot:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `session`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { renderTransitionScene } from "ggaction/scene";
const state = session.getState();
const result = session.dispatch({
  type: "frame", scene: sampledScene,
  version: state.frameVersion + 1, generation: state.generation
});
if (result.status === "applied") {
  renderTransitionScene(session.getState().scene, context);
}
```

The host creates `sampledScene`; the controller does not sample animations or
schedule frames. A stale generation or non-increasing version returns
`{ status: "stale" }` without reading scene contents. Unknown nodes, changed
topology, invalid concrete values, and excessive work fail without replacing the
current frame. A caller-owned scene is copied before use. Omitted nodes are not
hit targets in that frame.

## State and cleanup

`getState()` returns an immutable snapshot with `program`, `scene`, `frameVersion`,
`generation`, `hit`, `mounted`, and `destroyed`. A hit contains `target`,
`candidates`, `diagnostics`, `statistics`, and `frameVersion`. Singular transforms
and empty viewports produce no hit plus diagnostics.

Subscribers receive `{ type, state }`; event types are `inspect`, `leave`, `frame`,
`program`, `mount`, `unmount`, and `destroy`. Dispatch and program updates return
`{ status: "applied" | "queued" | "stale" }`. Reentrant operations run FIFO after
the current event, with a 256-command bound. Subscriber errors propagate and
clear queued work; the already published state remains available.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `session`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
unsubscribe();
unmount();
session.destroy();
```

Mounting another element removes the old listeners. Unmount is idempotent.
`destroy()` removes listeners, disposes the current index, and discards pending
work; it returns true once and false thereafter. Terminal state remains readable;
other session methods reject further work.

Preparation is limited to 100,000 scene nodes and 10,000,000 work units; queries
are limited to 2,000,000 units. Work includes geometry, metadata and guide sample
comparisons. The session does not persist host objects or hover state. Editing
gestures, selection transactions, keyboard navigation, history, and asset loading
are not supported commands. PNG/PDF exports remain static.

# Inspect overlapping chart items

Create a chart with two observations at the same location, then inspect both
through Canvas or SVG. Open the live example to compare the two surfaces.

## Prerequisites

Use the [browser module setup](./getting-started/) and a
`<canvas id="chart"></canvas>`. This complete program includes its source rows.

## Complete program

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";
import { render } from "ggaction";

export function createInspectionChart() {
  return chart().createCanvas({ width: 420, height: 300, margin: 70 })
    .createData({ id: "observations", keyField: "id", values: [
      { id: "a", x: 2, y: 3 }, { id: "b", x: 8, y: 7 }, { id: "c", x: 2, y: 3 }
    ] })
    .createPointMark({ id: "observations" })
    .encodeX({ field: "x", scale: { domain: [0, 10], nice: false } })
    .encodeY({ field: "y", scale: { domain: [0, 10], nice: false } })
    .createXAxis({ ticksAndLabels: { values: [0, 5, 10] }, title: false })
    .createYAxis({ ticksAndLabels: { values: [0, 5, 10] }, title: false })
    .createTitle({ text: "Inspect overlapping observations" });
}

const program = createInspectionChart();
render(program, document.querySelector("#chart").getContext("2d"));
```

## Add inspection

Continue in the same module after rendering the `program` above:

```javascript
import { createInteractionSession } from "ggaction/interaction";
const session = createInteractionSession({ program });
session.subscribe(({ state }) => {
  console.log(state.hit?.candidates ?? []);
});
const unmount = session.mount(document.querySelector("#chart"));
window.addEventListener("pagehide", () => session.destroy(), { once: true });
```

At CSS-local point `(126, 182)`, two logical point candidates are reported. At
`(294, 118)`, one is reported. Axis ticks and the title also expose guide roles.
Inspecting does not change data, selection resources, or action trace.

For SVG, render the same program with `renderToSVG` from `ggaction/svg`, insert
that markup, and mount a separate session on the SVG root. See the
[interaction API](./api/interaction/) for coordinate transforms, sampled
frames, supported commands, and cleanup.

# Program Composition

Combine already-authored chart programs without merging their datasets, marks,
scales, or guides. The result is another immutable `ChartProgram` whose parent
Canvas contains concrete snapshots of its named children.

## Arrange complete programs

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { hconcat, vconcat } from "ggaction";

const row = hconcat({
  id: "overview",
  programs: [
    { id: "main", program: scatterplot },
    { id: "detail", program: barChart }
  ],
  gap: 20,
  align: "center",
  padding: 16
});

const dashboard = vconcat({
  programs: [row, trendChart],
  gap: 18
});
```

This is a composition fragment: `scatterplot`, `barChart`, and `trendChart`
must each be a complete program with one materialized Canvas. See the
[runnable repository example](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/program-composition)
for complete child construction and Browser Canvas rendering.

The representative output deliberately keeps two different final grammars:
the `main` slot contains a titled point chart on a blue panel, while the
`detail` slot contains the titled orange bar chart installed by
`replaceCompositionChild`. Distinct child backgrounds and the visible parent
gap make the retained slot, replacement slot, and parent layout observable in
the full image and its gallery thumbnail.

Both functions initially require at least two programs. A direct `ChartProgram` receives
the deterministic slot name `view-1`, `view-2`, and so on. Use
`{ id, program }` when later code must replace a stable slot.

| Option | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `"composition"` | Names the composition for deterministic graphic namespaces |
| `programs` | required | Ordered complete child programs or `{ id?, program }` entries |
| `gap` | `16` | Non-negative distance between adjacent children |
| `align` | `"center"` | `"start"`, `"center"`, or `"end"` cross-axis placement |
| `padding` | `0` on every side | Non-negative scalar or partial four-side object |

## Automatic and explicit child sizes

The parent Canvas size is inferred from child dimensions, gap, and padding.
For `hconcat`, children whose height was omitted in `createCanvas` expand to the
largest child height. For `vconcat`, children whose width was omitted expand to
the largest child width. A unit child rematerializes against that resolved size.
A nested composition keeps its intrinsic child layout and `align` places its
complete snapshot inside the larger cross-axis slot; the outer composition does
not stretch inner facet cells, gaps, or guide geometry. An explicitly authored
child width or height is never overwritten.

When all child Canvas backgrounds match, that color also fills the parent gaps,
padding, and reserved guide lanes. Mixed child backgrounds retain the existing
parent surface (initially white). Child backgrounds remain independently editable,
and nested compositions keep independent clipping and coordinate scopes.

Use `createTitle` without a target on the composed program to add one overall
title. See [Titles](./api/titles/) for parent and individual-view title editing.

## Compose Cartesian, Polar, and Parallel charts

A complete Cartesian, Polar, or Parallel chart can be a direct or nested concat child.
The composition does not reinterpret theta, radius, x, y, scales, guides, or
selections. It snapshots each finished child into one namespaced concrete
graphic tree, so Canvas, SVG, PNG, and PDF renderers use the same result.

When a nested child changes, replace it in each ancestor explicitly:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `polarRow`, `dashboard`. Resource selectors used here: `target: "detail"`; `target: "polarRow"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const revisedPolarRow = polarRow.replaceCompositionChild({
  target: "detail",
  program: revisedPolarChart
});

const revisedDashboard = dashboard.replaceCompositionChild({
  target: "polarRow",
  program: revisedPolarRow
});
```

This preserves immutable earlier programs and makes the affected ancestor
layout visible in the action trace. See the
[cross-feature dashboard source](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/cross-feature-dashboard)
for a nested Polar replacement next to a Cartesian facet.

## State, trace, and action scope

`children` maps stable slot IDs to retained immutable programs.
`compositionSpec` stores concat direction or facet intent together with order,
gap, alignment, and padding. Grid state additionally records both ordered
domains, cell coordinates, scalar pairs, and blank status; repeat state records
the target, channel, and ordered fields. The
parent `graphicSpec` stores the fully materialized, namespaced child Canvas
tree; renderers read only that concrete state.

`hconcat`, `vconcat`, `facet`, `facetGrid`, and `repeatCharts` trace retained
child use and concrete materialization. Named structural edits rematerialize
from retained concat children. Layout edits and replacement rematerialize from
the retained child programs. Facet source, scale, and guide edits rederive stable-ID children
from the parent-retained unit state before replacing the parent snapshot.
Ordinary data, mark, encoding, scale, and guide
actions apply only to unit programs and reject a composition parent. Facet
titles, facet-header edits and existing shared-legend editors/removal are explicit parent-owned exceptions. Edit a
child first, then replace its slot when a concat dashboard needs a changed
chart.

## Path layer color

When adding an independent path layer with `createLayerPlot`, omitted color is
inherited only when it describes a whole series. A continuous point color that
varies along a new Line or Polar Line defaults to a single color; it is not
averaged or used to split the path into artificial series. Categorical colors
and compatible per-series continuous colors are retained. Set the native
constructor's `plot.options.color` and `groupBy` to choose another valid mapping,
or `plot.inherit.color: false` for a single-color layer. Explicit incompatible
color mappings are rejected. Area constructor color is categorical.

## Shared color legends

With `share: { color: true }`, compatible color-only legends are collected into
one legend at the right of the entire composition. The first visible color guide
in composition order supplies its presentation; all use the shared scale domain.
Child guide definitions remain intact, so disabling color sharing restores their
local legends. Combined legends that also explain unshared channels (such as
shape or size) remain local. Nested shared color guides are collected once.
Legend reservation and parent titles are included in the final Canvas bounds.

# Position Encodings

Choose the position family from the semantic mark and field relationship. All
position actions infer the current mark, use or create a compatible coordinate,
resolve a channel scale, and explicitly materialize the affected graphics.

Line aggregation groups exact observed independent-axis values and series.
Quantitative positions remain continuous and sorted numerically; they do not
require bins. With an explicit bin, vertices use interval midpoints instead.
The same rule applies to aggregate Y over X or aggregate X over Y.

Changing an Area's independent position also updates completed-key alignment.
Overlay areas use observed rows; stacked areas realign unique rows at the new
key using the existing fill policy. A stacked position cannot also be its
measurement or series field, and duplicate group/key rows require explicit
reaggregation of the original observations. No implicit mean of means is used.

For measured polar sectors, changing the category also updates a color role
that followed the old category. Polar guide samples follow the new domain;
custom guide styles are preserved.

## Supported marks and modes

| Action | Supported marks | Field types | Important modes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `encodeX` | point, line, area, bar, rect, rule, tick, text | point/line/area/bar/rect/rule/tick/text: quantitative, temporal, ordinal, nominal | field; rule, area, rect, and independent text also accept datum; bar accepts aggregate or bin |
| `encodeY` | point, line, area, bar, rect, rule, tick, text | point/line/area/bar/rect/rule/tick/text: quantitative, temporal, ordinal, nominal | field; rule, area, rect, and independent text also accept datum; bar accepts aggregate or count |
| `encodeX2` / `encodeY2` | area, ranged bar, rect, rule | area/ranged bar/rect/rule: matching primary | secondary field; rule, area, and rect also accept datum |
| `encodeTheta` | point, line, arc | point/line: quantitative, temporal, ordinal, nominal; arc: quantitative, ordinal, nominal | arc maps direct quantitative values, category counts, or category-weighted sums to proportional sectors |
| `encodeR` | point, line, arc | point/line/arc: quantitative | radial position; arc combines it with a categorical theta band |
| `encodeParallelCoordinates` | line | line: quantitative, ordinal | atomic ordered dimensions; one namespaced scale and axis per dimension |
| `encodeDx` / `encodeDy` | text | text: quantitative | independent Text only; finite field or constant logical-pixel offsets, no scale or guide; field offsets establish row grain |

## Choose an encoding

| Goal | Required state | Actions | Detailed page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Position points | point mark, quantitative, temporal, or ordinal fields | `encodeX`, `encodeY` | [Quantitative positions](./api/position/quantitative/) |
| Position Polar points | point mark, angle field and quantitative radius field | `encodeTheta`, `encodeR` | [Polar point tutorial](./tutorials/polar-points/) |
| Draw Polar lines or radar paths | line mark, angle field and quantitative radius field | `encodeTheta`, `encodeR` | [Polar line tutorial](./tutorials/polar-lines/) |
| Draw pies, donuts, rose charts, or radial bars | arc mark, direct quantitative theta, categorical count/weighted-sum theta, or quantitative radius | `encodeTheta`, optional `encodeR` | [Polar arc tutorial](./tutorials/polar-arcs/) |
| Draw cells or interval shading | rect mark, band positions, paired endpoints, or one plot-spanning interval | `encodeX`, `encodeY`, optional `encodeX2`, `encodeY2` | [Rect marks](./api/marks/rect/) |
| Draw an aggregate time series | line mark, temporal x and quantitative y | `encodeX`, `encodeY` | [Temporal lines](./api/position/temporal/) |
| Build vertical aggregate bars | bar mark, ordinal/temporal x and quantitative y | `encodeX`, `encodeY` | [Bar positions](./api/position/ordinal-bars/) |
| Build horizontal aggregate bars | bar mark, quantitative x and ordinal/temporal y | `encodeX`, `encodeY` | [Bar positions](./api/position/ordinal-bars/) |
| Order categorical positions | nominal/ordinal x, y, or theta | `orderCategories`, `removeCategoryOrder` | [Category ordering](./api/position/category-ordering/) |
| Bin and count values | bar mark, quantitative field | `encodeHistogram` or `encodeX` + `encodeY` | [Histograms](./api/position/histogram/) |
| Estimate a distribution | area mark, quantitative field | `encodeDensity` | [Encodings](./api/encodings/#atomic-density) |
| Center aligned area series | area mark, quantitative/temporal x, non-negative quantitative y, nominal group | `encodeY({ stack: "center" })` or `encodeColor({ layout: "center" })` | [Color encoding](./api/series/color/#center-stacked-areas) |
| Draw full-span or bounded rules | rule mark, field or datum endpoints | `encodeX`, `encodeY`, `encodeX2`, `encodeY2` | [Rule endpoints](./api/position-encodings/#rule-endpoints) |
| Control within-category grouping | categorical bar, point, or rule position | `encodeXOffset`, `encodeYOffset` | [Offsets](./api/position/offsets/) |

For ordinary grouped bar charts, prefer
`encodeColor({ field, layout: "group" })`; it calls the matching advanced
directional offset action for the same field.

For a center-stacked area, each group must have exactly one non-negative value
at every x position. `encodeY({ stack: "center" })` preserves the original y
field and creates concrete lower/upper area boundaries around zero. The
equivalent `encodeColor({ layout: "center" })` also creates the matching nominal
group when it is absent. Center stacking is not supported for bars, ranged
areas, signed values, duplicate group/x rows, or missing positions.

## Shared inference

- `target` defaults to the current compatible mark.
- `coordinate` uses the layer coordinate, then the documented `main`
 Cartesian or `polar` Polar default for the requested channel family.
- Scale IDs default to their channel names: `x`, `y`, `theta`, `radius`, `xOffset`, and `yOffset`.
- Automatic continuous y ranges run bottom-to-top. Discrete y positions run
 top-to-bottom so horizontal categories follow domain order.
- Temporal values accept finite timestamps, four-digit numeric/string years,
 and valid date strings. Four-digit values are interpreted as UTC years.
- Ambiguous resources produce an error instead of an arbitrary selection.

## Polar positions

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program
  .encodeTheta({ field: "angle" })
  .encodeR({ field: "distance" })
  .encodePointRadius({ value: 3 });
```

`encodeTheta` accepts point or line marks with quantitative, temporal, ordinal,
or nominal fields. For an arc mark, an aggregate-free quantitative field makes
one proportional sector per positive source row. `aggregate: "count"` over a
nominal or ordinal field creates count-proportional sectors. `aggregate: "sum"`
plus a non-negative finite `weight` field creates category-weighted
proportional sectors. Categorical theta plus quantitative `encodeR` creates
radial sectors; direct quantitative arc theta does not combine with `encodeR`.
Quantitative angle scales are linear; temporal angles use time scales; discrete
angles use point or band scales. The automatic range is `[0, 360]` degrees with
0 at 12 o'clock and clockwise positive direction.

`encodeR` accepts a quantitative field and linear, log, pow, sqrt, or symlog
scale policies. Its automatic range fits the smaller plot dimension. Explicit
ranges are non-negative logical pixels and must fit the current plot bounds.

The two actions are order-independent. One Polar channel may exist as an
incomplete semantic assignment, but points or paths become visible only after
both channels and their scales resolve. A line may use
`createLineMark({ closed: true })` for a closed radar path. Cartesian x/y and
Polar theta/radius cannot be mixed on one layer.

## Measured radial sectors

On an Arc mark with categorical theta, `encodeR` can aggregate a measure per
category and encode either annular area or radial length. This fragment assumes
`program` already has data with `category` and non-negative numeric `value` fields:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program
  .createArcMark({ innerRadius: 0.5 })
  .encodeTheta({ field: "category", fieldType: "nominal" })
  .encodeR({ field: "value", aggregate: "sum", mapping: "area" })
  .createRadialAxis();
```

Use `mapping: "radius-length"` to make length from the inner edge proportional
to the aggregate. Use `{ aggregate: "count", mapping: "area" }` without a field
to count rows per category. Both modes use equal-angle sectors and a zero-based
linear scale. Zero categories remain in categorical domains but draw no sector.
Negative, nonfinite, all-zero, and unrepresentable positive-thickness inputs are errors.

The radial axis shows count or sum units with the same mapping as the sectors.
An explicit radius range `[inner, outer]` defines the hole and must agree with
an explicitly specified Arc innerRadius (ratio or fixed pixels). These modes require zero theta
padding and `padAngle: 0`; `nice: true`, `zero: false`, and `reverse: true` are errors.

Reassigning `encodeR` preserves omitted mapping and aggregate. To change the
mapping on a shared measured scale, use `editScale({ id, radialMapping: "area" })`;
all its compatible sectors and radial guides update together. Ordinary point
radius and measured Arc radius require separate scales.

Use `encodeR({ field: "value", mapping: false })` to refine a measured Arc into
ordinary row-level radial length. This one action removes the inherited
count/sum aggregate, clears the scale's measured mapping, and updates existing
radial guides. It preserves the mark, data, categorical theta order, and
compatible styling. This is an explicit semantic change: `mapping: "area"`
makes aggregate annular area proportional to value, while `mapping: false`
makes each row's radius proportional to its value. A measured scale shared by
another aggregate Arc must be separated before this transition.

## Rule endpoints

Rule positions use the same `encodeX` and `encodeY` actions and accept exactly
one of `field` or `datum`. Datum-only rules infer finite numbers as quantitative
and other supported scalar values as nominal. Field rules, temporal data, and
ambiguous values require an explicit `fieldType`:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program
  .createRuleMark()
  .encodeX({ datum: 15 })
  .encodeY({ datum: 20 })
  .encodeY2({ datum: 80, fieldType: "quantitative" });
```

`encodeX2` and rule `encodeY2` require their corresponding primary endpoint
and share its scale, coordinate, and field type. `x` alone draws a vertical
full-span rule; `y` alone draws a horizontal full-span rule. `x+y+y2` and
`y+x+x2` draw bounded intervals, while all four endpoints draw a diagonal.
Calling the same action again replaces only that endpoint.

## Quantitative ranges

Full `encodeXRange` and `encodeYRange` accept field names or finite
`{ datum: number }` bounds for Rect and Rule marks. Either or both bounds may
be constants; the two endpoints share one scale and coordinate. No source rows
or columns are added. The wrapper validates the final pair before changing it
and records the ordinary primary/secondary encoding actions.

Bar ranges require two fields. Temporal ranges also require two fields;
use the individual position encoders for temporal constants. Area bounds retain
the more specific requirements below.

## Area bounds

Area `encodeXRange` and `encodeYRange` accept a field name or `{ datum: number }`
for each bound, with at least one field. Bounds retain their order even when they cross.
The two endpoints share one scale; reassignment validates the final pair and scale together.
`encodeX2` and `encodeY2` accept quantitative datum bounds without an explicit fieldType.
Use a finite, nonzero baseline for log scales.

# Quantitative Positions

## At a glance

| Action | Shortest call | Required state | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `encodeX` | `encodeX({ field: "x" })` | point mark and finite field | Concrete horizontal positions |
| `encodeY` | `encodeY({ field: "y" })` | point mark and finite field | Concrete vertical positions |

## Point `encodeX(options)` and `encodeY(options)`

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program
  .encodeX({ field: "Horsepower" })
  .encodeY({ field: "Miles_per_Gallon" });
```

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | non-empty string | required |
| `target` | point mark ID | current mark |
| `fieldType` | `"quantitative"` | `"quantitative"` |
| `coordinate` | coordinate ID | layer coordinate, then `"main"` |
| `scale.id` | scale ID | channel name |
| `scale.type` | `"linear"` | `"linear"` |
| `scale.domain` | `"auto"` or two finite numbers | `"auto"` |
| `scale.range` | `"auto"` or two finite numbers | `"auto"` |
| `scale.nice` | boolean | omitted |
| `scale.zero` | boolean | omitted |

Automatic domains combine compatible fields that share a scale. Automatic
ranges use plot bounds, and every encoded value must be finite. The actions
ensure a Cartesian coordinate exists and attach it to the point layer.

Calling the same action again on the same target replaces that channel's
field. If `scale.id` is omitted, the current channel scale is reused and all
connected marks, axes, and grids are recomputed. An explicit new scale ID
rebinds a non-shared guide while retaining the old named scale. Inferred axis
titles follow the new field; explicit titles and appearance stay unchanged.

## Errors and limitations

A conflicting layer coordinate, non-Cartesian coordinate, cross-channel scale,
or non-finite field value is rejected before partial output is retained. A
guide cannot be rebound away from a scale that still has another consumer.

## Related

[Position encoding index](./api/position-encodings/) ·
[Scale options](./api/scales/) · [Scatterplot tutorial](./tutorials/scatterplot/)
