# Axes

## At a glance

| Action | Shortest call | Inference/defaults | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `createAxes` | `createAxes()` | Stored coordinate family, position scales, titles | Complete x/y, theta/radius, or Parallel dimension axes |
| `editXAxis` | `editXAxis({ ticks: false })` | Existing x-axis components | Selected components edited or removed |
| `editYAxis` | `editYAxis({ position: "right" })` | Existing y-axis components | Retained components moved together |
| `removeXAxis` / `removeYAxis` | `removeXAxis()` | Existing complete axis | Semantic, graphic, and stored axis state removed |

Cartesian axis lines, ticks, labels and titles must not overlap a chart title or
legend on the same edge. This applies to creation, focused and whole-axis edits,
and Canvas or scale updates, regardless of authoring order. Increase the margin
or change offsets when space is insufficient; a failed action preserves the
earlier program.

Automatic axis titles use the source field or aggregate. Statistical reference
lines and bands reuse that title; their internal output columns do not introduce
another measure name.
Grouped summary outputs use their aggregate and source field, including after
changing the source measure while retaining an output alias.

An omitted offset for a vertical Y-axis title reserves a quarter-em ink gap when
its estimated text box is clamped to the Canvas edge. This applies at every font
size when the extra reserve fits beside the actual axis labels. If it would
introduce a label collision, placement keeps the existing Canvas-fit offset.
Automatic margin fitting keeps space for the inferred ink reserve.
Explicit offsets and preferred placement with sufficient margin stay exact.

## Keep a title outside its labels

Cartesian axis titles accept `offset: { from: "labels", gap: 8 }`. The gap is a
finite non-negative distance in logical pixels outside the occupied label block.
It follows the same axis owner and physical side, including rotated labels and
independent facet scales. Declare the axis first, then refine its title:

> **Executable complete.** Import chart from ggaction; all rows and both axes are declared in this complete program.

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 500, height: 360, margin: 90 })
  .createData({ values: [{ distance: 0, amount: 0 }, { distance: 1, amount: 120 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: "distance", y: "amount" })
  .editYAxisTitle({ offset: { from: "labels", gap: 8 } });
```

The stored offset retains this intent. Label text, fonts, scales, data, Canvas,
theme and text metrics can change the resulting distance without replacing it
with a fixed number. Empty display labels do not contribute; at least one
nonempty label on the same side is required. Remove the title together with its
last labels, or switch its offset to a number. The existing collision and Canvas
checks still apply, including when `overlap: "allow"` is set.
With `createCanvas({ plot: { width, height } })`, automatic guide margins also
fit relative titles: the requested font, gap, and plot dimensions stay exact.
A fixed outer Canvas still rejects a title that exceeds its authored margins.

Numeric offsets keep their signed distance from the axis frame; omitted offsets
keep their existing automatic defaults. An omitted edit preserves either mode.
The relative object accepts only `from` and `gap`. It is not a Polar/Parallel
title option, an axis frame offset, or a label offset.

## Rotate labels outside the plot

Rotated Cartesian labels stay outside their selected plot edge in both fixed-size
and automatic-plot Canvases. `offset` measures the gap to the complete rotated
text bounds. Vertical X-axis labels are centered over their ticks; slanted labels
use an end anchor inferred from their rotation and axis side. Reserve enough
margin for the full label length and the axis title. Rotation does not enlarge a
fixed Canvas or change its margins.

## Choose nearest-step linear ticks

Set `rounding: "nearest"` on Cartesian tick selection when automatic ticks should
choose the nearest 1–2–5 decade step. The default count density is 5: a 0–140
domain gets labels 0, 20, …, 140. Count is an approximate density, not an exact
number of ticks. Omission keeps the existing behavior; `"ceiling"` restores it.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ plot: { width: 200, height: 120 }, margin: { left: 40, top: 20, right: 20, bottom: 30 } })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 0, y: 0 }, { x: 1, y: 133 }] })
  .createLinePlot({
    x: { field: "x", scale: { domain: [0, 1] } },
    y: { field: "y", scale: { domain: [0, 140] } },
    guides: {
      axes: { x: false, y: { title: false, ticksAndLabels: { rounding: "nearest" } } },
      grid: false,
      legend: false
    }
  });
```

Complete axes, grouped ticks-and-labels, and focused Cartesian tick/label actions
accept the same option. It is restricted to count-mode linear axes. Explicit
`values`, temporal/transformed/discrete axes, and Polar/Parallel axes reject it.
When editing a values-mode axis, also provide `count` to select automatic ticks.

Once selected on ticks, count/rounding/value edits update existing labels and
inferred grids together. Label-only edits must agree with existing ticks. A
label-only axis does not supply a grid policy. Explicit grid count/values use
their existing independent policy; `values: "auto"` restores inference from
ticks. Named axes with conflicting policies need explicit grid selection.
Independent facets choose ticks from each actual child domain, and data/Canvas/
scale updates and saved programs preserve the policy.

## Keep endpoint labels inside the axis span

Set Cartesian labels `flush: true` to keep unrotated text bounds inside the mapped scale span. This moves text inward only when its bounds cross an endpoint, without changing tick positions, text, font sizes or the outward gap. It works on X and Y axes, retains `alongOffset`, and moves wrapped lines together. The default is `false`. Rotated labels and text wider than the entire span are rejected.

Flush preserves the existing overlap policy. When adjacent labels intentionally overlap, request `overlap: "allow"`; this does not disable Canvas or title collision checks. Specify required flush geometry at complete-axis creation so the initial axis also fits. An independently explicit `title.overlap: "allow"` permits that title to intersect its own labels; see [intentional title-label overlap](./api/axes/complete/#intentional-title-label-overlap).

## Color individual tick labels

Use Cartesian labels `colorMap: [{ value, color }]` for per-value colors. Lookup uses raw typed tick values, independently of `labelMap` display text. Missing entries use the existing global `color`; `[]` stores an empty map and `"auto"` removes it. Continuous/time keys must be finite numbers or Unix milliseconds; categorical keys preserve their types. Duplicate keys, extra entry fields and empty colors are rejected. Wrapped lines share their tick color. Complete, whole-axis, grouped and focused label actions use the same policy, and tick/Canvas/scale changes preserve it. Polar and Parallel axes do not accept this option.

## Override displayed tick text

Numeric labels accept `format: ","` for integer grouping (`1234` becomes `1,234`) or
`format: ",.2f"` for grouping with two decimal places. The existing precision range is
0–12. Grouped percent and scientific formats are unsupported. Temporal labels accept
`format: "%a"` for UTC weekday names such as `Mon`. Formatting changes displayed text;
it preserves raw values, scale domains and tick positions.

Cartesian label `labelMap` works with categorical values, numeric ticks and time ticks. Provide typed `{ value, label }` entries. Continuous keys must be finite numbers; time keys use Unix milliseconds. Missing entries retain the normal formatter, and `"auto"` clears the map. Scale domains, tick positions and raw data are preserved. Use focused labels, nested ticks-and-labels or whole-axis editors to update the same policy.

Numeric axes also accept `format: "ticks"`: infer fixed decimal places from each
axis's settled tick spacing, retaining `0.00` at a `0.05` step and integer labels
at a `100` step. Independent facets resolve their own precision. Omitted/auto
output is unchanged; time and discrete scales reject this numeric option.
See [numeric label formats](./api/axes/complete/) for
precision limits and replay behavior.

## Shift ticks and labels along an axis

Cartesian ticks and labels accept `alongOffset`, a signed finite displacement in logical pixels. Positive values move X-axis items right and Y-axis items down, including top/right axes and reversed scales. It defaults to zero and leaves the scale and axis baseline unchanged. Tick and label offsets are independent absolute values: set both when both should move. The existing label `offset` remains the outward gap from the plot edge. Complete axes, whole-axis editors and focused editors accept the same options; Canvas and scale updates preserve them. Polar and Parallel axes do not accept this option.

## Independent Cartesian axes

Use `createYAxis({ id: "share", position: "right" })` to establish another axis,
then `editYAxisTitle({ target: "share", text: "Share" })` to refine it. See
[Independent named Cartesian axes](./api/axes/complete/#independent-named-cartesian-axes)
for side occupancy, selection, arrays and independent scales.

## Standalone Cartesian axes

An axis does not need an invisible mark or dataset. Supply an existing Cartesian
coordinate and a scale with an explicit domain:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const ruler = chart().createCanvas({ margin: 80 })
  .createCoordinate({ id: "frame", type: "cartesian" })
  .createScale({ id: "amount", type: "linear", domain: [0, 100] })
  .createXAxis({ coordinate: "frame", scale: "amount" });
```

The title defaults to the scale ID. Set `title: false` to omit it or use
`title: { text: "Amount" }`. Both resource IDs are required for standalone
creation; an automatic domain needs data consumers. Scale edits, Canvas resize,
coordinate frame aspect changes, and serialization preserve the binding.

## Polar component creation

Create a missing Polar axis component without rebuilding the other components.
These actions are available from `ggaction`.

| Component | Theta action | Radial action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | `createThetaAxisLine` | `createRadialAxisLine` |
| Tick marks | `createThetaAxisTicks` | `createRadialAxisTicks` |
| Tick text | `createThetaAxisLabels` | `createRadialAxisLabels` |
| Title | `createThetaAxisTitle` | `createRadialAxisTitle` |

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 480, height: 480, margin: 80 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { direction: 0, distance: 2 },
    { direction: 120, distance: 4 },
    { direction: 240, distance: 6 }
  ] })
  .createPointMark()
  .encodeTheta({ field: "direction", scale: { domain: [0, 360] } })
  .encodeR({ field: "distance", scale: { zero: true } })
  .createThetaAxis({ title: false })
  .createThetaAxisTitle({ text: "Direction" })
  .editThetaAxisTitle({ fontWeight: 600 })
  .createRadialAxisLine({ angle: 45 })
  .createRadialAxisTicks({ values: [0, 3, 6] })
  .createRadialAxisLabels({ values: [0, 3, 6] })
  .createRadialAxisTitle({ text: "Distance" });
```

All eight actions accept optional `scale` and `coordinate` IDs. Existing axis
bindings take precedence over inference; otherwise exactly one compatible Polar
encoding must identify the resources. Use the matching focused editor to change
an existing component. Duplicate creation fails. After `removeThetaAxis()` or
`removeRadialAxis()`, the same create actions can rebuild selected components.

Tick and label creation accepts either `count` or exact data-space `values`.
Other style options match the corresponding focused editor below. Radial
creation also accepts `angle` in degrees: the first component establishes it
(default `90`), and later components share it. Change the angle with
`editRadialAxis({ angle })`; conflicting component angles are rejected. Theta
components do not accept `angle`. Only radial titles accept
`position: "inside" | "outside"`.

Omitted title text follows the encoded field or its explicit title. Component
styles and bindings survive Canvas, scale, and compatible encoding edits.

## Omit, remove, and restore components

All four complete axis creators accept `false` for `line`, `ticksAndLabels`,
and `title`. Omission or `{}` creates the component with inferred defaults.
At least one component must remain enabled. To disable an entire axis, use
the outer `createAxes({ x: false, ... })` selection.

The corresponding complete editors accept `false` for `line`, `ticks`,
`labels`, `ticksAndLabels`, and `title` to remove existing components.
An object edits an existing component; an omitted option preserves it.
Restore a missing component with its focused create action.

`ticksAndLabels: false` removes both existing components. If only one remains,
remove it with `ticks: false` or `labels: false`. Do not combine the group with
individual tick/label options. The group's nested `ticks` and `labels` still
accept style objects, not `false`.

Removing the last component cleans up the axis state and preserves grids,
marks, and scales. Removed components stay absent after Canvas or scale edits.
`editRadialAxis({ angle })` requires an existing axis component.

When a chart facade reuses guides, a component declared `false` must be absent.
If it already exists, remove it explicitly before requesting that declaration.
Theta creation rejects `angle`, which was previously ignored; angle belongs
to radial axes.

## `createAxes(options?)`

See [Complete Axes and Labels](./api/axes/complete/#createaxesoptions) for creation,
display mapping, formatting, wrapping, Polar/Parallel decisions, and examples.

## Editing a complete axis

Use `editXAxis()` or `editYAxis()` when several components of one existing
axis should change together:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program
  .editXAxis({
    line: false,
    ticksAndLabels: {
      count: 6,
      ticks: { length: 7 },
      labels: { color: "#475569", fontSize: 11 }
    },
    title: { text: "Engine displacement" }
  })
  .editYAxis({ position: "right" });
```

The complete edit facade does not create an axis or change its scale and
coordinate binding. Each component accepts its existing edit object or `false`;
`false` removes that component's stored materialization config and concrete
graphic together; title removal also clears its semantic text. `ticksAndLabels:
false` removes both components and cannot be combined with standalone `ticks`
or `labels`. Omitted components remain unchanged unless `position` is present,
which moves every retained component on that axis.

Removing the last component also clears the empty complete-axis semantic and
stored config. Recreate one component with its ordinary `create*AxisLine`,
`create*AxisTicksAndLabels`, or `create*AxisTitle` action, or recreate the full
axis with `createXAxis()`/`createYAxis()`. Later Canvas and scale edits do not
restore removed components.

Use `editThetaAxis()` for grouped theta component edits. Use
`editRadialAxis({ angle: 180 })` to move the radial line, ticks, labels, and
title together. Focused `editThetaAxisLine/Ticks/Labels/Title` and matching
`editRadialAxis*` actions change one visible component without raw graphic IDs.
`editRadialAxisTitle({ position: "inside" | "outside" })` switches only the
radial title placement while preserving its text and style.

## Removing an axis

`removeXAxis()`, `removeYAxis()`, `removeThetaAxis()`, and
`removeRadialAxis()` remove the complete axis: line, ticks,
labels, title, semantic guide state, and stored materialization settings. Marks,
scales, coordinates, and the opposite axis remain.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const withoutXAxis = program.removeXAxis();
const selected = program.removeYAxis({ scale: "y", coordinate: "main" });
```

Optional selectors must match the existing resource. A missing or mismatched
axis throws before anything changes.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `position` | x: `"bottom"/"top"`; y: `"left"/"right"` |
| `line` | `false` or `{ color?, lineWidth? }` |
| `ticks` | `false` or `{ count?, values?, length?, color?, lineWidth?, alongOffset? }` |
| `labels` | `false` or `{ count?, values?, offset?, format?, color?, fontSize?, fontFamily?, fontWeight?, rotation?, maxWidth?, wrap?, lineHeight?, overlap?, alongOffset?, labelMap?, flush?, colorMap? }` |
| `ticksAndLabels` | `false` or `{ count?, values?, ticks?, labels? }` |
| `title` | `false` or `{ text?, at?, offset?, rotation?, color?, fontSize?, fontFamily?, fontWeight? }` |

Axis label and title weights follow the shared
[Canvas font-weight policy](./api/marks/text/#font-weights).

Use either `ticksAndLabels` or the independent `ticks`/`labels` options in one
call. The action validates the entire request before editing any component, so
an invalid later component cannot leave a partial result.

## Edit several existing axes

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
// Fragment: program already contains x and y axes.
program.editAxes({
  x: { labels: { fontSize: 11 } },
  y: { ticksAndLabels: { count: 4, labels: { fontSize: 11 } } }
});
```

`editAxes` groups existing channel editors in one atomic call. Omitted axes are preserved; it never creates an absent axis. See the [action reference](./reference/actions/guides/#editaxes) for the complete signature.

## Errors and limitations

Ambiguous scale or coordinate candidates require explicit IDs. Each channel
has one semantic axis, so parallel duplicate axes cannot be created.

[Guides](./api/guides/) · [Grids](./api/grids/) ·
[Advanced axis components](./advanced/axis-components/)

An explicit Cartesian `labelMap` entry with `label: ""` hides only that displayed label. Tick marks, stored tick values and scale domains stay unchanged. Empty labels remain suppressed after Canvas/scale replay; clear the map with `"auto"` to restore the normal formatter.

# Grids

Cartesian grid creators and editors accept `strokeDashMap: [{ value, strokeDash }]`
alongside the uniform `strokeDash` pattern. A matching raw typed value overrides only
that line; unmatched values use the uniform pattern. `strokeDashMap: "auto"` or `[]`
clears only the overrides. Entries do not add grid values. Patterns are even-length
arrays of finite non-negative lengths, with `[]` solid. Duplicate typed keys are errors.
Band-boundary grids use the first selected band's pattern for a shared edge.

## At a glance

| Action | Shortest call | Inference/defaults | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `createGrid` | `createGrid()` | Cartesian horizontal or applicable Polar families | Concrete guides behind related marks |
| `editGrid` | `editGrid({ horizontal: { count: 6 } })` | Existing selected directions | One or both directions rematerialized |
| `removeGrid` | `removeGrid({ vertical: true })` | Existing selected directions | Semantic, graphic, and stored grid state removed |

## `createGrid(options?)`

Cartesian grids accept continuous, band and point scales. Band grids use centers by default; set `bandPosition: "boundary"` for both edges of each selected cell. Categorical grids accept category `values` and reject `count`.

An explicit `bandPosition`, including `"center"`, requires a band scale; continuous
and point scales reject it. In `createLinePlot`, only a categorical x band scale
can use it through `guides.grid.vertical`. The horizontal grid follows the
line's continuous y scale and does not accept band positioning. Density plots use continuous value and density scales; Horizon and Rug plots use continuous quantitative or temporal measure scales. Their facade grids also reject explicit band positioning. Area plots retain categorical band grids on the independent channel: vertical for `valueChannel: "y"`, horizontal for `valueChannel: "x"`.

Set Cartesian `zIndex` to a finite rank: positive values draw above related marks, zero or negative values draw behind them. Grids on each side sort by rank, with horizontal before vertical on a tie. Editors and resizing retain the chosen order.

Creates Cartesian or Polar grid geometry from encoded scales. Cartesian
defaults to horizontal only. A Polar-only chart creates theta spokes when theta
is encoded and radial circles when radius is encoded; charts with both channels
create both families.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program.createGrid();
```

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program.createGrid({
  horizontal: {
    color: "#e2e8f0",
    lineWidth: 1,
    strokeDash: []
  },
  vertical: true
});
```

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `horizontal` | boolean or direction options | `true` |
| `vertical` | boolean or direction options | `false` |
| `theta` | boolean or Polar direction options | Polar-only: encoded theta |
| `radial` | boolean or Polar direction options | Polar-only: encoded radius |

Direction options are:

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `scale` | Scale ID; inferred from y for horizontal or x for vertical |
| `coordinate` | Cartesian coordinate ID; inferred from encoded layers |
| `count` | Positive requested line density |
| `values` | Exact finite data-space values; mutually exclusive with `count` |
| `color` | Stroke color; default `#e2e8f0` |
| `lineWidth` | Non-negative stroke width; default `1` |
| `alongOffset` | Signed finite logical-pixel displacement; vertical lines right, horizontal lines down; default `0` |
| `strokeDash` | Even-length non-negative dash array; default `[]` |

When values and count are omitted, a grid reuses compatible existing axis
ticks. Without an axis it uses histogram bin boundaries for a binned x scale,
or five nice ticks for another continuous scale. Explicit values and count
always take precedence.

`alongOffset` is independent of tick and label displacement. It applies after scale mapping and band-boundary construction, survives edits and Canvas/scale updates, and does not change the scale domain or mark positions. Use zero to reset it. Polar grids do not accept this option.

Horizontal lines span the plot width at y-scale positions. Vertical lines span
the plot height at x-scale positions. Grid graphics are inserted before the
first related mark in rendering order, even when `createGrid` is called after
that mark was created.

Canvas and connected scale changes explicitly rematerialize concrete grid
positions. Grid style is graphical state; only the resolved scale and
coordinate IDs are stored in `semanticSpec`.

The trace preserves direction-level actions:

```text
createGrid
├─ createHorizontalGrid?
└─ createVerticalGrid?
```

Polar dispatch uses `createRadialGrid` for concentric closed paths and
`createThetaGrid` for center-to-edge spokes. Theta defaults to six ticks;
radius defaults to five. A zero radial tick remains available to the axis but
does not create a degenerate zero-radius circle. Polar grid color defaults to
`#d7e0ea`.

Use `false` to disable a direction. If scale or coordinate inference is
ambiguous, provide its ID explicitly.

## Editing grids

Use the direction-specific edit actions after that grid exists:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program
  .editHorizontalGrid({ count: 6, color: "#cbd5e1" })
  .editVerticalGrid({ values: [50, 100, 150], strokeDash: [4, 2] });
```

Edit options are `count`, `values`, `color`, `lineWidth`, and `strokeDash`.
Use either `count` or `values`. `values: "auto"` restores current axis/scale
inference. At least one option is required.

Use `editGrid()` to update both directions through one aggregate action:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program.editGrid({
  horizontal: { count: 6, color: "#cbd5e1" },
  vertical: { values: [50, 100, 150], strokeDash: [4, 2] }
});
```

Both selected directions must already exist. The complete request is validated
before either directional edit runs, so an invalid vertical patch cannot leave
a partially edited horizontal grid.

Grid edits preserve the existing scale and coordinate binding. They invoke a
wrapped directional rematerialization action, replacing only that direction's
concrete line geometry and appearance. `editGrid` delegates to these same
directional actions, which remain available for focused edits.

Polar grids use the same pattern through `editThetaGrid`, `editRadialGrid`, or
`editGrid({ theta: {...}, radial: {...} })`. `removeGrid` accepts the same
direction names.

`createGuides()` selects this default horizontal grid automatically when a y
encoding is present. Pass `createGuides({ grid: false })` to opt out.

## Removing grids

`removeGrid()` removes every existing direction. Select a subset with explicit
booleans:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const noGrid = program.removeGrid();
const horizontalOnly = program.removeGrid({ vertical: true });
```

At least one direction must be selected; explicit false/false is an error.
Scales, coordinates, marks, and axes remain.

## Errors and limitations

Each selected direction requires one compatible resolved scale and matching
Cartesian or Polar coordinate. Ambiguous resources require explicit IDs.

[Guides](./api/guides/) · [Axes](./api/axes/) ·
[Advanced axis components](./advanced/axis-components/)

# Legends

 encoding + scale Guide meaning
 →
 symbol recipe Categorical, gradient, or composite
 →
 rect · line · text Concrete guide graphics

## At a glance

| Action | Shortest call | Inference/defaults | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `createLegend` | `createLegend()` | Current/unique compatible mark; right position | Categorical, size, stroke-width, gradient, interval, or opacity guide; sampled channels and gradient ticks accept exact `values` |
| `editLegend` | `editLegend({ position: "left" })` | Unique existing legend; omitted properties retained | Rematerialized content, layout, and appearance |
| `editLegendBlock` | `editLegendBlock({ target: "points", channel: "size", title: "Magnitude" })` | Explicit mark and represented channel | Only the selected logical block is rematerialized |
| Focused edits | `editLegendLabels({ fontSize: 11 })` | Same target inference as `editLegend` | One legend component rematerialized |
| `removeLegend` | `removeLegend({ channels: ["size"] })` | Existing legend owner; omitted channels remove all | Selected complete blocks removed |

Legends are inferred from final mark encodings and materialized as concrete
graphics. Start with the family that matches the encoded channel and use the
editing page when changing an existing guide.

Right and left legends start at the top of the actual plot, excluding the chart title.
The complete legend includes its visible title, symbols, labels, and optional border.
Multiple blocks share one stack whose top aligns with the plot; blocks retain their spacing.
Shared facet legends align with the top of the translated child plots.
When `offset` is omitted, the native gap follows the actual occupied axis guides on the same edge, including left and right. An explicit `offset` remains anchored to the plot.

Parallel-coordinate dimension labels and titles, and polar theta and radial
labels and titles, also reserve space outside the plot.
Their measured bounds update the default legend clearance after font edits,
Canvas resizing, and snapshot restoration.
Top, bottom, and in-plot corner positions keep their own alignment rules.

## Editing one block

Use the optional singular `channel` on `editLegend` or a focused editor to select one existing block:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
// Fragment: program already owns color and opacity legends for one point mark.
program.editLegendLabels({ channel: "opacity", fontSize: 10 });
```

This changes only the selected block. It preserves sibling typography and sample values. Specify `target`
when more than one mark owns legends. Singular `channel` cannot accompany plural `channels`, which replaces
whole-target content, or whole-group `blockLayout`/`at` controls.

## Fine positioning

Keep an edge anchor while adjusting its position with `editLegend` or `editLegendLayout`. `offset` sets the perpendicular gap from the plot; `alongOffset` is a signed pixel shift along that edge. Positive values move right on top/bottom and in-plot corners, and down on left/right. Omission preserves the value; `0` resets the shift.

> **Executable complete.** Import chart from ggaction. This complete example includes two observations, an explicit color legend and sufficient margins. Keep the returned shifted program to render the revised position.

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ plot: { width: 240, height: 180 }, margin: 130 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { x: 1, y: 2, group: "A" },
    { x: 3, y: 4, group: "B" }
  ] })
  .createScatterPlot({ id: "plot", x: "x", y: "y", color: "group", guides: false })
  .createLegend({ target: "plot", channels: ["color"] });

const shifted = program.editLegend({
  target: "plot", channel: "color", position: "bottom", offset: 60, alongOffset: -12
});
```

Fine adjustment on the same edge keeps sibling blocks in their existing slots.

This moves the color block 12 logical pixels left of its normal alignment. Omit `channel` to move the target’s legend group together. Selected blocks rejoin the group with `position: "inherit"`, which clears their local shift. Free `at` placement cannot be combined with `alongOffset`; switch back to an explicit edge first. Canvas fit and guide collision checks remain active. These positions persist through data updates, facets, shared concat legends, and saved programs. Shared concat edits validate the visible parent legend against retained content; hidden child copies do not block fine positioning.

To move only the entries while keeping the legend title anchored, use
`program.editLegend({ target: "plot", channel: "color", itemsOffset: { x: 12, y: 6 } })`.

Both coordinates are signed logical Canvas pixels: positive `x` moves right and positive `y` moves down.
Symbols and labels move together; continuous legends move the gradient and its ticks/labels.
A partial `{ x }` or `{ y }` preserves the other coordinate. Omission retains the offset;
`itemsOffset: "auto"` restores automatic body placement. Empty objects, unknown keys, and
non-finite coordinates are rejected. Use `channel: "all"` to apply the edit to all blocks.
Whole-legend moves retain this relative offset. Styles, data/scale edits, facets, scoped
compositions and saved programs preserve it, and fitting uses the shifted concrete bounds.

## Supported legend families

| Legend family | Supported marks | Channels |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Categorical color/shape/dash | point, line, area, bar, rect, arc, text | ordinal color; point shape; line strokeDash; compatible composites follow family constraints |
| Categorical stroke | point, line, area, bar, rect, arc, rule, tick | ordinal stroke; final-item or series identities |
| Continuous color gradient | point, aggregate bar, rect, text, tick | sequential color; gradient swatch, no symbol recipe |
| Continuous stroke gradient | point, line, area, bar, rect, arc, rule, tick | sequential stroke; separate gradient, no symbol recipe |
| Discretized color interval | point, aggregate bar, rect, tick | quantize/quantile/threshold color; rectangle swatches |
| Discretized stroke interval | point, line, area, bar, rect, arc, rule, tick | quantize/quantile/threshold stroke; outline-colored interval symbols |
| Size | point | size; continuous numeric samples or every discrete interval; point glyph symbol |
| Opacity | point, line, area, bar, rect | quantitative opacity samples; representative point symbol even for Line and Area consumers; Rule opacity has no legend |
| Stroke width | line, rule | quantitative strokeWidth samples; line symbol |

## Focused legend families

 [Categorical legends Create categorical, size, and interval guides and control their layout.](./api/legends/categorical/)
 [Continuous legends Gradient color and sampled opacity guides.](./api/legends/continuous/)
 [Composite symbols Layered line, point, and swatch recipes plus optional borders.](./api/legends/composite/)

## Errors and limitations

Continuous color legends support point, aggregate-bar, and rect marks. Continuous
stroke legends support every stroke-capable mark at its documented item/series grain. Field
Opacity legends support Point and Line; discretized color legends support Point, aggregate Bar, and Rect. Interactive legends are unsupported.
Combined point-series and size legends support every edge. Continuous size
blocks sample the domain; discrete size blocks show every interval.
Side positions stack the blocks; horizontal positions place them in rows. A left block must
fit outside any left y-axis guides; omitted offsets reserve this clearance automatically.
Stroke-width legends support all four edges and plot corners through `createLegend` and
`editLegendLayout`. Use `layout: "edge"`, `offset`, `itemGap`, and horizontal
`align`, `direction`, `columns`, and `titlePosition` controls. Title, count,
label/title styles, and border are editable. Side positions require vertical
direction, center alignment, one column, and a top title. Symbol recipes,
gradient, and order are unsupported; edit quantitative mapping through `editScale`.
Continuous size, opacity, stroke-width, color-symbol and color/stroke-gradient legends accept `values` for exact
ascending samples. Exact values must fit the effective domain and cannot be
combined with `count`; use `editLegend({ values: "auto" })` to return to the
remembered automatic sample count. Automatic samples retain exact domain endpoints, so rounding cannot extrapolate opacity beyond its range. For a gradient tick selection, use
`editLegend({ channel: "color", values: [40, 60, 80] })` on an existing matching
scale. Use `editLegendBlock()` for sampled blocks, order, title, labels, spacing,
and supported symbol appearance when a target has multiple blocks.
Automatic symlog gradient ticks spread across the transformed scale and include
zero when it replaces an interior sample. Automatic log, power, square-root and
symlog gradient labels are reduced when they would overlap; the stored `count`
remains the requested sampling count. A longer gradient or smaller label font can
show more ticks. Explicit `values` always remain exact, including close labels.
Right-side layout requires sufficient right margin; bottom layout requires
sufficient bottom margin; top layout requires enough top margin for its title,
item grid, offset, and optional border. A fixed outer Canvas reports a layout error when there is insufficient space. Use
`createCanvas({ plot: { width, height } })` to retain exact plot dimensions while
measured guide overflow grows the outer margins. Symbol layers are never dropped.

## Space rows by content

Create the complete legend first, then refine its spacing. This fragment requires
an existing item-based legend:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program.editLegendLayout({ rowPadding: 7, titlePadding: 20 });
```

`rowPadding` is the empty vertical distance between adjacent rows' occupied
sample and label bounds. It accounts for each row's own symbol size and stroke;
a text-only overflow row reserves only its label. Multi-column grids measure
the union of each row. `itemGap` continues to control horizontal spacing and
supplies the original vertical pitch when `rowPadding` is omitted.

`titlePadding` independently sets the occupied title-to-body distance: vertical
for top or bottom titles, horizontal for an inline left title. Hidden titles
reserve no distance. Text bounds use the library's deterministic font-size and
hard-line-break measurement, rather than browser-specific glyph ink.

Both values accept finite non-negative logical pixels, including zero.
`editLegend` and `editLegendLayout` accept `"auto"` to remove either policy;
omitting a value preserves it. Creation accepts numbers only. The original
layout is unchanged when neither policy is supplied. Gradient strips accept
`titlePadding` only; reset `rowPadding` before switching an item legend to a
gradient. Both options require `layout: "edge"`, rather than `"legacy-bottom"`.
See [editing legends](./api/legends/editing/#focused-edits) for block selection.

## Put a compact categorical legend inside the plot

Use a corner position such as `"top-left"` and
`overflow: { maxItems: 29 }` in `createLegend` or `editLegend`. The first 29
categories keep their original symbols; a text-only summary reports the remaining
count. `border: { background: "white" }` provides an opaque panel behind the
legend. The limit changes the displayed guide only, preserving every data row
and color assignment. See the [exact legend contract](./reference/actions/guides/#createlegend)
for supported anchors and layout restrictions.

For a categorical line-only sample recipe, add
`summarySymbol: "first-hidden"` inside `overflow` to paint one sample beside the
summary. It uses the first hidden category in the final legend order and retains
its mapped stroke, dash pattern, width and opacity. This does not add a category
or reveal another label. Omission keeps the text-only summary; when all entries
fit, no summary or extra sample appears. Other sample recipes and legend families
reject this option.

**Title alignment.**

Use `titleStyle: {align: "left"}` to align a top title inside the measured
legend content block. The same style accepts `"center"` and `"right"` for
categorical, gradient, interval, size, opacity and stroke-width legends. This
text alignment is separate from the complete legend's placement `align`.
Omitting it preserves the native layout's current default.

On an existing legend, `editLegendTitle({align: "right"})` changes only that
choice. `editLegendTitle({align: "auto"})` restores the native default; the
whole edit equivalent is `editLegend({titleStyle: {align: "auto"}})`. These
are fragments requiring an existing legend. A top-to-inline title transition
can reset the choice in the same whole edit; inline `titlePosition: "left"`
rejects an explicit title alignment. Border padding, group anchors, item
positions and spacing retain their existing rules.

When creating a separate size legend, an explicit `position` is honored even if a color or shape legend for the same mark uses another edge. Omit size `position` to inherit the categorical legend edge. Resizing retains that choice.

**Label alignment.** `editLegend({target: "plot", labels: {align: "right"}})`
aligns label text within each measured label column. `left`, `center`, and
`right` are supported for every legend family, including multiline labels.
Symbols, ticks, titles, and the legend's placement stay in their existing slots.
The option is also accepted at creation; omission preserves native defaults.

## Combine interval color, size, and shape

For one Cartesian point layer, `combine: "color-size-shape"` combines interval color (or stroke), interval size, and ordinal shape for the same field. Hue and size must have identical threshold boundaries. Provide one ascending finite representative per interval; the shape scale evaluates that exact value, including its configured fallback. This preserves ordinal shapes without converting them into interval bins.

> **Executable complete.** Standalone ES module with ggaction installed.

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const cuts = [5, 10, 15, 20, 25];
const points = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 1000, height: 800, margin: 250 })
  .createData({ values: Array.from({ length: 30 }, (_, value) => ({ value })) })
  .createScatterPlot({
    x: "value", y: "value", point: { fill: "none", strokeWidth: 2 },
    stroke: { field: "value", fieldType: "quantitative", scale: {
      type: "threshold", domain: cuts,
      range: ["red", "orange", "gold", "green", "blue", "purple"]
    } },
    size: { field: "value", scale: {
      type: "threshold", domain: cuts, range: [50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300]
    } },
    shape: { field: "value", scale: {
      domain: cuts, range: ["circle", "square", "triangle-up", "cross", "diamond"],
      unknown: "circle"
    } },
    guides: false
  });
const program = points.createLegend({
  combine: "color-size-shape",
  channels: ["stroke", "size", "shape"],
  values: [0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25]
});
```

Any of the three channels selects the same block for editing or removal. Use `editLegend({ combine: "separate" })` to split it. The samples inherit fixed point appearance; optional `symbol` overrides may change opacity, stroke width, or an unmapped fill/stroke, but cannot replace mapped color, size, or shape. Use `editLegendBlock` with a numeric `labelMap` for exact interval wording. Existing two-channel combinations keep their current behavior.

# Categorical and Size Legends

## `createLegend(options?)`

Creates inferred legend blocks. It supports combined line-series,
color-stacked histogram, grouped ordinal-bar, grouped area, independent stroke, composite point-series,
quantitative point-size, continuous-color gradient, and field-opacity legends.
It also infers interval swatches for quantize, quantile, and threshold point
color scales.

For a line legend that explains a categorical dash pattern, samples inherit the
line’s fixed stroke color. Mapped color or stroke scales and explicit legend-block
symbol overrides take precedence. Editing the line’s fixed color updates its
existing samples; the sample recipe’s opacity remains independent of mark opacity.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

~~~javascript
program.createLegend();
~~~

A size encoding is independently eligible; color and shape are not required:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

~~~javascript
program.createLegend({ channels: ["size"], position: "right", count: 4 });
~~~

With one size-encoded point mark, both `createLegend()` and `createGuides()`
infer the same block. Multiple size-encoded point marks require `target`.
Standalone size legends support four edges and four plot corners, edge layout, grid controls,
text styles, and borders. A size block paired with a categorical point legend
supports every edge. Continuous size scales use evenly sampled domain values.
Quantize, quantile, and threshold size scales show every interval and reject an
explicit `count`.

An explicit `channels` array selects exactly the content to create. On a point
mark encoding all three channels, use `channels: ["color", "shape", "size"]`
to include all three, or `["color", "size"]` to show color swatches and size
samples without a shape explanation. Selecting just `["color"]` or `["shape"]`
does not add a size block. Sample `count` requires size to be selected in a
categorical request and requires a continuous size scale. Encodings and mark
appearance remain unchanged.

Stroke may be selected independently with `channels: ["stroke"]`. When Point
fill and outline use different fields, create separate color and stroke blocks;
their domains, titles, symbols, edits, highlighting, and removal stay independent.

Omitting `channels` on a point mark infers its encoded categorical color, shape,
and quantitative size. Color alone uses swatches; shape uses typed symbols;
color plus size and shape plus size each create both corresponding blocks.
The result matches explicitly listing those channels. If several point marks
can own an inferred size companion, specify `target`.

Every categorical legend uses the same right-side default:

| Mark | Channels | Position | Symbol |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| line | encoded `color`, `stroke`, and/or `strokeDash` | `right` | line |
| bar histogram | `color` | `right` | swatch |
| grouped ordinal bar | `color` | `right` | swatch |
| grouped area | `color` | `right` | swatch |
| point | inferred or selected `color` only | `right` | swatch |
| point | inferred or selected `shape` only | `right` | typed point |
| point + matching line | `color` + `shape` | `right` | line over typed point |
| quantitative point size | `size` | four edges and four corners, standalone or combined | five equal-area circles |
| quantitative/temporal point color | `color` | `right` | continuous gradient with five labels; explicit symbols representation shows sampled points |
| discretized quantitative point color | `color` | `right/left/top/bottom` | ordered interval swatches |
| categorical supported-mark stroke | `stroke` | `right/left/top/bottom` | actual fill with mapped outline |
| quantitative point opacity | `opacity` | `right` | five constant-size circles with sampled opacity |

A shape-only point legend also works when the chart contains unrelated lines.
The automatic line-and-point symbol requires the point and line to share both
the encoded color field and color scale. Removing the point's color encoding
preserves its remaining shape legend.

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | compatible mark ID | current or unique compatible mark |
| `channels` | compatible channel array; continuous guides use one `color` or `opacity` | compatible encoded channels |
| `order` | `"scale"`, `{ values: [...] }`, or `{ channel: "x"/"y"/"theta" }`; categorical only | `"scale"` |
| `position` | four outside edges or `top-left/top-right/bottom-left/bottom-right` inside the plot | `"right"` |
| `blockLayout` | `"row"`, `"column"`, or `"wrap"`; layout of all blocks owned by one target | existing edge flow; new corner group uses row |
| `at` | finite `{ x, y }`; occupied group top-left relative to the plot | no free anchor |
| `layout` | categorical `"edge"` or `"legacy-bottom"` | `"edge"` |
| `align` | `"left"`, `"center"`, or `"right"` | `"center"` |
| `direction` | `"horizontal"` or `"vertical"` | `"vertical"` at either side; `"horizontal"` at top/bottom |
| `columns` | positive integer | all items in one row at top |
| `offset` | non-negative number | `8`; omission clears an occupied same-edge axis, explicit values stay plot-relative |
| `titlePosition` | `"top"` or `"left"` | `"top"` |
| `title` | non-empty string or `false` | encoded field name; `false` initially hides it |
| `symbol` | `"auto"`, shorthand object, or layered recipe | inferred from mark |
| `labels` | label style object | default sans-serif label style |
| `titleStyle` | title style object | default sans-serif title style |
| `itemGap` | positive number | `18` for vertical items; horizontal items keep `24` at top and `20` at bottom |
| `rowPadding` | non-negative finite number | omitted; opt into occupied edge-to-edge vertical row spacing |
| `titlePadding` | non-negative finite number | omitted; independently set title-to-body spacing |
| `border` | boolean or border style object | `false` |
| `count` | size-legend symbol count from `2` through `10,000` | `5` for point legends |
| `gradient` | `{ length?, thickness? }` with positive values | `{ length: 120, thickness: 12 }` |

Pass `position: "bottom"` explicitly to place the legend below the plot.
Without `rowPadding`, vertical items reserve the larger of `itemGap`, painted sample height, and
`labels.fontSize * 1.2`. This conservative line-height allowance retains the
18-pixel pitch for ordinary 12-pixel labels and grows for larger labels; it is
not a font-specific glyph-height guarantee. Horizontal grids are unchanged.
Opt-in [content spacing](./api/legends/#space-rows-by-content) uses each row's
actual sample and logical text bounds. It takes precedence over the vertical
pitch while retaining `itemGap` for column separation and later reset. Both
spacing policies override the corresponding legacy `editLegendBlock({gap})`
distance while active; resetting them restores that retained fallback.
For a combined categorical-and-size legend, `title: false` hides the categorical
title; the size block retains its independent title, matching `editLegend`.
Bottom legends use the same item grid as top legends and can use left, center,
or right alignment; side legends require center alignment. Left categorical,
composite point, and size blocks use vertical flow and preserve symbol-to-label
and resolved-domain order. Both sides use vertical direction and a top title. `columns` is a positive
integer and defaults to one on the sides. Items fill each column from top to
bottom in domain order before starting the next column. Each column reserves
its measured symbol and label width; `itemGap` separates columns. Provide
enough side margin for the complete grid. Moving a horizontal grid to either
side preserves its column count; use `titlePosition: "top"` when needed.
Incompatible direction or title options produce an error.

For example, this complete program places 21 years in three columns on the right:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({
    width: 620, height: 380,
    margin: { top: 20, right: 300, bottom: 60, left: 70 }
  })
  .createData({ values: Array.from({ length: 21 }, (_, i) => ({
    x: i, y: i % 5, year: String(1980 + i)
  })) })
  .createScatterPlot({
    x: "x", y: "y", color: { field: "year", fieldType: "ordinal" },
    guides: { legend: { position: "right", columns: 3 } }
  });
```

Categorical legends use `layout: "edge"` by default, including a bottom legend
with no other layout options. To preserve the former compact single row anchored
near the Canvas bottom edge, specify both `position: "bottom"` and
`layout: "legacy-bottom"`. This mode keeps labels at Canvas height minus 28 and
the title at height minus 52. It supports alignment, item gap, symbols, styles,
and borders; columns, vertical direction, a left title, or a custom plot offset
require `layout: "edge"`. Layout mode is preserved by edits and replay.
Large text or symbols that overlap the fixed title row, cross the plot, or
exceed the Canvas produce an error; the fixed anchors do not move.

Top and bottom legends use a general item grid. `columns` caps the column count;
`direction: "horizontal"` fills rows first and `"vertical"` fills columns
first. For a single edge legend, `align` positions the actual outer bounds of
the complete title, items and border against the plot left edge, center or right
edge. Strokes and label extents count toward these bounds. `offset` measures
the gap from the plot to the nearest outer legend edge. The final block must
fit the requested Canvas. The title appears above the grid by default, or beside it with
`titlePosition: "left"`.

Each item reserves the actual extent of every symbol layer, including strokes
and mapped shapes. Labels start after this shared sample slot plus
`labels.offset` (8 for color, 10 for series). Narrower shapes retain the same
label column. Side rows expand for large labels or symbols, with at least
12 pixels between the visible title and item content. Horizontal grids and
borders use the same extents; inline titles are vertically centered beside
the complete grid. Hidden titles reserve no space.

Plot-corner item blocks measure that 12-pixel title-to-content gap from actual
painted bounds. They do not inherit the outside side legend's fixed first-row
anchor. The native corner inset and item pitch remain unchanged; content that
still exceeds the inset plot fails without resizing or moving the plot.

A categorical legend resolves at most 10,000 domain items. A layered symbol
recipe contains at most one line, one point, and one swatch layer.

When two or more legend blocks share the top or bottom edge, the lane starts at
the plot's left edge and keeps 40 logical pixels between complete occupied
blocks. A left-positioned categorical title participates in the same inline
center line as a left-positioned sampled-opacity title.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `densityArea`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

~~~javascript
densityArea.createLegend({
  position: "top",
  direction: "vertical",
  columns: 3,
  titlePosition: "left",
  offset: 8
});
~~~

Automatic recipes refresh when a matching companion line is added, removed,
or rebound to another color scale. Creating the legend before or after the
line produces the same result. Explicit symbol recipes retain their layers
and order through those changes; `editLegend({ symbol: "auto" })` restores
inference. Title visibility and text styles remain intact.

## Item order without changing color

`createLegend` and `editLegend` accept the same categorical `order` policy.
An explicit non-empty list puts those categories first and appends omitted
categories in source first-appearance order. Explicit scale-domain entries absent
from the source remain at the end. Unknown and duplicate categories are errors.
Color, shape, and dash assignments remain attached to category values.

To follow the same target's categorical x, y, or theta domain, use
`order: { channel: "theta" }` (substitute x or y as needed). The linked encoding
must use the same field and category set as the legend. Its later order/scale
changes update the legend. Removing that encoding or changing it to an
incompatible field/domain fails; first reset with `editLegend({ order: "scale" })`.
Omitted `order` on an edit preserves the policy. Continuous and interval legends
do not accept categorical ordering.

Inside a complete chart's `guides.legend`, linked channels follow that chart's
position roles: categorical Cartesian positions use `x` or `y`; Pie, Rose, and
Radial Bar use `theta`. Line, Area, Density, and Parallel facade declarations
offer `"scale"` or explicit `values`, since their declared positions do not
provide a categorical axis to link.

### Combined categorical and size layout

Point legends can combine categorical color or shape with quantitative size on
any edge. For a point chart with both encodings, this fragment places a bordered
legend above the plot:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
program.createLegend({
  channels: ["color", "size"],
  position: "top",
  count: 3,
  offset: 30,
  columns: 2,
  border: true
});
```

At top and bottom, categorical content precedes size content with 40 pixels
between their occupied bounds. Blocks wrap to another row away from the plot
when necessary. The whole group, including its border, follows `align` and
`offset`. `direction`, `columns`, `titlePosition`, and `itemGap` apply to both
item grids. Newly combined blocks share label and title typography at every
edge, including the default title color `#334155`. Each block retains its own
title text, sample sizes, and label gap. A size legend created independently
keeps its stored styles when added to a categorical legend; its standalone
default title color remains `#0f172a`.
Opting into `blockLayout` or moving the group to a corner or free anchor retains
this typography inheritance and each symbol's paint. Placement and typography
inheritance are independent, including after Canvas, scale, data, and persistence replay.
Title spacing also includes labels that are taller than the samples.
A size border retained from an earlier standalone legend stays inside the
shared outer border. Other legends place this complete group as one block.
Combined legends require `layout: "edge"`; `"legacy-bottom"` is unsupported.
A separately positioned size legend can coexist with a categorical
`"legacy-bottom"` legend on another edge. Each keeps its own placement and styles.

## Combine ordinal size and shape

`createLegend({ combine: "size-shape" })` draws one categorical block whose
sample uses both the mapped shape and the mapped physical area. It requires
one point owner, the same nominal or ordinal field for both encodings, and
identical typed, ordered ordinal domains. Explicit `channels` must contain
exactly `"shape"` and `"size"`; with omitted channels, an encoded color legend
remains an independent block. Different owners, fields, grain, numeric size
scales, or domain order are rejected.

Omitting `combine`, or creating with `"separate"`, preserves the previous output.
An edited combination is retained unless explicitly changed. Whole-target
`editLegend({ combine: "separate" })` splits the pair and copies shared text,
title and placement styles; combining independent blocks uses supplied styles
or the combined native defaults, rather than choosing one old block's styles.
A split preserves an independent color block. Incompatible display maps must
be reset before splitting.

Either member selects the same combined block. Removing either member removes
the entire block without removing either mark encoding. Fixed sample shape or
size overrides conflict with the mapping; stroke, fill, opacity, labels and
categorical item order retain their existing controls. Zero mapped area retains
its category and text slot. Current data and scale revisions revalidate both
encodings, so an invalid revision fails instead of silently splitting the block.

## Recipe layer opacity

Each `symbol.layers` line, point or swatch accepts optional `opacity` in0..1.
The supplied value applies once to that layer's complete fill and outline;
it does not change other recipe layers, labels, title or frame. Omission keeps
historical fallback appearance. Replacing a recipe without opacity, including
`symbol:'auto'`, removes its explicit layer opacity.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
program.createLegend({
  channels: ['shape'],
  symbol: {layers: [
    {type: 'line', opacity: 0.3},
    {type: 'point', fill: 'red', stroke: 'blue', strokeWidth: 4, opacity: 0.7}
  ]}
});
```

A mapped size-shape block retains its mapped shape and physical area when the
point layer supplies opacity. Canvas uses a bounded transparent glyph source;
SVG uses whole-element opacity. PDF rasterizes only the explicitly affected
glyph, preserving surrounding vector output. Existing block symbol-opacity
patches retain their established behavior and do not opt into this new path.

## Independent legend appearance {#independent-legend-appearance}

The complete example starts with a color legend, then edits its gradient,
orientation, title and border. Its horizontal ramp measures 120 by 16 logical
pixels. The bottom title clears the full strip, ticks and labels by 12 pixels.
The border uses one continuous `[4, 2, 6, 1]` dash pattern around the frame.
A later block edit moves only the size legend to `"bottom-left"`; the gradient
keeps its own placement.

## Layered recipe opacity {#layered-recipe-opacity}

The linked canonical source has a `createRecipeOpacityProgram(opacity)` factory.
It builds one line-and-point recipe with an explicit opacity of 0, 0.7 or 1
on both layers. These are separate authored recipes; the categorical legend
does not infer opacity from individual categories. Each case retains the same
40-pixel line, 6-pixel point radius, outline and opaque label. The original
single-point opacity example remains available above.

## Sample windows

Keep an encoded size while showing only a vertical slice of its symbol:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resource selectors used here: `target: "points"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
program.createLegend({ channels: ["size"], clipHeight: 30 });
program.editLegendSymbols({ channel: "size", clipHeight: 24 });
program.editLegendBlock({ target: "points", channel: "size", clipHeight: "auto" });
```

A positive finite `clipHeight` centers the window on each glyph anchor. The
original radius, physical area, shape and stroke remain intact; the symbol is
cropped rather than shrunk. Labels, titles and frames stay outside the window.
Item spacing uses the visible sample and label bounds. Smaller symbols retain
their original height.

This applies to sampled size, opacity and color-symbol legends, combined legends,
and categorical recipes containing a point. Every layer of a composite sample
shares its window. Gradient ramps, interval swatches, line-only recipes and
stroke-width samples reject this option. Editing with `"auto"` removes the window;
omitting it preserves the current setting.

## Quantitative color and size

`createLegend({combine: "color-size"})` creates one numeric sample list for a
Cartesian circle point mark. Both encodings must use the same quantitative
field and grain, continuous scales, and identical finite domain endpoints.
Each sample uses the original color mapper and `sqrt(mappedArea / Math.PI)`;
transformed scales keep their independent mappings. Mark data and mappings do
not change. Omission keeps separate legends.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resource selectors used here: `target: "points"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
program.createLegend({combine: "color-size", values: [0, 5, 10]});
program.editLegendSymbols({channel: "color", symbol: {stroke: "black", strokeWidth: 1, opacity: 0.7}});
program.editLegendBlock({target: "points", channel: "size", labelMap: [{value: 5, label: "middle"}]});
program.editLegend({combine: "separate"});
```

Color and size select the same block. Exact values, automatic count, numeric
format, labels, title, local position, border and sample window each have one
owner. Mapped fill, size and radius cannot be overridden. A sample's stroke,
stroke width and opacity can be styled. Splitting restores a gradient and a
size list, retains compatible shared styles and placement, and carries exact
samples only to the size list. Recombining starts with combined defaults.
Incompatible field, shape, grain or endpoint edits fail atomically.

The combined legends example
compares samples 0, 5 and 10 with independently specified black, gray and white
circles of radius 1, 2 and 3.

## Related

[Legend overview](./api/legends/) · [Composite symbols](./api/legends/composite/) · [Editing legends](./api/legends/editing/)
