# Expressions and Normalization

[Family overview](./api/data/source-and-derived/) · [Exact action lookup](./reference/actions/)

## `createComputedData({ id, source?, as, expression })` {#createcomputeddata-id-source-as-expression}

Add a scalar field to every source row with a serializable formula. Full and Basic
support both existing v1 expressions and [explicit v2 expressions](./api/data/expressions-and-normalization/#version-2-expressions).
The following legacy syntax and rules describe v1:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resource selectors used here: `source: "sales"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const shares = program.createComputedData({
  id: "shares",
  source: "sales",
  as: "share",
  expression: {
    op: "divide",
    left: { field: "part" },
    right: { field: "whole" }
  }
});
```

Leaves are `{ field }` and `{ constant }`; constants may be finite numbers,
strings, booleans, or null. The closed union includes arithmetic, comparison,
boolean logic, `if`, `coalesce`, `concat`, `log`, `sqrt`, `floor`, `datePart`, `toNumber`, `getPath`, and `replaceLiteral`. Conditional
and boolean nodes short-circuit value evaluation, while every branch and field
name is structurally checked first. The action stores this data AST as
provenance and never evaluates callbacks, source strings, or arbitrary code.
Expression nodes and arrays must contain only enumerable own data properties;
getters, setters, symbol keys, hidden properties and sparse operand arrays reject
before evaluation. Argument trace summaries do not invoke getters.

Use `{ op: "toNumber", operand: { field: "amountText" } }` to explicitly convert a decimal or scientific-notation string into a finite number in a new derived field. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Empty strings, null, booleans, hexadecimal text and non-finite results reject. Finite numeric inputs remain unchanged.

Use `{ op: "floor", operand: { field: "measurement" } }` to round a finite
number down: `1.8` becomes `1`, and `-1.8` becomes `-2`. Strings require an
explicit `toNumber`; null and nonnumeric operands reject. Compose floor with
division and multiplication to derive interval bounds while retaining each row.

Use `{ op: "datePart", part: "year", operand: { op: "parseTime", operand: { field: "dateText" } } }`
to extract an integer calendar year. The only supported part is `"year"`.
The default time zone is UTC; optional `timeZone` accepts a named IANA time zone,
such as `"America/New_York"`. The operation consumes epoch milliseconds;
parse strings explicitly rather than treating numeric years as timestamps.
Null propagates; other nonnumeric or nonfinite inputs reject. Timestamps must
lie within ±8,640,000,000,000,000 milliseconds, and fractional milliseconds follow
Date's integer truncation. Years zero and before the common era retain their
astronomical numbering. Subtract extracted years to obtain calendar-year
duration, independently of elapsed days or leap years. For example, 1986-12-30
to 2024-07-17 yields `38`. Replacing the expression without `timeZone` resets UTC.

Use `{ op: "parseTime", operand: { field: "dateText" }, format: "%d/%m/%Y" }`
for an explicit day/month/year date. The closed formats are `%Y-%m-%d`,
`%d/%m/%Y`, `%m/%d/%Y`, and `auto` (the default, reusing ordinary temporal
normalization). Explicit calendar formats produce UTC millisecond timestamps;
invalid calendar dates, unparseable input, and nullish values produce `null`.
Preserve the raw field and apply an existing filter or missing-data policy to
these nulls before assigning a position. This typed node accepts no arbitrary
format expression or callback.

Use `{ op: "getPath", operand: { field: "item" }, path: ["nested", "value"] }`
to extract a scalar from nested plain records. The operand is exactly one literal
root-field reference; the path has 1–8 nonempty string keys. Keys containing dots
remain literal. Traversal reads only own data properties, never getters, arrays,
prototypes, callbacks or dynamic expressions. Missing properties and nullish
intermediates produce `null`; present non-record intermediates, non-scalar leaves
and nonfinite numbers reject. A root absent from the entire dataset rejects;
a known root missing in some rows yields `null`. Reserved path keys
`__proto__`, `prototype`, and `constructor` reject. Ordinary `{ field: "item.value" }`
still names one literal top-level field.

Use `{ op: "replaceLiteral", operand: { field: "amountText" }, search: "%", replacement: "" }`
to remove the first exact, case-sensitive `%`. Both search and replacement are
literal strings; search must be nonempty. No match preserves the input. Dollar
characters such as `$&`, `$1`, and `$$` remain literal replacement text. The
operand must evaluate to a string; null, numbers, booleans and structured values
reject without coercion. Compose with `toNumber` and arithmetic for percent
values. Regular expressions, flags and dynamic search/replacement are unsupported.

Arithmetic remains finite and strictly numeric. Other operations do not coerce
types. Undefined scalar cells normalize to null; ordinary field references still reject missing row keys. The explicit `getPath` missing-root policy above applies only to that operation.
Non-null results must have one primitive type across all rows. Expressions are
bounded to depth 16 and 128 nodes, with at most 10,000,000 row-nodes.

## Version 2 expressions

Choose `expression: { version: 2, registry: "standard@1", root }` explicitly.
The existing v1 syntax retains its results, limits, and errors. Version 2 uses
eight node kinds:

| Node | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| Literal | `{ type: "literal", value }` |
| Literal field name | `{ type: "field", name }` |
| Nested field | `{ type: "fieldPath", root, path }` |
| Named scalar input | `{ type: "parameter", id }` |
| Unary operation | `{ type: "unary", op, operand }` |
| Binary operation | `{ type: "binary", op, left, right }` |
| Conditional | `{ type: "if", condition, then, else }` |
| Registry function | `{ type: "call", name, args, options? }` |

Unary operations are `negate` and `not`. Binary operations are `add`, `subtract`,
`multiply`, `divide`, `eq`, `neq`, `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, `gte`, `and`, and `or`.
The closed function registry covers numeric, string, array, and calendar
operations. Use [getExpressionFunctions](./inspection/#expression-functions)
to inspect names, argument limits, input/output types, and option families.
Trigonometric calls require `options.angleUnit` (`radians` or `degrees`).
`parseTime` requires an explicit `format` (`%Y-%m-%d`, `%d/%m/%Y`, `%m/%d/%Y`,
or `iso-offset`). `datePart` requires `part` and `timeZone`; `timeFloor` requires
`unit` and `timeZone`, plus `weekStartsOn` from 0 (Sunday) to 6 for a week.

Every branch is validated before evaluation, including inactive references and
known field types. `if`, `and`, `or`, and `coalesce` evaluate only their selected
values. Conditions require booleans. A field name containing dots remains one
literal column name; `fieldPath` traverses up to eight own record keys and
produces missing when an optional path is absent.

Missing (`undefined`) and `null` remain distinct. Nullish arithmetic and numeric
domain failures produce missing; nullish comparisons return false. Invalid operand
types still reject the complete action. Computed outputs must have one scalar
type among non-null, non-missing values. Materialization reports include evaluated
and missing row counts plus numeric/domain/bounds diagnostics; read them through
[program inspection](./inspection/). No invalid source row is silently removed.

Version 2 limits depth to 64, nodes to 4,096, arguments per call to 64, and
row-node work to 10,000,000. Strings have at most 1,048,576 UTF-16 units,
arrays at most 100,000 elements, and cumulative value work at most 10,000,000.
Callback functions, source strings, regular expressions, custom registries,
getters, and executable objects are unsupported.

## Parameters

`createParameter({ id, value, type?, nullable? })` creates a named scalar input.
The ID is required. Type is inferred from a non-null number, string, or boolean;
numbers must be finite. The default `nullable` is false. To start at null, supply
both the intended `type` and `nullable: true`. Zero, negative zero, false, and
an empty string remain valid values. Undefined, objects, arrays, and Date values
are invalid; convert dates to epoch milliseconds explicitly when needed.

This complete ES module creates a computed column, then updates its parameter:

> **Executable complete.** Run this standalone ES module; all data and imports are included. Both immutable programs own a Canvas and materialized point chart.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const original = chart().createCanvas()
  .createData({ id: "sales", values: [{ amount: 10 }, { amount: 20 }] })
  .createParameter({ id: "factor", value: 2 })
  .createComputedData({
    id: "adjusted", as: "adjustedAmount",
    expression: {
      version: 2, registry: "standard@1",
      root: {
        type: "binary", op: "multiply",
        left: { type: "field", name: "amount" },
        right: { type: "parameter", id: "factor" }
      }
    }
  })
  .createScatterPlot({ id: "points", data: "adjusted", x: "amount", y: "adjustedAmount" });
const updated = original.editParameter({ target: "factor", value: 3 });
console.log(original.semanticSpec.datasets.at(-1).values.map(row => row.adjustedAmount)); // [20, 40]
console.log(updated.semanticSpec.datasets.at(-1).values.map(row => row.adjustedAmount)); // [30, 60]
```

`editParameter({ target, value })` preserves the parameter's type and nullability.
An edit has a total work limit of 10,000,000 input row operations across its
dependent transforms; computed transforms count one operation per AST node per
input row. The count uses the new rows after filtering. Exceeding the limit rejects
the edit and preserves the earlier program.
It revises all dependent datasets and chart consumers atomically, including shared
lookup dependencies, scales, guides, and highlights. Unrelated branches stay shared.
An unchanged value preserves revisions; negative zero and zero are distinct edits.
A failed computation or consumer validation leaves the original program unchanged.

If a parameter is used by a live data source URL, a changed value requires
[`prepareDataUpdate` and `applyDataUpdate`](./api/data/source-and-derived/#prepared-data-updates).
A direct changed-value `editParameter` reports `prepared-data-required`.
An unchanged value still needs no loading or revision. The prepared path updates
all affected source tables and computed consumers together.

`removeParameter({ id })` requires an existing, unreferenced parameter. Remove or
rewrite every consuming expression first; retained datasets also count as references.
Deletion has no cascade or force mode. Creation and v2 computed creation are available
in Full and Basic; parameter editing and removal require Full.

Parameters belong to one unit. Use an explicit `childPath` when editing a concat
child. Facet and repeated-chart parent edits update their retained source and
rebuild the dependent children. [Editable snapshots](./data-updates/#save-and-restore-snapshots)
preserve the parameter values and exact revisions without rerunning expressions
when restored. Earlier runtimes reject snapshots containing unsupported parameter
or expression versions.

## `createNormalizedData({ id, source?, field, as, groupBy?, method, ... })` {#createnormalizeddata-id-source-field-as-groupby-method}

Materialize common row-preserving comparisons without manually joining group
statistics back to source rows:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resource selectors used here: `source: "sales"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const indexed = program.createNormalizedData({
  id: "indexed",
  source: "sales",
  field: "revenue",
  as: "revenueIndex",
  groupBy: "region",
  method: "index",
  sortBy: [{ field: "year", order: "ascending" }]
});
```

`share`, `minmax`, and `zscore` summarize each group. Z-scores use population
variance by default and support `variance: "sample"`. `index`, `change`, and
`percentChange` use a finite explicit baseline or the first/last row from a
stable non-empty `sortBy`. Index values use 100 as the baseline; percent change
is a fraction, so a 50% increase produces `0.5`.

An exact zero denominator rejects by default. Use
`zeroDenominator: "null"` or `"zero"` to select an explicit replacement.
`change` accepts a zero baseline and therefore has no zero-denominator option.
Share rejects negative input. Every method preserves original row order and
keeps group calculations independent.

# Missing Keys and Values

[Family overview](./api/data/source-and-derived/) · [Exact action lookup](./reference/actions/)

## `createCompleteData({ id, source?, key, groupBy?, values?, sequence?, calendar?, fill?, members? })` {#createcompletedata-id-source-key-groupby-values-sequence-fill-members}

Materialize missing keys inside each observed group without silently turning
absence into zero:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resource selectors used here: `source: "sales"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const completed = program.createCompleteData({
  id: "completeSales",
  source: "sales",
  groupBy: "region",
  key: "month",
  values: [1, 2, 3],
  fill: { amount: null },
  members: "sourceRows"
});
```

`values`, `sequence`, and `calendar` are mutually exclusive. If all are omitted, the action
uses the key values observed anywhere in the source, preserving typed identity
and first appearance. A numeric sequence uses finite `start`, `end`, and
positive `step`. Only observed group tuples are completed; the action does not
form a Cartesian product of separate grouping fields.

Repeated observations for a group/key pair are preserved in source order, without
aggregation. Only absent pairs receive one synthesized row. Existing keys outside an
explicit domain are errors. Original rows keep all cells. A synthesized row gets
the group and key values, then `fill` values or `null` for the other source fields.
When `members` is present, original rows contain their source index and synthetic
rows contain `[]`. Output follows group first appearance and key-domain order and
is capped at 10,000 rows, including repeated observations, before allocation.

### Complete a calendar day range

Use `calendar: { unit: "day", start, end, timeZone }` for a contiguous range of
civil dates. Both endpoints are included. `start` and `end` are strict Gregorian
`YYYY-MM-DD` strings, and `timeZone` is required: use `"UTC"` or an IANA name.
For example, `2024-01-01` through `2024-12-31` contains 366 days.

First bucket timestamps in the same zone and explicitly aggregate repeated
observations. This complete ES module preserves a missing day as `null` and an
observed zero as `0`:

> **Executable complete.** Standalone ES module with ggaction installed; the sample declares all input events.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const dayRange = {
  unit: "day", start: "2024-11-02", end: "2024-11-04",
  timeZone: "America/New_York"
};
const daily = chart()
  .createData({ id: "events", values: [
    { at: "2024-11-03T05:30:00Z", amount: 2 },
    { at: "2024-11-03T06:30:00Z", amount: 3 },
    { at: "2024-11-04T12:00:00Z", amount: 0 }
  ] })
  .createTimeUnitData({
    id: "buckets", field: "at", unit: "day", as: "day",
    timeZone: dayRange.timeZone
  })
  .createSummaryData({
    id: "totals", groupBy: "day",
    aggregates: [{ op: "sum", field: "amount", as: "total" }]
  })
  .createCompleteData({
    id: "days", key: "day", calendar: dayRange,
    fill: { total: null }, members: "sourceRows"
  });

const dailyPlot = daily.createCanvas()
  .createPointMark({ data: "days", missing: "skip" })
  .encodeX({ field: "day", fieldType: "temporal" })
  .encodeY({ field: "total" });
```

The two repeated clock-hour events sum to `5` on November 3. Day starts are
stored as epoch milliseconds; neighboring starts can be 23 or 25 hours apart.
A midnight gap uses the first valid instant of that day. A civil date removed
by a zone transition is an error. Results do not depend on the process time zone.

Source keys must exactly match the generated numeric day starts. Completion
does not parse strings, floor midday timestamps, or convert keys from another
zone. It keeps repeated rows unless you aggregate them first. Synthetic rows
have no contributing input rows. An empty ungrouped source creates the requested
days; an empty grouped source creates no groups. Declare the key and group
fields in the source schema when creating an empty source.

The domain and total output each have a 10,000-item limit. Calendar completion
also preflights a 10,000,000-unit work budget covering source cells, zone boundary
resolution, group expansion, output cells, and row provenance. A wide source or
many groups can reach this limit before the row limit.

`editCompleteData({ target: "days", calendar: { ...dayRange, end: "2024-11-05" } })`
replaces the whole calendar policy. Supplying `values` or `sequence` switches
domain mode; omitting all three preserves the current policy. Source revisions
recompute the pipeline and reject newly observed dates outside the range.

## `createImputedData({ id, source?, fields, groupBy?, sortBy?, method?, value?, edges?, maxGap? })` {#createimputeddata-id-source-fields-groupby-sortby-method-value-edges-maxgap}

Replace explicit `null` or `undefined` cells without changing row grain or final
source order:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `completed`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const imputed = completed.createImputedData({
  id: "imputedSales",
  fields: "amount",
  groupBy: "region",
  sortBy: [{ field: "month" }],
  method: "linear",
  edges: "keep"
});
```

Omitted `method` means `"mean"`: each numeric field uses the observed finite-value mean within its group. For example, `completed.createImputedData({ id: "means", fields: "amount", groupBy: "region" })` preserves all other cells and row order. A group with no observed value follows `edges`; sort order is optional.

`constant` requires `value`. `forward` and `backward` copy the nearest available
anchor in the requested stable group order. `linear` requires one ascending
numeric or temporal-string sort field and finite numeric target values; it uses
actual position distance rather than row indexes. No method crosses a group
boundary.

`edges` defaults to `"keep"`; `"error"` rejects an eligible run with no required
anchor. `maxGap` is a positive row-count limit. A longer run stays missing and is
not converted into an edge error. `NaN` and infinities are invalid values rather
than missing cells.

<!-- Source: /api/data/revisions-and-removal/ -->

# Data Revisions and Removal

[Family overview](./api/data/source-and-derived/) · [Exact action lookup](./reference/actions/)

Aligned-array datasets use `editFlattenData({target, fields?, as?, dependents?})` in the Full entry point.
Basic supports creation without expanding its public editing surface. Alias roles follow the original
input field, so alias changes rebind compatible direct consumers. When changing the number of selected
fields, provide a matching alias array. Generic `editDerivedData` accepts the same `flatten` definition.

Named lookups use `editLookupData({target, field?, lookup?, dependents?})` in Full.
A supplied `lookup` replaces its whole reference definition. Revisions of either input
update the joined records and their consumers in dependency order. Change the primary
source through `reviseData`; generic transform definitions cannot replace `source`.

## Keeping rows identified across source revisions

`reviseData({source, id, values, schema?, keys?, rowMap?})` creates an immutable
snapshot and refreshes its consumers. A source created with `keyField` or
`keyFields` keeps that definition. A source created with separate `keys`
requires a complete new `keys` array. Matching keys retain item identity even
when row order or values change; a removed key can reappear later.

For a source without explicit keys, replacement rows get new identities by
default. Pass `rowMap` to retain known correspondence: each output position
contains its old row index or `null` for a new row. The array must match the new
row count and cannot repeat old indices. Keyed sources reject `rowMap`.
Independent branches allocate distinct identities for new rows. Earlier
programs remain unchanged, and invalid mappings reject the whole revision.

For a live source created with `prepareDataUpdate`, use a prepared `revise`
request to reload its URL or name while retaining that binding. A direct
`reviseData` call with application-owned rows detaches the live binding after
consumer validation succeeds. The original snapshot retains its receipt; the
new rows are not recorded as a response from the old URL. An unused live output
can be removed with `removeData`, which also removes its binding.

## Editing derived data {#editing-derived-data}

Every standalone value-producing data action creates a logical dataset owner.
The owner ID remains stable while successful edits create immutable physical
revisions. Use the generic action when an editor must receive a complete
normalized transform definition:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resource selectors used here: `target: "twice"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const revised = program.editDerivedData({
  target: "twice",
  definition: {
    type: "computed",
    as: "value2",
    expression: {
      op: "multiply",
      left: { field: "value" },
      right: { constant: 3 }
    }
  },
  dependents: "recompute"
});
```

`definition` contains only the requested public transform. It cannot contain a
dataset `id`, `source`, materialized `resolved` values, or a revision pointer.
The Complete transform may still use its own `values` domain because that field
is part of the transform rather than a dataset value envelope. Generic edits
replace the complete transform definition. Source replacement remains exclusive
to the compatibility-preserving `editBin2DData` API.

Focused editors accept partial transform changes and preserve every omitted
top-level decision:

| Transform family | Focused editor |
| --- | --- |
| computed | `editComputedData` |
| filter | `editFilteredData` |
| sort | `editSortedData` |
| fold | `editFoldData` |
| summary | `editSummaryData` |
| one-dimensional bin | `editBinData` |
| time unit | `editTimeUnitData` |
| window | `editWindowData` |
| density | `editDensityData` |
| stack | `editStackData` |
| regression | `editRegressionData` |
| interval | `editIntervalData` |
| ECDF | `editECDFData` |
| normalize | `editNormalizedData` |
| complete | `editCompleteData` |
| impute | `editImputedData` |

Each focused action requires `target`. It accepts the stable logical owner ID or
the owner's current physical revision ID. An older physical revision is stale
and rejects. A dataset produced privately inside a chart facade is chart-owned
and must be changed through that chart's editor. At creation time, `source` accepts either an
ordinary physical dataset ID or a logical owner ID; a logical source always
resolves to its current revision at call time. Focused editors do not accept a
new `source` (except the separately documented `editBin2DData` compatibility API).
To replace source rows, create a new source and rebuild its derivation, then
use `bindMarkData` for eligible independent marks.

`dependents` defaults to `"reject"`. An edit therefore fails atomically when a
derived dataset reads the target. Pass `dependents: "recompute"` to revise the
entire downstream closure in deterministic topological order. The editor first
builds and validates a speculative program. Only then does it record the same
revisions in the returned program, rebind all direct marks and known stored data
references, and release obsolete physical revisions in reverse topological
order. A cycle or an unsupported internal transform aborts the operation without
altering the input program.

Output names are tracked by semantic role. Renaming a role updates downstream
field references and visual encodings when the old name has one unambiguous
meaning. A rename rejects if the old output name is shared by several roles or
if a downstream expression contains a field reference that cannot be rewritten
safely. Mode changes clear fields owned by the previous mode before the new
definition is normalized. In focused weighted editors, `weight: false` removes
an existing weight; omission preserves it.

## `editSortedData({ target, sortBy, dependents? })` {#edit-sorted-data}

Replace the complete sort-key list for an existing sorted-data owner. Omitted
keys are not merged because their precedence is part of the ordering meaning.
The edit creates a new immutable physical revision, preserves the logical owner,
and follows the same stable comparison and null-placement rules as
`createSortedData`. Use `dependents: "recompute"` when downstream derived data
must advance with the new row order.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `ordered`. Resource selectors used here: `target: "orderedSales"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const descending = ordered.editSortedData({
  target: "orderedSales",
  sortBy: [{ field: "revenue", fieldType: "quantitative", order: "descending" }]
});
```

An edit must change the requested transform or source. A semantic no-op throws
before creating a revision. Successful revisions use deterministic IDs of the
form `<owner><Role>Revision<n>`. Earlier `ChartProgram` values remain unchanged.
The returned program keeps the previous current dataset unless it pointed at the
edited current revision, in which case it moves to the new revision.

The following chain demonstrates rejection by default, downstream replay, and
logical-source reuse:

> **expected-error.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resource selectors used here: `source: "raw"`; `source: "twice"`; `target: "twice"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const before = chart()
  .createData({ id: "raw", values: [{ x: 1 }, { x: 2 }, { x: 3 }] })
  .createComputedData({
    id: "twice",
    source: "raw",
    as: "scaled",
    expression: {
      op: "multiply",
      left: { field: "x" },
      right: { constant: 2 }
    }
  })
  .createSummaryData({
    id: "average",
    source: "twice",
    aggregates: [{ op: "mean", field: "scaled", as: "mean" }]
  });

// Expected failure: an existing descendant requires an explicit replay policy.
try {
  before.editComputedData({ target: "twice", expression: {
    op: "multiply", left: { field: "x" }, right: { constant: 3 }
  } });
} catch (error) {
  console.log(error.message);
}

const after = before.editComputedData({
  target: "twice",
  expression: {
    op: "multiply",
    left: { field: "x" },
    right: { constant: 3 }
  },
  dependents: "recompute"
});

// before still has mean 4; after has mean 6.
// A later source: "twice" resolves to the new current revision in after.
```

## `removeData({ id })` {#removedata-id}

Full programs can delete one named dataset after its final live consumer has
been removed:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resource selectors used here: `target: "temporaryPoints"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const cleaned = program
  .removeMark({ target: "temporaryPoints" })
  .removeData({ id: "temporaryRows" });
```

The ID is always explicit. `removeData` does not infer the current dataset and
does not support batches, cascading deletion, or `force`. It rejects a dataset
still used by a mark, another derived dataset, a retained facet recipe, or a
chart-owned statistical resource. The error lists each owner and its exact
reference path, so callers can remove or rebind those consumers first.

A current-data pointer alone does not keep a dataset alive. Successful removal
clears that pointer without selecting a replacement. Historical action traces
also do not keep resources alive. A standalone logical transform can be removed
by its logical ID after its final consumer is gone; its current revision and
owner record are deleted together while its upstream source remains.

Removal changes no graphics, domains, layout, or composition children. It is
available from `ggaction` and absent from `ggaction/basic`. Concat parents do not
offer cross-child removal; call the action in the program that owns the resource.

<!-- Source: /api/composition/facets/ -->

# Facets and Field Repetition

[Family overview](./api/composition/) · [Exact action lookup](./reference/actions/)

## Use different horizontal and vertical gaps

A facet can set `gap: { x: 32, y: 48 }` to leave more space between rows than
between columns. The existing number form applies the same gap in both directions.
This complete example preserves one plot per panel:

> **Executable complete.** Import chart from ggaction. This complete program includes all four panel rows and retains the original dataset while creating the facet.

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 240, height: 180 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { panel: "A", x: 1, y: 2 }, { panel: "B", x: 2, y: 3 },
    { panel: "C", x: 3, y: 1 }, { panel: "D", x: 4, y: 4 }
  ] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: "x", y: "y" })
  .facet({ field: "panel", columns: 2, gap: { x: 32, y: 48 } });
```

Both keys are required, even for a single row or column. Values must be finite and
non-negative; partial objects and unknown keys are rejected. The same pair is
supported by field repetition and row-column grids. Existing spacing rules still
apply: canvas gaps separate child canvases, plot gaps separate data regions, and
content gaps separate retained content. A row-column grid still rejects content
spacing. Titles, headers, guides and legends keep their existing ownership and
collision checks. Concat continues to accept only a number.

## Declare a legend for the complete facet

Pass a legend object to `guides.legend` to create it against the combined inner plots.
This runnable example keeps each child plot 60 pixels wide while its parent legend uses
the 246-pixel union of four plots and three 2-pixel gaps:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ plot: { width: 60, height: 275 }, margin: { top: 35, right: 5, bottom: 60, left: 45 } })
  .createData({ values: Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, i) => ({
    x: i, y: i + 1, group: i % 2 ? "B" : "A", panel: String(i % 4)
  })) })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: "x", y: "y", color: "group", guides: false })
  .facet({ field: "panel", columns: 4, spacing: "plot", gap: 2,
    guides: { axes: "outer", legend: { position: "top-left" } } })
  .editLegendTitle({ fontSize: 11 })
  .editLegendLabels({ fontSize: 10 });
```

The object uses ordinary `LegendOptions` defaults. `target` refers to the source mark;
it is inferred only when unique. Child legend styles are independent. Use `"shared"`
to promote or infer the template legend with its existing behavior, and `false` for
no parent shared guide. Child dimensions and margins stay fixed.

Automatic `"shared"` inference keeps continuous or discretized color and stroke
in separate native legend blocks, each using its own scale. Compatible ordinal
channels keep their combined categorical symbols. A mark with numeric color can
also retain an ordinal shape companion. Existing child legend owners keep
their configured styles when promoted.

Existing legend editors, channel/block selectors and removal work on facet, grid and
repeat parents. A missing parent legend can be declared with
`editFacetGuides({ legend: { position: "top-left" } })`. Removing the final block keeps
it absent during later edits. `"shared"` restores template promotion; an object replaces
the parent declaration. `createLegend` remains an action for unit charts.

Corners and free `at` coordinates use the final plot union. Explicit local block anchors
use the same union. Occupied text, symbols and border must fit and clear retained axes,
headers and the chart title. A layout edit that makes the union too small fails without
changing the previous program. Parent styles and automatic title/sample/offset policies
survive data, source, scale, theme, text-metric and layout changes and editable persistence.
Shared appearance scales and compatible source mark recipes are required in every child.

Point-bearing parent legend blocks support `clipHeight` just like unit legends.
Each block retains its own window during layout edits and editable import; a
clipped size block can share its owner with an unclipped color gradient.
Use `editLegendBlock({ target: "scatterPlot", channel: "size", clipHeight: "auto" })`
to remove only the selected block window.

A color-size combination also works on a parent: use `combine: "color-size"`
with `channels: ["color", "size"]` for one Cartesian circle-point source whose
color and size encode the same quantitative field with matching domain endpoints.
The two channels select one combined block. Both scale bindings, samples and
`clipHeight` survive saving, loading and layout edits; removing that block leaves
other parent legend blocks intact.

## Rotate panel headers

Put a region name beside its panel with the existing header editor:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
program.editFacetHeaders({
  role: "column",
  side: "left",
  rotation: { value: -90, unit: "degrees" }
});
```

This is a fragment for an existing facet program. A one-field facet uses the
`column` header role for each panel, including panels arranged in one column.
Grid facets also provide a `row` role. The [complete example](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/facet-header-rotation)
declares the axes and grid before arranging the two region panels.

The same `rotation` option is available in common `headers` and in
`headers.row` or `headers.column` during `facet`, `facetGrid` and `repeatCharts`.
A number means radians; the structured form makes the unit explicit. Omission
preserves the current choice, and `0` restores the unrotated layout.

For role headers, `offset` measures the outward gap to the rotated text block;
`align` positions that block along the plot edge. The layout reserves its rotated
width or height. With plot spacing, an outer rotated header uses existing child
margin space before reserving more. Child plots keep their sizes. Text that
crosses the Canvas, another header or a retained guide still fails clearly.
Legacy headers inside child canvases retain their existing anchor when rotated;
increase their margin or offset when the rotated text needs more room.

For an existing facet with plot spacing, the fragment
`program.editFacetHeaders({ anchor: "content" })` moves each header outward when its
marks extend beyond the plot edge. Alignment along the edge still follows the plot.
This uses concrete mark geometry, including strokes and clipping, regardless of
opacity; axes, legends and titles are excluded. The same option works in initial
`headers`, including row and column overrides. Field titles keep their plot anchor.
Omission or `anchor: "plot"` preserves the existing placement. Content anchoring
requires `spacing: "plot"` or `"content"` and sufficient space; it never changes child plot sizes.

## Repeat the current chart by a field

Call `facet` on one complete unit chart to repeat it for each observed field
value:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const faceted = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 250, height: 230 })
  .createData({ values: cars })
  .createPointMark()
  .encodeX({ field: "Horsepower" })
  .encodeY({ field: "Miles_per_Gallon" })
  .encodePointRadius({ value: 2.5 })
  .encodeColor({ field: "Cylinders", fieldType: "ordinal" })
  .facet({
    field: "Origin",
    columns: 3,
    guides: { legend: "shared" }
  })
  .createTitle({ text: "Horsepower and Fuel Economy" });
```

The input rows in this runnable fragment must contain complete values for the
encoded fields. See the
[repository example](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/cars-origin-scatterplot-facet)
for the complete data preparation and guide options.

Data-bound Cartesian text layers also repeat: encode x, y, and text before
faceting. Label data must share the partition ancestor; filters replay per cell.
Reuse the point layer's scale IDs to align labels with its positions. A cell with
no matching label rows retains its other marks.

`facet` uses field values in source first-appearance order. It infers one
common row-preserving dataset ancestor, then filters and replays supported
derived data independently inside each cell. Omitted `columns` creates one row;
a positive value wraps cells row-major. A facet uses the shared 10,000 generated-item limit,
and source-row count multiplied by child count must not exceed the shared
10,000,000-unit work budget.

To facet on a key created by `createFoldData`, pass its materialized dataset ID
explicitly as `data`. Every repeated layer must depend on that fold snapshot.
The original wide rows, fold definition and complete folded table remain intact;
each child filters the folded table, then replays only downstream transforms.
Omitting `data` keeps the usual row-preserving inference. Other statistical
transforms do not become valid partition anchors. `facetGrid` accepts the same
explicit fold boundary. Changing a fold definition creates a new snapshot;
select that snapshot explicitly when creating a new composition.

Explicit tick, label, and grid values are intersected with each cell domain; shared scales restore the source selection.

Final-item `filterMarks` recipes are also evaluated within each partition, after
the target mark has been rebound to that partition. Empty matches preserve
shared-scale panels, and `editFacetSource` can add, replace, or remove the filter.

| Option | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `"facet"` | Names the parent and deterministic child namespaces |
| `field` | required | Field in the selected partition dataset whose values define cells |
| `data` | unique common ancestor | Selects a common row-preserving ancestor, or an explicit materialized fold snapshot shared by every layer |
| `values` | source first-appearance order | Selects and orders a non-empty set of observed scalar values |
| `columns` | number of values | Sets the grid column count |
| `gap` | `16` | Sets horizontal and vertical cell spacing |
| `spacing` | `"canvas"` | Measures gaps between child canvases or, with `"plot"`, inner plot tracks; `"content"` independently packs full retained bounds |
| `topLane` | `"stacked"` | With plot spacing, `"shared"` places parent title and top headers in the existing top margin |
| `align` | `"center"` | Aligns unequal cells inside grid tracks |
| `padding` | `0` on every side | Adds scalar or four-side parent padding |
| `scales` | every used role `"shared"` | Sets `"shared"` or `"independent"` per `x`, `y`, `xOffset`, `yOffset`, `theta`, public `r`, `color`, `stroke`, `size`, `shape`, `opacity`, `strokeDash`, or all `parallelDimensions` |
| `headers` | default header style | Common text style/map plus optional `row` and `column` overrides; role objects also accept `side` |
| `guides.axes` | `"each"` | `"outer"` keeps occupied-edge Cartesian x/y axes; `{ x: "outer", y: "each" }` shares only X; Polar and Parallel axes remain local and reject `"outer"` |
| `guides.legend` | `false` | `"shared"` promotes one compatible parent-owned categorical, gradient, discretized-color, size, or opacity legend |

Author the legend position on the unit chart before calling `facet`. Promotion
preserves an explicit `left`, `right`, `top`, or `bottom` edge and the
horizontal `align` used by top and bottom legends; there is no separate facet
legend-position option:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const source = chart()
  .createCanvas({
    width: 420,
    height: 300,
    margin: { top: 40, right: 40, bottom: 90, left: 60 }
  })
  .createData({ values: cars })
  .createPointMark()
  .encodeX({ field: "Horsepower" })
  .encodeY({ field: "Miles_per_Gallon" })
  .encodeColor({ field: "Cylinders", fieldType: "ordinal" })
  .createLegend({
    channels: ["color"],
    position: "bottom",
    direction: "horizontal",
    align: "center"
  });

const facetedWithBottomLegend = source.facet({
  field: "Origin",
  columns: 1,
  guides: { legend: "shared" }
});
```

For a promoted top or bottom legend, the parent reserves a horizontal lane and
keeps the child-grid width unchanged. Left and right legends reserve a vertical
lane instead. If the source has no concrete legend and `facet` infers the
legacy categorical shared legend, the default remains `right`. Subsequent
`editCompositionLayout` calls preserve the promoted edge and alignment.

Shared auto domains use the full faceted result; independent auto domains are
resolved from each cell. An explicit semantic domain always wins. Regression,
density, interval/error-band, and box-summary/outlier datasets are replayed
after the cell filter, so each panel receives a fresh statistical result rather
than a clipped copy of the full-chart result.

The Cartesian slice supports point, line, area, histogram, aggregate bar,
ranged bar, rule, regression, density, interval/error-band, and box-plot layers.
Polar Point, Line, direct Arc, Pie, Rose, and Radar charts and Parallel-coordinate
charts can also be faceted when their visible layers share one valid
row-preserving partition ancestor and one coordinate family. Public scale
policy `r` addresses the semantic radius role; `radius` is not an alias.
`parallelDimensions` applies one policy independently to every dimension scale,
so unrelated units are never merged into one domain. Shared domains do not
share pixel ranges: every Polar frame and Parallel dimension position is
resolved against its child Canvas.

These are fragments that require already-complete unit programs:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `polarUnit`, `parallelUnit`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const radialPanels = polarUnit.facet({
  field: "region",
  scales: { theta: "shared", r: "independent" }
});

const parallelPanels = parallelUnit.facet({
  field: "region",
  scales: { parallelDimensions: "shared" }
});
```

A shared legend is accepted only when every represented child scale and legend
recipe is concretely compatible; scale resolution alone does not make a guide
shareable. Polar theta/radius axes and Parallel dimension axes remain inside
each panel. Requesting outer axes for either family fails before a composition
is returned.

Create a chart title after `facet` so the title is owned directly by the
parent. A title that already fits the unit Canvas is promoted for authoring
order compatibility rather than repeated in every cell.

The parent title aligns to the union of the child plot bounds, excluding cell
margins and the shared legend. Each repeated header is likewise centered on
its own child plot—not on the complete child Canvas—so asymmetric axis space
does not visually offset panel titles.

Edit the repeated header style without addressing generated graphic IDs:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `faceted`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const emphasized = faceted.editFacetHeaders({
  fontSize: 13,
  fontWeight: 700,
  color: "#0f172a",
  offset: 10
});
```

Facet-header weights follow the shared
[Canvas font-weight policy](./api/marks/text/#font-weights).

An unqualified edit updates the common header style and keeps the existing
one-header-per-cell layout. A row or column role switches to separate strips:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const labeledMatrix = matrix
  .editFacetHeaders({
    labelMap: [{ value: "Q1", label: "First quarter" }]
  })
  .editFacetHeaders({
    role: "row",
    side: "left",
    align: "center",
    labelMap: [{ value: "North", label: "Northern region" }]
  })
  .editFacetHeaders({
    role: "column",
    side: "bottom",
    align: "start"
  });
```

Row-column grids create one header for each occupied column, followed by one
for each occupied row. One-field facets and `repeatCharts` support the column
role and retain one header per cell. Supported sides depend on the facet topology:

| Facet topology and role | Supported sides |
| --- | --- |
| Row-column grid, row headers | `left`, `right` |
| Row-column grid, column headers | `top`, `bottom` |
| One-field facet or repeat, column headers | `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right` |

For one-field facets, `editFacetHeaders({ role: "column", side: "right" })`
places each value beside its own panel. Left/right headers reserve measured
width for every physical column, including wrapped grids with zero gap or
padding. Child plot sizes stay unchanged. `align` follows the vertical plot
span on the sides and the horizontal plot span at the top/bottom.
Role settings override the common style and map.
`labelMap: "auto"` on a role returns to the common map, while an unqualified
reset returns to the normal visible formatter. Typed raw values remain the
partition identity. Duplicate display text and `""` are allowed; an empty
mapped header keeps its stable item position and reserves no strip space.

Header strips are measured before child placement. Changes to fonts, labels,
sides, composition layout, titles, or shared legends therefore rebuild the
required parent space without moving or rewriting child program identity.

A complete example with a right-side header for each panel:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const panels = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 200, height: 160, margin: 35 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { panel: "First", category: "A", value: 2 },
    { panel: "Second", category: "A", value: 5 }
  ] })
  .createBarPlot({ x: "category", y: "value", guides: false })
  .facet({ field: "panel", columns: 2, gap: 0, padding: 0 })
  .editFacetHeaders({ role: "column", side: "right" });
```

## Build a row and column facet grid

Use `facetGrid` when two source fields define the comparison:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `unit`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const matrix = unit.facetGrid({
  id: "matrix",
  rows: { field: "region", values: ["North", "South"] },
  columns: { field: "period", values: ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3"] },
  combinations: "full",
  gap: 12
});
```

Omitted row or column `values` use source first-appearance order. `"observed"`
creates children only for pairs present in the source while retaining each
pair's actual grid coordinates. `"full"` creates the Cartesian
product. A missing pair remains a named Canvas with its semantic layers,
coordinate, canonical empty graphics, and header, so neighboring cells never
shift into its position. Shared domains are inferred from populated cells and
allow the empty child to materialize local axes or grids. An independent
automatic domain with no final values is an error; an explicit domain is valid.

The child limit is 100 after applying the combination policy. The same
10,000,000-unit partition-work limit used by `facet` applies. `facetGrid`
supports the same Cartesian, Polar, and Parallel chart families, scale policies,
axis restrictions, and compatible shared legends as `facet`.

See the [runnable grid example](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/facet-grid)
for a 2 × 3 full grid with one missing source pair.

## Repeat a positional encoding across fields

`repeatCharts` accepts direct materialized lookup and computed datasets as well as
ordinary source data. It changes the selected encoding field without rewriting
expressions or lookup inputs. A parent `editParameter` rebuilds repeated children
from the retained source when a repeated computed field depends on that parameter.

`repeatCharts` compares several fields without copying the complete unit recipe:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `unit`. Resource selectors used here: `target: "product"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const metrics = unit.repeatCharts({
  id: "metrics",
  target: "product",
  channel: "x",
  fields: ["speed", "quality", "cost"],
  columns: 3,
  guides: { legend: "shared" }
});
```

The action accepts `x` or `y` on one direct Cartesian mark, `theta` or public
`r` on eligible Polar Point/Line/direct Arc/Rose roles, and one
`{ parallelDimension: field }` on Parallel coordinates. The Parallel form
replaces exactly one dimension and preserves its position, field type, explicit
title, sibling dimensions, row key, and missing-value policy. `target` may be
omitted only when exactly one primary mark is eligible. Attached labels and
statistical-reference dependents owned by that target replay with it. Child IDs
and headers follow the ordered field list.

This fragment requires a complete Parallel-coordinate unit:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `parallelUnit`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const comparisons = parallelUnit.repeatCharts({
  channel: { parallelDimension: "horsepower" },
  fields: ["horsepower", "weight", "displacement"]
});
```

The repeated role defaults to independent domains; requesting it as shared
produces the union domain. Other used roles default to shared, and one compatible
non-repeated legend may be promoted to the parent.

Every repeated field can describe a different quantity, so outer-axis
promotion is rejected. Pie and Radar raw theta/r repetition, composite roles,
derived target datasets, and unrelated sibling layers also fail atomically.
See the [runnable repeat example](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/repeat-charts).

## Space between plots

Use `facet({ field: "group", spacing: "plot", gap: 5 })` when the five-pixel gap
should separate the data regions. The default `"canvas"` mode includes both
children's margins between those regions. Plot mode retains each data region's
size and reserves child margins once around the outer grid. Panel backgrounds
cover their plots; the parent background covers the surrounding area.

The same option works with `facetGrid`, `repeatCharts`, and facet
`editCompositionLayout`. Headers and retained guides must fit the specified gap;
otherwise the action reports a collision. `guides: { axes: "outer" }` removes
interior axes, but remaining edge labels still need enough space. Increasing the
gap or changing guide/header settings resolves those collisions without changing
panel dimensions.

## Share the existing top margin

With plot spacing, `topLane: "shared"` lets the parent title and top headers use the
existing child top margin and parent padding. The default `"stacked"` reserves their
height separately. This complete program retains seven 40 × 200 plots inside a
508 × 262 Canvas, including the upper Y-axis endpoint:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

export const days = ['Sun','Mon','Tue','Wed','Thu','Fri','Sat'];
export const rows = days.flatMap(panel => [{panel,group:'a',value:13},{panel,group:'b',value:14}]);

export function createFacetLaneUnit() {
  return chart().createCanvas({width:136,height:262,margin:{left:40,right:56,top:43,bottom:19}})
    .createData({values:rows})
    .createBarPlot({x:'group',y:{field:'value',scale:{domain:[0,50],nice:false}},guides:false})
    .encodeColor({field:'group',layout:'overlay'})
    .createAxes({x:{title:false,ticksAndLabels:{labels:{fontSize:10,color:'black',offset:5.5}}},
      y:{ticksAndLabels:{values:[0,10,20,30,40,50],labels:{fontSize:10,color:'black',alongOffset:.890625}},title:false}})
    .createLegend({title:'group',titleStyle:{fontSize:10},labels:{fontSize:10}});
}

export function createFacetSharedTopLaneProgram() {
  return createFacetLaneUnit().facet({field:'panel',values:days})
    .editFacetGuides({axes:'outer',legend:'shared'})
    .editCompositionLayout({spacing:'plot',gap:22})
    .editFacetHeaders({fontSize:10,fontWeight:400,offset:10.609375})
    .createTitle({text:'Grouped Bar Chart',align:'left',offset:-2.953125,
      titleStyle:{fontSize:13,fontWeight:700,color:'black'}})
    .editCompositionLayout({topLane:"shared"});
}

const program = createFacetSharedTopLaneProgram();
```

The same option works at facet, grid and repeat creation or in
`editCompositionLayout`. Text must fit and clear the plots and retained labels;
insufficient space reports a collision. Adjust explicit padding, title or header
settings to make space. The action keeps child dimensions and font sizes.

Omitting the option in an edit preserves it. Reset with
`editCompositionLayout({ topLane: "stacked" })`. To switch back to Canvas spacing,
reset both together: `editCompositionLayout({ spacing: "canvas", topLane: "stacked" })`.
Concat compositions reject this option. Shared legend placement keeps its existing
edge, offset and occupied bounds.

## Name the complete facet field

Panel names identify individual values; a field title names what all panels share.
Use the complete runnable example linked above.
Create a title through `headers.column.title`, or edit a prepared facet with
`editFacetHeaders({ role: "column", title: { text: "Region" } })`. Grids also support
`role: "row"`. Repeats require an explicit title text, just like ordinary facets.

A field title appears once across the union of occupied plots, including wrapped
or sparse layouts. It is independent of `createTitle`. Its font inherits the role
header unless overridden. Initial creation requires nonempty one-line `text`;
later title objects merge their changes. `title: false` removes the role title.
Common headers and `role: "all"` cannot own a title.

Title options are `text`, `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, `fontWeight`, `color`, `offset`,
`align`, `rotation`, and `alongOffset`. Alignment defaults to `"center"`, with
`"start"` and `"end"` also available. Rotation defaults to horizontal on top/bottom,
−90° on the left and +90° on the right; explicit rotations use the usual radians
or `{ value, unit }` form. `alongOffset` shifts along that edge.

The title's `offset` measures the distance to its nearest rotated ink edge from
the plot union with plot spacing, or the occupied child Canvas union with Canvas
spacing. The default clears same-side category headers and retained child margins
by 8 pixels. An explicit offset preserves that requested distance. Existing outer
margin and header space is reused once; only the remaining title lane is reserved.
Titles must fit without overlapping panel headers, plots or retained chart text.
A conflicting edit fails atomically. Omitting all title options preserves existing
charts exactly, and source, layout, theme, font metrics and saved editable programs
retain the field-title owner.

## Independently packed panels

For an existing Cartesian program with axes, this fragment packs complete visible panel
bounds while keeping every Y axis and one common bottom X footer per occupied column:

Use `program.facet({ field: "group", columns: 2, spacing: "content", gap: 16,
headers: { anchor: "view" }, guides: { axes: { x: "outer", y: "each" } } })`.
The program must already contain a `group` field and Cartesian mark encodings.

Panel plot sizes and logical group order stay fixed. Different axis labels or mark overflow
can give panels in the same logical row different plot origins. `gap` adds clearance between
measured content bounds. The parent Canvas includes the final footer, title and legend lanes.
The full-body `view` header anchor includes retained guides; `content` continues to measure
marks and the plot only. Both anchors accept plot or content spacing.

Use content spacing with wrapped `facet` or `repeatCharts`. Keyed `facetGrid` retains aligned
tracks and rejects it. Shared top lanes require plot spacing. Repeat keeps axes local and
rejects any `outer` channel. Per-channel policies require Cartesian coordinates.
`align` controls slots in canvas/plot spacing; content flow uses independent measured bounds.
