# Complete Axes and Labels

[Axis family overview](./api/axes/)

## Composite marks over guides

Use `underlay: true` when the complete Cartesian axis should be painted before
ordinary marks. The plot border accepts the same choice. This makes guides part
of the backdrop for a difference-blended bar. Geometry, clips and source rows
stay the same; the drawing order changes.

This complete example declares the axis first and then edits its placement:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
import {chart} from "ggaction";
export const rows=[{category:'a',value:6},{category:'b',value:9}];
export function createPlotUnderlayProgram({axisUnderlay=true,borderUnderlay=true,blend="difference"}={}){return chart()
 .createCanvas({width:240,height:180,margin:{left:40,right:20,top:20,bottom:40}})
 .editCanvas({plotBorder:{color:'#ddd',lineWidth:1,underlay:borderUnderlay}})
 .createData({values:rows})
 .createBarPlot({x:'category',y:{field:'value',scale:{domain:[0,10],nice:false}},guides:false})
 .encodeBarWidth({band:1})
 .editBarMark({fill:'yellow',stroke:'yellow',strokeWidth:4})
 .editBarMark({cornerRadius:10,blend})
 .createXAxis({line:{color:'#888',lineWidth:2},ticksAndLabels:false,title:false})
 .createGrid({horizontal:{values:[0,5,10],color:'#ddd',lineWidth:1},vertical:false})
 .editXAxis({underlay:axisUnderlay});}

const program = createPlotUnderlayProgram();
```

The option also works in `createXAxis`, `createYAxis`, nested `createAxes`,
guides and chart facades. Select a named axis through the existing `target` on
whole-axis edits. Focused component editors and Polar/Parallel axes keep their
existing options.

Omitted edits preserve placement. `editXAxis({ underlay: false })` restores
the ordinary overlay. Frame offsets and placement edits preserve each other.
All retained components move as one axis; marks and text keep their relative order.
Nonpositive Cartesian grids remain behind these underlays, and positive grid
`zIndex` values keep their existing position after marks. Source, scale, data,
Canvas, theme, facet and editable-persistence replay retain the requested placement.

## Independent named Cartesian axes

Create an axis with `id` when it needs an independent identity. The default IDs are
`x` and `y`. Refine or remove a named axis with `target`, which selects the axis,
not its mark or scale. This complete runnable program uses an independent right scale:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resource selectors used here: `target: "share"`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart().createCanvas({ width: 600, height: 400, margin: 80 })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 1, y: 2 }, { x: 2, y: 4 }] })
  .createScatterPlot({ x: "x", y: "y", guides: false })
  .createYAxis()
  .createScale({ id: "ratio", type: "linear", domain: [0, 1] })
  .createYAxis({ id: "share", position: "right", scale: "ratio", coordinate: "main" })
  .editYAxisTitle({ target: "share", text: "Share" });
```

`createAxes` and `createGuides.axes` also accept nonempty X/Y arrays, with an explicit
`id` in every entry. Arrays create axes in entry order and fail atomically if any
entry conflicts. A chart facade accepts the same arrays for its own position scales.
One axis may occupy each physical side of a coordinate; moving another axis there
fails even with a different frame offset. Named axes use one common side for their
components. Move the complete axis to change that side; focused edits preserve it.

An omitted `target` selects the canonical X/Y axis if present, otherwise the unique
named axis in that channel. Several named candidates require an explicit target.
Unknown IDs, wrong channels, conflicting scale/coordinate filters, reserved channel
IDs and duplicate graphic identities fail. Polar and Parallel axes do not accept
these selectors. A focused creator restores a missing component of an existing named
axis; the complete creator establishes its identity. Removing the final component
also removes the owner. Scale, data, Canvas, theme and editable persistence preserve
all remaining owners. A grid with several eligible scales requires an explicit scale;
conflicting axis tick policies require explicit grid `count` or `values`.

For facet `axes: "outer"`, named components follow their actual top, right, bottom
or left occupied edge, including incomplete rows. `axes: "each"` retains every axis.
Named text bounds must fit the Canvas and remain separate from other axis text.

## Moving a complete axis and refining its text

On an existing Cartesian program, create the full axis before focused text edits:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
program
  .createXAxis({ offset: 20, title: { text: "Measurement" } })
  .editXAxisTitle({ offset: -40, alongOffset: 30, align: "right" })
  .editXAxisTitle({ baseline: "bottom" })
  .editXAxisLabels({ align: "left" });
```

The complete-axis `offset` moves its line, ticks, labels and title outward together.
It must be non-negative; zero restores the plot edge. Marks and grids stay fixed.
Whole-axis edits validate labels against the final title position on the same axis,
including numeric title offsets. A genuine final collision still rejects the edit.
The nested title `offset` is signed: positive outward, negative into the plot.
`alongOffset` is a separate translation along the axis: positive right for X and
down for Y, even with a reversed scale. Numeric `at` still means a scale-domain value.

Title alignment (`left`, `center`, `right`) and baseline (`top`, `hanging`, `middle`,
`alphabetic`, `ideographic`, `bottom`) apply before rotation. Defaults remain center/middle.
Multiline titles keep their text and 1.2×font-size spacing; top/hanging/alphabetic
anchor the first line, bottom/ideographic the last, and middle centers the block.
Omitted edits retain explicit settings. Explicit defaults restore alignment/baseline;
remove and recreate a title without `offset` to restore automatic title clearance.

Explicit label `align` changes text anchoring before rotation while keeping existing
resolved label positions. It takes precedence over inferred side/flush anchoring.
Remove and recreate labels without alignment to restore inference. All final rotated
bounds must still fit, and axis-title/label collision checks remain active.

## Styling native tick dashes

Create a complete axis first, then refine its native ticks. On an existing Cartesian
program with a quantitative y encoding, this fragment keeps the zero tick solid:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
program
  .createYAxis({ ticksAndLabels: { values: [0, 1, 2] } })
  .editYAxisTicks({ strokeDash: [2, 2], strokeDashMap: [{ value: 0, strokeDash: [] }] });
```

Patterns contain an even number of finite non-negative lengths; `[]` means solid.
Map keys use raw typed values, so `1` differs from `"1"`. Missing map entries use the
uniform pattern. An omitted edit preserves the map; `strokeDashMap: "auto"` or `[]`
removes only its overrides. Values absent from the current ticks stay available for
later scale/data refresh. The same tick options work inside complete-axis creation,
whole-axis edits and ticks-and-labels groups. Polar and Parallel ticks are unchanged.

## `createAxes(options?)`

Creates complete axes for encoded Cartesian x/y, Polar theta/radius, or Parallel dimension channels. This is the recommended axis
action for ordinary chart authoring.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program.createAxes({
  y: { ticksAndLabels: { count: 6 } }
});
```

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `coordinate` | `{ id?, type? }` | unique coordinate used by x/y layers |
| `x` | axis options, nonempty named-axis array, or `false` | create when x is encoded |
| `y` | axis options, nonempty named-axis array, or `false` | create when y is encoded |
| `theta` | Polar axis options or `false` | create when theta is encoded |
| `radius` | Polar axis options or `false` | create when radius is encoded |

`coordinate.type` accepts `"auto"`, `"cartesian"`, `"polar"`, or `"parallel"` as a stored
type assertion.

An explicit coordinate ID and type must agree with the stored coordinate.
Options from another family are rejected, including `false`: x/y options
require Cartesian encodings, theta/radius options require Polar encodings,
and Parallel axes do not accept these channel-specific option objects.

Each x/y axis option supports:

| Option | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `scale` | scale ID; inferred when one scale is used on the channel |
| `position` | x: `"bottom"` or `"top"`; y: `"left"` or `"right"` |
| `line` | `false` or `{ color?, lineWidth? }` |
| `ticksAndLabels` | `false` or `{ count?, values?, ticks?, labels? }` |
| `title` | `false` or title options including `text`, `at`, `offset`, and font styling |

Cartesian `ticksAndLabels.labels.colorMap` accepts typed `{ value, color }` entries. It overrides individual raw tick colors and falls back to `labels.color`; it does not depend on the displayed text. Use `"auto"` to remove the map. Continuous keys must be finite numeric/timestamp values.

Use `ticksAndLabels.labels.flush: true` to keep unrotated X or Y label bounds inside the mapped axis span. It defaults to false and preserves the normal overlap policy; use explicit `overlap: "allow"` when neighboring labels intentionally overlap. Text, fonts and tick positions are retained. Rotated labels and a label wider than the entire span are rejected.

Set `ticksAndLabels.labels.flushThreshold` to a non-negative number when only ticks near a range edge should flush. Selection uses the mapped tick position, not the amount of text overflowing the edge. For example, `labels: { flush: true, flushThreshold: 1 }` only adjusts labels whose ticks are within one logical pixel of either endpoint. `0` selects exact endpoints. Omission preserves full label containment. Focused or whole-axis edits accept `flushThreshold: "auto"` to restore that behavior; omitted edits preserve the threshold. A stored threshold has no effect while `flush` is false. Reversed axes and wrapped label groups use the same policy.

Cartesian `ticksAndLabels.ticks.alongOffset` and `ticksAndLabels.labels.alongOffset` independently shift mapped positions in logical pixels. Positive moves right for X and down for Y; the default is zero. This preserves scale data and the outward label `offset`.

Use either `count` or exact data-space `values` for ticks. Ambiguous coordinates
or scales must be selected explicitly. `createAxes` reads stored coordinates;
it never creates or repairs them. Tick, label, and grid `count` values and
explicit `values` arrays are limited to 10,000 generated items.

Linear scales create numeric nice ticks. Time scales choose a UTC calendar
interval near the requested count and format labels automatically. Automatic
formatting starts from the domain span, then raises precision only when two
distinct resolved ticks would otherwise share a label. For example, a
1970–1982 domain produces `1970`, `1972`, ..., `1982`, while sub-month ticks
include the day needed to distinguish them. Explicit time values are finite
timestamps. Exceptionally long valid date domains use a nice multi-year step
when the fixed calendar interval would grossly oversample the requested count.

A band or point x scale uses its complete domain as the default tick and label
values. Each value is placed at the shared band or point center and formatted
with `String(value)`. Explicit `ticksAndLabels.values` may select a domain
subset in the requested order. Discrete axes reject `count` so categories are
not silently omitted. Reversed ranges and Canvas rematerialization preserve
the stored category values.

Cartesian labels and categorical theta labels can replace display
text without changing raw values:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const named = program.createXAxisLabels({
  labelMap: [
    { value: 1, label: "One" },
    { value: "1", label: "String one" },
    { value: "KR", label: "South Korea" }
  ]
});
```

Map lookup uses the typed raw value, so `1` and `"1"` remain distinct. Values
missing from the map use the normal formatter. Repeated visible labels do not
merge scale entries, ticks, legend symbols, or selections. An empty label
hides that text while retaining its item; `labelMap: []` stores an explicit
empty map and `labelMap: "auto"` removes the map. On continuous Cartesian axes, keys must be finite numbers or Unix-millisecond timestamps. Numeric strings, booleans, null and non-finite keys are rejected. A map only changes the displayed text; it does not change scale domains, tick positions or data. New ticks absent from the map use the existing numeric or UTC formatter. Continuous theta axes, radial axes, and Parallel dimension axes reject this option. The same option is available in focused label actions, nested
ticks-and-labels options, complete Cartesian axes, and categorical theta
facades.

For a binned histogram x encoding, omitted tick options use the inferred bin
boundaries. This keeps the axis aligned with every rect edge. Explicit
`ticksAndLabels.count` or `ticksAndLabels.values` takes precedence. Count y
axes use numeric nice ticks and infer titles such as `count(Displacement)`.

Titles are inferred from the unique encoding consuming each scale. Aggregate
encodings include their operation, so `mean` on `Acceleration` becomes
`mean(Acceleration)`. Pass `title.text` when inference is ambiguous or a custom
label is desired.

The default edges remain bottom for x and left for y. A complete axis forwards
an explicit edge to its line, ticks, labels, and title:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program.createAxes({
  x: {
    position: "top",
    ticksAndLabels: { labels: { format: ".1f" } }
  },
  y: { position: "right" }
});
```

Top ticks point upward and right ticks point right. Labels and titles are
placed outward from the selected edge. The Canvas margin must already be large
enough; guide creation does not resize it. A later explicit `fitCanvas()` call
can shrink excess margin on a Full unit chart.

Cartesian label styles accept `rotation`, `maxWidth`, `wrap`, `lineHeight`, and
`overlap` in focused label actions, ticks-and-labels groups, and complete axis
facades. Numeric rotations are radians; `{ value, unit }` accepts radians or
degrees. Setting a positive `maxWidth` stores deterministic word or character
wrapping as concrete text lines. Word wrapping is the default, and an oversized
word is split only between Unicode grapheme clusters using `Intl.Segmenter`.
Combining marks, Hangul sequences, and emoji clusters stay intact, even when a
single cluster exceeds `maxWidth`. LF, CRLF, and CR breaks preserve separate
lines and blank-line spacing. `lineHeight` defaults to `fontSize * 1.2`
and cannot be smaller than the font size.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
program.createXAxis({
  ticksAndLabels: {
    labels: {
      maxWidth: 72,
      wrap: "word",
      rotation: { value: -24, unit: "degrees" }
    }
  }
});
```

`overlap` defaults to `"error"`. Explicit `"allow"` permits label-to-label
intersection. Canvas overflow still fails; title-label collisions are controlled
separately by the title policy below.
`editXAxisLabels({ maxWidth: false })` or its y counterpart removes wrapping;
that reset cannot include `wrap` or `lineHeight` in the same call. Canvas and
scale replay rebuild the same lines from the stored policy. The 10,000-item
limit applies after wrapping.

### Intentional title-label overlap

A Cartesian title defaults to `overlap: "error"`. Set `title.overlap: "allow"`
when that title is deliberately placed across its own axis labels. This keeps
Canvas bounds and label-label checks active. Apply `labels.overlap` separately
when neighboring labels also overlap.

Fragment after a data-backed Cartesian chart has been created:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
.createAxes({
  y: {
    ticksAndLabels: { labels: { overlap: "allow" } },
    title: { text: "Group", offset: 80, overlap: "allow" }
  }
})
```

Focused title editors and whole-axis edits accept the same policy. Omitted edits
preserve it; an explicit `"error"` reset must fit without that collision. The
policy belongs to one axis title and remains valid when labels are created or
edited later, including named axes, facets and saved programs.

Cartesian title text preserves explicit hard line breaks as a centered block.
See [axis-title text and rotation](./reference/actions/guides/#ticklabel-groups-and-axis-titles)
for line spacing, blank lines and bounds checks.

Cartesian title `rotation` accepts a finite legacy number in radians or an
explicit `{ value, unit: "degrees" | "radians" }` object. Both forms normalize
to radians before materialization. This does not change the degree-valued
`angle` used to place radial-axis components.

Use axis-only `format: "ticks"` to infer fixed decimal precision from each axis's
settled numeric tick spacing. A step of `0.05` preserves labels such as `0.00`
and `−0.10`; a step of `100` uses integers. Independent facet scales calculate
precision separately from one shared recipe. Existing display-label maps take
precedence, and omitted/`"auto"` output stays unchanged. This option works on
numeric Cartesian, Polar and Parallel axes; time and discrete axes reject it.
The smallest positive spacing is normalized to twelve significant digits before
choosing precision. Precision increases only to distinguish different ticks,
up to twelve decimals; finer unsupported precision is rejected. One tick uses
its normalized decimal places, and an empty tick list stays empty. Values,
domains and tick positions are preserved. Edits and replay recompute the labels.

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```js
// Fragment: after creating a numeric y encoding.
program.createYAxis({
  ticksAndLabels: { labels: { format: "ticks" } }
});
```

Numeric label formats use `.0f` through `.12f` for fixed decimals, `.0%`
through `.12%` for percentages, and `.0e` through `.12e` for scientific
notation. A leading zero in a one-digit precision, such as `.01f`, is accepted
and means `.1f`.
UTC time formats compose `%Y` (year), `%m` (two-digit month), `%d` (two-digit
day), and `%b` (English abbreviated month) with literals, for example `%b %Y`,
`%Y-%m`, or `%Y/%m/%d`; use `%%` for a literal percent sign. Every time format
must contain at least one date directive, and unknown or dangling directives
are rejected. Numeric formats apply to quantitative scales, including log,
sqrt, pow, and symlog; time formats require a time scale. Discrete labels use
`"auto"` and may apply `labelMap`. The existing `{ decimals:
nonNegativeInteger }` form remains available for numeric labels. Explicit
formats remain exact and may intentionally produce repeated display strings.

The selected coordinate ID is stored on each semantic axis. Canvas size and
margin edits explicitly rematerialize positional scales and every connected
axis component.

A temporal aggregate-bar scale keeps its inset range for bar centers, ticks,
and labels. Its axis baseline alone spans the complete plot edge, matching the
crossing grid geometry so a differently colored zero-grid line cannot remain
visible as end caps. Reversed scales reverse the stored baseline endpoints
without changing that complete visible span.

The trace preserves its decomposition:

```text
createAxes
├─ createXAxis (when selected)
└─ createYAxis (when selected)
```

For a Polar coordinate, the same aggregate becomes:

```text
createAxes
├─ createThetaAxis
└─ createRadialAxis
```

`createThetaAxis()` creates the outer circular baseline, outward ticks,
perimeter labels, and an inferred title. `createRadialAxis()` creates one
center-to-edge baseline; its `angle` defaults to `90` degrees (right). Both
support `ticksAndLabels: { count?, values?, ticks?, labels? }` and title style.
Use `line: false`, `ticksAndLabels: false`, or `title: false` to omit components.
The radial title defaults to `position: "inside"` at the baseline midpoint.
Use `title: { position: "outside" }` to place it beyond the radial endpoint;
`offset` is measured from the midpoint normal when inside and from the endpoint
when outside.

For a Parallel coordinate, `createAxes()` delegates to public `createParallelAxes()`.
Each encoded field gets a baseline, ticks, labels, and a title. Use
`createParallelAxis({ field })` to create one missing field axis and
`editParallelAxis({ field, ... })` to edit its components. These actions are Full-only.

The following fragment assumes `program` has a Parallel dimension named
`Miles_per_Gallon` with existing axes:

> **Contextual fragment.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Caller-provided receivers: `program`. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
const styled = program.editParallelAxis({
  field: "Miles_per_Gallon",
  line: { color: "#7c3aed", lineWidth: 3 },
  title: { text: "Fuel economy", fontWeight: 700 }
});
const restored = styled
  .editParallelAxis({ field: "Miles_per_Gallon", ticks: false })
  .createParallelAxis({
    field: "Miles_per_Gallon", line: false, labels: false, title: false,
    ticks: { length: 10 }
  });
```

`field` is required and must match an encoded dimension. `target` uses the stored
axis owner or the unique encoded Parallel line. A different owner is an error.
Create requires missing components: omitted components get defaults, `false`
skips them, and all-disabled creation is invalid. Edit requires existing components:
objects patch, `false` removes, and omissions preserve. To remove a field's entire
axis, use `removeParallelAxis({ field })`; use `removeParallelAxes()` for all axes.
Removing the final component also clears the empty owner while preserving marks and scales.

Ticks and labels accept independent `count` or exact `values`, or share them through
`ticksAndLabels`. Do not combine the grouped and independent forms. Count is
quantitative-only; ordinal values must be domain members. Count and values are
mutually exclusive. Group members accept styles, not nested `false`.
Counts, value arrays, and each rendered collection are limited to 10,000 items.
Values must be distinct and inside the scale domain; an empty values array retains
an empty component. Label `format` follows [axis components](./advanced/axis-components/).

Defaults preserve the original Parallel appearance: line width 1.25, tick length 8,
automatic count 5, labels 9 pixels left at size 11, and titles 20 pixels above at size
13 and weight 600. Titles accept `text`, `offset`, color and font styles; labels
accept `offset`, format and font styles. Parallel axes do not accept Cartesian
positions, radial angles or title rotation, and do not fit the Canvas automatically.

Field styles and explicit titles survive resizing, scale edits and dimension
reordering. Removed fields lose their recipes. An owner created by `createParallelAxes`
also creates defaults for newly encoded fields; one started by `createParallelAxis`
keeps new fields hidden. Explicitly removed field axes stay hidden while their field
remains encoded. Recreate missing components through `createParallelAxis`.

For individual lines, ticks, labels, and titles, see
[Advanced axis components](./advanced/axis-components/).

Numeric labels also accept `","` for grouped integers and `",.0f"` through `",.12f"` for grouped fixed decimals. UTC formats accept `%a` for an English weekday abbreviation, such as `%a %d` → `Mon 01`. These formats use the shared axis, legend and text formatter.

An explicit Cartesian `labelMap` entry with `label: ""` hides only that displayed label. Tick marks, stored tick values and scale domains stay unchanged. Empty labels remain suppressed after Canvas/scale replay; clear the map with `"auto"` to restore the normal formatter.

<!-- Source: /tutorials/image-assets/ -->

# Place a retained image

Prepare image bytes explicitly, then use one image mark to control its fit,
alignment, viewport and alternative text. The [runnable example](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/image-assets/)
uses one pinned SVG asset for six placements and retains the bytes for offline export.

## Prepare and place

The canonical [example program](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/image-assets/program.js) loads its
inline asset through `prepareImageResource` and applies the returned handle to the
same immutable program. Its application-owned decoder reports the source dimensions.
The synchronous `createImageResource` action stores the validated bytes. Then
`createImageMark` places that resource in a square viewport.

```js
// Fragment after the exact prepared resource has been committed.
program = program.createImageMark({
  image: "logo",
  viewport: { x: 50, y: 60, width: 100, height: 100 },
  fit: "contain",
  align: [0.5, 0.5],
  alt: "Four colored quadrants with a white center"
});
```

`contain` preserves the whole source; `cover` fills the viewport and clips overflow;
`fill` scales both dimensions independently. `editImageMark` preserves omitted
options. Set `viewport:"auto"` to follow the plot size after resizing.

## Render and preserve

Browser Canvas uses `prepareImageRendering` with an explicit decoder and passes the
result as `render(program, context, {images})`. SVG, PNG and PDF export the retained
bytes without fetching the source URI. See [rendering](./api/rendering/#embedded-images)
for the decoder and resource budgets. The example's public program, explicit primitive,
and four backend tests share the same placement inputs.

Use `replaceImageResource` with a newly prepared replacement to update every image
mark that references the resource. Item keys and alternative text remain stable.
`removeMark` removes a placement while retaining the shared image source.

## Complete program

Run this browser ES module with `ggaction` installed and a `<canvas id="chart">` element.
The decoder also supports Node with the optional native Canvas peer.
The decoration primitives reproduce the example title and viewport background.

```js
import { chart, prepareImageResource, prepareImageRendering, render } from "ggaction";
const frame = { width: 200, height: 210 };
const viewport = { x: 50, y: 60, width: 100, height: 100 };
const fixtures = [{ title: "contain · center", fit: "contain", align: [0.5, 0.5] }];
const imageClip = false;
const assetSVG = '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="200" height="100" viewBox="0 0 200 100"><rect width="200" height="100" fill="#de5b49"/><rect x="100" width="100" height="50" fill="#397bb8"/><rect y="50" width="100" height="50" fill="#259782"/><rect x="100" y="50" width="100" height="50" fill="#edbd46"/><circle cx="100" cy="50" r="16" fill="white"/></svg>';
const assetHash = '97f99c97b9a4d34f5c4914c2cf9cd7a2df05e55ec2b9dbd08081609b808718c6';
async function decodeImage({ bytes, mimeType }) {
  let image;
  if (typeof globalThis.Image === "function") {
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([bytes], { type: mimeType }));
    try { image = new Image(); image.src = url; await image.decode(); }
    finally { URL.revokeObjectURL(url); }
  } else {
    const nativeModule = "@napi-rs/canvas";
    image = await (await import(/* @vite-ignore */ nativeModule)).loadImage(bytes);
  }
  return { image, width: image.width, height: image.height, originClean: true };
}
const base = chart().createCanvas({ width: frame.width, height: frame.height, margin: 0 });
const requestToken = "example-image";
const prepared = await prepareImageResource(base, {
  kind: "create", id: "logo", uri: "fixture:quadrants", expectedHash: assetHash, mimeType: "image/svg+xml"
}, { requestToken, load: () => ({ bytes: new TextEncoder().encode(assetSVG), mimeType: "image/svg+xml" }),
  decode: async request => { const { width, height, originClean } = await decodeImage(request); return { width, height, originClean }; } });

function createImageExample(fixture = fixtures[0]) {
  return base.createImageResource({ prepared, requestToken })
    .createGraphics({ id: "label", type: "text", parent: "plot-main" })
    .editGraphics({ target: "label", property: "x", value: 12 })
    .editGraphics({ target: "label", property: "y", value: 25 })
    .editGraphics({ target: "label", property: "text", value: fixture.title })
    .editGraphics({ target: "label", property: "fontSize", value: 14 })
    .editGraphics({ target: "label", property: "fontFamily", value: "Arial" })
    .editGraphics({ target: "label", property: "fontWeight", value: "normal" })
    .editGraphics({ target: "label", property: "textAlign", value: "left" })
    .editGraphics({ target: "label", property: "textBaseline", value: "alphabetic" })
    .editGraphics({ target: "label", property: "fill", value: "#243447" })
    .createGraphics({ id: "backdrop", type: "rect", parent: "plot-main" })
    .editGraphics({ target: "backdrop", property: "x", value: 50 })
    .editGraphics({ target: "backdrop", property: "y", value: 60 })
    .editGraphics({ target: "backdrop", property: "width", value: 100 })
    .editGraphics({ target: "backdrop", property: "height", value: 100 })
    .editGraphics({ target: "backdrop", property: "fill", value: "#e2e8f0" })
    .editGraphics({ target: "backdrop", property: "stroke", value: "none" })
    .editGraphics({ target: "backdrop", property: "strokeWidth", value: 0 })
    .createImageMark({ image: "logo", viewport, fit: fixture.fit, align: fixture.align,
      opacity: fixture.opacity ?? 1, clip: fixture.circleClip ? imageClip : false,
      alt: "Four colored quadrants with a white center" });
}

const program = createImageExample();
const images = await prepareImageRendering(program, {decode: decodeImage});
render(program, document.querySelector("#chart").getContext("2d"), {images});
```

## Add a pixel-alpha shadow

Use `editImageMark({target:"image",shadow:{color:"#0008",offsetX:4,offsetY:4,blurRadius:6}})` after creating an image mark. Use `shadow:false` to remove it. The actual image transparency shapes the shadow, and the image viewport clips the result. PNG and PDF prepare it automatically. For Canvas or SVG, call `prepareShadowRendering` with a Canvas factory and the image decoder, then pass the returned `shadows` handle to the renderer. Canvas also needs `prepareImageRendering` as above. Dispose the shadow handle when done and prepare again after editing the chart. See [rendering](./api/rendering/) for the complete host contract.

<!-- Source: /tutorials/font-assets/ -->

# Prepare fonts before text layout

Keep font loading explicit, measure with the loaded bytes, and save the final
text layout for offline output. The [runnable example](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/font-assets/)
uses licensed Korean and monochrome emoji subsets with fixed content hashes.
It includes a combining accent and a wrapped Korean title.

## Load, measure, apply

The canonical [program](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/font-assets/program.js)
first creates a title using the requested font families. Its initial estimated
layout is a usable immutable program while loading runs. For each named font,
`prepareFontResource` asks the application to load and decode bytes and verifies
the expected SHA256. `createFontResource` commits the prepared result to the exact
original receiver using the current request token.

`prepareTextMetrics` takes the explicit font IDs and asks the application to
measure every width needed by the existing layout. `applyTextMetrics` commits the
exact profile and rematerializes the title. Widths that have not been measured
cannot silently use an estimate. A late result for an edited receiver is stale.
The [host adapter](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/font-assets/host.js)
uses browser `FontFace` and Canvas measurement, or a native Canvas in Node.

## Draw the prepared text

The complete example entry below runs inside the linked example directory after
the standard browser module setup. Its local `program.js` performs the font
resource and metric preparation described above; `host.js` registers and releases
the exact requested font alias.

```js
import { render, prepareFontRendering } from "ggaction";
import { createFontExample } from "./program.js";
import { registerFont } from "./host.js";

const program = createFontExample();
const canvas = document.querySelector("canvas");
const fonts = await prepareFontRendering(program, { register: registerFont });
try { render(program, canvas.getContext("2d"), { fonts }); }
finally { fonts.dispose(); }
```

SVG embeds the same font bytes. PNG/PDF register them for the duration of output.
They use the stored lines and origins rather than measuring or wrapping again.
Editable snapshots retain the font resource and exact profile; graphic snapshots
retain self-contained concrete fonts. Restore does not fetch the original URI.

## Change labels or fonts

Edits that need only already measured queries stay synchronous. New labels may
need more queries: remove the exact profile with `removeTextMetrics()`, edit the
text, and prepare/apply a new profile on that receiver. Replacing a bound font
uses `prepareFontResource` with `kind:"replace"` and a measurement callback, then
`replaceFontResource`; bytes, metrics and text update together.

Restrictive `removeResource({kind:"font",id})` rejects an active metric binding.
Explicit cascade first removes the metric profile and recomputes estimated text.
See [embedded fonts](./api/rendering/#embedded-fonts) for the complete host
contracts, budgets, error behavior and registration lifetime.

The subsets only cover the example text. Choose fonts covering your own content;
the library does not claim that one font covers every script or emoji sequence.

# Hierarchy resources and plots

Create hierarchy data, compute an explicit layout, then draw a tree or treemap. These actions require the Full entry point. The [hierarchy tutorial](./tutorials/hierarchy/) uses the same public programs as the examples and renderer tests.

## createHierarchyData

```typescript
createHierarchyData(options: CreateHierarchyDataOptions): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Create a typed hierarchy from flat parent rows, nested children, or grouped paths.

Exactly one source form is required: `key + parent`, `key + children`, or `groupFields`. Typed keys distinguish numbers, strings and booleans. Values are finite and nonnegative. `leaf-sum` is the default; `inclusive` validates parent totals, and `own-plus-children` adds each own value to its children. Groups support only leaf sums. `forest:false`, `missingCategory:"error"` for groups, and `maxNodes:10000` are the defaults. An enabled forest or grouped source uses a synthetic root with no source contribution. Missing parents, cycles, duplicate keys and invalid values fail. Nested lineage retains the actual source member path.

## editHierarchyData

```typescript
editHierarchyData(options: EditHierarchyDataOptions): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Revise hierarchy input options and refresh every dependent layout and plot atomically.

Omitted options retain stored intent; the source form cannot change. A nonempty patch is required. A new data binding must resolve to a materialized dataset. Every dependent layout receives one new revision; its plots, labels and selections refresh. Raw and computed source revisions follow the same closure. Input programs and traces remain unchanged when any consumer fails.

## layoutHierarchy

```typescript
layoutHierarchy(options: LayoutHierarchyOptions): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Compute an explicit tree, treemap, or normalized partition layout from a named hierarchy.

`method` is `tree`, `treemap`, or `partition`. Tree requires finite nonnegative `nodeSize:[breadth,depth]`, `siblingGap`, `depthGap` and `orientation:"vertical"|"horizontal"|"radial"`. Radial additionally requires nonnegative `radius`, finite `startAngle` and `sweep` in `(0,360]` degrees. Treemap requires positive finite `size:[width,height]`, nonnegative `padding`, and `method:"slice-dice"|"squarify"`. Partition accepts only optional `maxNodes`. Input order is default; key/value ordering requires an explicit ascending/descending direction, and field ordering additionally requires a field, with optional nulls first/last and year/timestamp temporal unit. Ambiguous grouped sort fields fail. Layout results retain exact hierarchy revisions and numerical geometry.

## editLayout

```typescript
editLayout(options: EditLayoutOptions): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Patch a stored hierarchy or graph layout and refresh its existing consumers.

The existing layout method remains fixed. `options` is a partial patch of that method. Graph layouts require nonempty options and reject hierarchy-only `order`; see [graph layouts](./api/data/source-and-derived/#layoutgraph). Omitted targets select the current layout, then a unique layout, and reject ambiguity across both families. Changing a radial tree to vertical/horizontal removes its radial-only options. The proposed geometry and every plot are checked before state-changing child actions. Layout numeric intent has one owner and is independent of Canvas placement.

## removeResource

```typescript
removeResource(options: RemoveStoredResourceOptions): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Remove a named stored resource after checking exact dependencies.

`kind` identifies a stored resource; data, scale and coordinate use their existing dedicated removers. Restrict is default. `cascade:true` may remove generated dependents; authored dependents and live hierarchy plots still require explicit removal first. `removeMark` releases a plot while retaining its hierarchy/layout for reuse. Basic does not expose this method.

## createTreePlot

```typescript
createTreePlot(options: TreePlotOptions): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Draw hierarchy nodes and parent links from a stored tree layout.

The omitted first ID is `treePlot`; another tree plot needs an explicit ID. The layout must use method tree. Omitted layout uses current eligible context, then the unique eligible resource; ambiguity fails. Nodes default to radius 6, fill #2563eb, stroke #ffffff, width 1 and opacity 1. Links default to #94a3b8, width 1.5 and opacity 1; false disables them. `origin:"auto"` centers stored bounds in the plot frame; explicit `[x,y]` is plot-local. `clip:false` is default.

## editTreePlot

```typescript
editTreePlot(options: EditTreePlotOptions): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Edit tree nodes, links, labels, placement, or the bound tree layout.

A nonempty patch is required. Omitted values preserve style, meaning and placement; `links:{}` reenables links with stored/default style. New layout bindings require method tree. Unchanged node keys retain selection identity when geometry or order changes.

## createTreemapPlot

```typescript
createTreemapPlot(options: TreemapPlotOptions): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Draw nested rectangles from a stored treemap layout.

The omitted first ID is `treemapPlot`; another owner needs an explicit ID. The layout must use method treemap. Cells default to fill #3b82f6, stroke #ffffff, width 1 and opacity 1. Origin and clipping match tree plots. Internal labels are hidden when padding leaves no label band; zero-value rectangles retain finite zero-area geometry.

## editTreemapPlot

```typescript
editTreemapPlot(options: EditTreemapPlotOptions): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Edit treemap cells, labels, placement, or the bound treemap layout.

A nonempty patch is required. Omission preserves prior values; a new layout must use method treemap. Cell overrides and label identity follow the exact typed node keys, independently from rectangle order.

## Labels, overrides and retained identity

Labels are disabled by default. `labels:{}` displays each node total in 12px sans-serif; tree labels use offset `[0,14]`, treemap labels `[0,0]`. `labels:false` removes them. Set `content:"value"`, `fill`, `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, `fontWeight`, `offset` and optional `overrides`. Override text with `{key:"A",text:"Branch A"}` or `{path:["Europe","Denmark"],text:"Denmark"}` for grouped data. Body overrides use the same targets and their own paint fields. Arrays replace the prior override array.

Authoring rejects unknown or duplicate targets. When a source revision removes a previously styled node, its override becomes dormant and inspection reports `orphan-style`; the style returns only for the same typed key. String `"1"` and number `1` are different keys. Selection includes the node body and label, while links remain structural.

## Revising and restoring

Source and parameter revisions refresh dependent hierarchy resources, layouts and plots in order. Invalid topology, layout or concrete output leaves the original program unchanged. Concat children retain separate identities. Facets support complete subtree partitions; a partition that separates a child from its parent fails. Repeat positional field changes are not applicable.

Editable serialization retains layout geometry and exact source refs. Restore validates that state without running a layout algorithm. Canvas, SVG, PNG and PDF read the same concrete graphics. Empty sources produce empty models; zero totals produce finite zero-area partitions and an inspection diagnostic.

Body and label `fill` accepts the shared `FillPaint` contract: solid color, linear gradient, pattern or radial gradient. Pattern origins are materialized in object or plot coordinates, and text fills retain concrete glyph bounds. Layout, Canvas and data revisions recompute those bounds while preserving the authored fill. Stroke remains a solid color. Partition cells and labels use the same paint owner.

## Outlines and shadows

Body and label styles accept `outline:{color,width}|false` and `shadow:{color,offsetX?,offsetY?,blurRadius?}|false`, including per-item overrides. Omission preserves an effect during edits; false removes it, including an inherited role effect. Effects reuse the [mark appearance contract](./api/appearance/mark-style/). An authored outline and stroke in the same style patch conflict; an existing stroke is retained underneath the outline and returns when it is removed. Each effect preserves its original item identity and source geometry. Style edits, resize, highlight replay and offline restore do not rerun the stored layout.

Tree links accept shadow, while their ordinary stroke remains the link appearance.

<!-- Source: /tutorials/hierarchy/ -->

# Hierarchy tutorial

A hierarchy describes parent-child meaning. A layout computes positions, and a plot draws those positions. Keeping these steps separate lets two views share the same source while using different layouts.

## Run the maintained examples

Serve the repository over HTTP and open [the tree example](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/tree-layouts) or [the treemap example](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/treemap-layouts). Their canonical public programs are `examples/tree-layouts/program.js` and `examples/treemap-layouts/program.js`; the same functions produce the images and test fixtures on this page.

Use the Getting Started browser module setup with a canvas whose id is `chart`. This is the complete vertical tree program:

```javascript
import { chart, render } from "ggaction";

const vertical = chart()
  .createCanvas({
    "width": 640,
    "height": 500,
    "margin": {
      "left": 0,
      "right": 0,
      "top": 72,
      "bottom": 0
    },
    "background": "#ffffff"
  })
  .createData({
    "id": "hierarchy-source",
    "values": [
      {
        "id": "Root",
        "parent": null,
        "value": 10
      },
      {
        "id": "A",
        "parent": "Root",
        "value": 6
      },
      {
        "id": "B",
        "parent": "Root",
        "value": 4
      },
      {
        "id": "A1",
        "parent": "A",
        "value": 2
      },
      {
        "id": "A2",
        "parent": "A",
        "value": 4
      }
    ],
    "keyField": "id"
  })
  .createHierarchyData({
    "id": "hierarchy",
    "key": "id",
    "parent": "parent",
    "value": "value"
  })
  .layoutHierarchy({
    "id": "layout",
    "method": "tree",
    "options": {
      "nodeSize": [
        48,
        32
      ],
      "siblingGap": 112,
      "depthGap": 118,
      "orientation": "vertical"
    }
  })
  .createTreePlot({
    "origin": [
      320,
      28
    ],
    "nodes": {
      "radius": 18,
      "strokeWidth": 2,
      "overrides": [
        {
          "key": "Root",
          "fill": "#475569"
        },
        {
          "key": "A",
          "fill": "#2563eb"
        },
        {
          "key": "A1",
          "fill": "#60a5fa"
        },
        {
          "key": "A2",
          "fill": "#60a5fa"
        },
        {
          "key": "B",
          "fill": "#f59e0b"
        }
      ]
    },
    "links": {
      "strokeWidth": 2
    },
    "labels": {
      "offset": [
        0,
        32
      ],
      "fontSize": 14,
      "overrides": [
        {
          "key": "Root",
          "text": "Root · 10"
        },
        {
          "key": "A",
          "text": "A · 6"
        },
        {
          "key": "A1",
          "text": "A1 · 2"
        },
        {
          "key": "A2",
          "text": "A2 · 4"
        },
        {
          "key": "B",
          "text": "B · 4"
        }
      ]
    }
  })
  .createTitle({
    "text": "Tree · vertical",
    "subtitle": "One hierarchy, five stable nodes and four parent links",
    "align": "left",
    "alongOffset": 32,
    "offset": 2,
    "gap": 8,
    "titleStyle": {
      "color": "#0f172a",
      "fontSize": 20,
      "fontFamily": "sans-serif",
      "fontWeight": 600
    },
    "subtitleStyle": {
      "color": "#64748b",
      "fontSize": 12,
      "fontFamily": "sans-serif",
      "fontWeight": 400
    }
  });
render(vertical, document.querySelector("#chart").getContext("2d"));
```

Each program uses the same ordered action flow: `createCanvas`, `createData`, `createHierarchyData`, `layoutHierarchy`, then `createTreePlot` or `createTreemapPlot`, and `createTitle` for the heading. Explicit IDs bind the source, hierarchy and layout. Colors and text target typed node keys so a layout change cannot transfer a style to a different node.

## Change geometry while retaining meaning

Continue from `vertical` above with `vertical.editLayout({target:"layout", options:{siblingGap:150}})` to widen sibling spacing. Use `order:{by:"value",direction:"descending"}` in a subsequent layout edit to sort siblings by value. Each call rematerializes the dependent plot and leaves the original program unchanged.

Tree orientation is explicit. The radial variant additionally supplies radius, start angle and sweep. Angles are degrees clockwise from the top. Canvas changes move the stored layout into its plot frame; they do not rerun the hierarchy algorithm.

## Compare rectangle layouts

Slice-dice alternates subdivision directions. Squarify chooses rows to reduce extreme aspect ratios. Both preserve the hierarchy's values and typed node identities. Padding reserves space around children and permits internal labels; an internal label has zero opacity when no padding band remains.

## Edit data and remove views

Use `reviseData` for source values or `editHierarchyData` for hierarchy input policy. Both update the full dependent layout and plot closure. Unknown parents or invalid values reject the revision, leaving the earlier program and trace intact.

Removing a mark keeps its reusable layout. Remove the layout before its hierarchy, and remove the hierarchy before its source dataset. Shared or authored dependents are never silently discarded. See [Hierarchy resources and plots](./api/hierarchy/) for complete signatures, defaults, grouped and nested source forms, labels, sorting and removal rules.

<!-- Source: /api/graphs/ -->

# Graph plots

Create [observed graph data and a layout](./api/data/source-and-derived/#observed-graph-data), then draw the stored node positions. Full supports fixed, circular and deterministic force layouts. The [graph tutorial](./tutorials/graphs/) uses the same program as the browser and renderer examples.

## createGraphPlot

```typescript
createGraphPlot(options?: TargetedOptions<GraphPlotOptions>): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Draw circles, edge paths and optional labels from one graph layout. The first omitted ID is `graphPlot`; additional plots need explicit IDs. An omitted layout uses the current eligible graph layout, then the unique eligible layout. Missing or ambiguous inputs fail.

`origin:"auto"` centers the stored node bounds in the plot frame without scaling coordinates. An explicit `[x,y]` translates by plot-local pixels. `clip:false` is the default; true clips to the plot frame. Resizing the Canvas updates placement while preserving the layout result.

Nodes accept `radius`, `fill`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `opacity`, and `overrides`. Defaults are radius 6, fill #2563eb, stroke #ffffff, width 1 and opacity 1. Fill accepts the shared structured paint values. Each override combines the same optional style fields with a required original typed node `key`.

Edges accept `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `opacity`, `parallelGap`, `loopRadius`, `arrowSize`, and `arrows`. Defaults are #94a3b8, 1.5, 1, 16, 20, 8 and `"auto"`. Auto arrows follow graph direction; true forces arrows and false hides them. Dimensions are nonnegative finite pixel values. Opacity is in [0,1]. Parallel edges retain separate curved routes in source order; self-loops remain visible. A directed edge and its arrow share one logical identity.

## editGraphPlot

```typescript
editGraphPlot(options: TargetedOptions<EditGraphPlotOptions>): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Apply a nonempty patch to layout binding, placement, node/edge appearance, or labels. Omitted target selects the current eligible mark, then a unique graph plot; ambiguity fails. Omitted fields preserve stored intent. Override arrays replace their previous array. Null, undefined, unknown fields and invalid values fail before changing the program.

## Labels and identity

Labels are disabled by default. `labels:{}` displays original node keys; `labels:false` removes them. Defaults are fill #0f172a, 12px sans-serif normal, and offset `[0,14]`. Set `field` to one retained node attribute. Scalar values become strings, null/undefined become empty strings, and object/array values fail. Label overrides accept a typed key, optional text, and optional fill/font style; offset is shared by the plot.

Overrides must initially name existing distinct keys. A later source revision can make a stored override dormant. Inspection reports `orphan-style`, and only the same typed key can regain that style. Number `1` and string `"1"` remain different.

Selection fields include `kind:"node"|"edge"`, `key`, and node attributes as `attribute:<name>`. Edges additionally expose sourceKey, targetKey, weight, origin, directed and ruleId. Node degree/incoming/outgoing fields describe retained adjacency. Exact source rows distinguish the node and edge tables. An edge selection includes its arrow; a node selection includes its label.

Highlight `color` or `stroke` changes node borders, edge paths and arrow fill; label paint stays readable. Opacity and offset affect every component of the selected item. Fill, size, shape, fontSize and strokeDash highlights are unsupported. Use node style edits to change node fill or radius. Removing a highlight restores the current baseline.

## Updates, removal and outputs

Data, graph and layout revisions preflight all dependent plots, then update exact revisions and materialize nodes, edges, arrows and labels explicitly. Failure preserves the previous program and trace. Concat supports explicitly scoped plot/layout edits. Raw position encodings, axes and scale legends do not apply to these stored layout coordinates. Graph facet/repeat and induced filtering are not currently supported.

Remove a plot with `removeMark` before removing its bound layout or graph. Resource cascade does not silently remove live graph marks. Editable serialization validates stored data, layout and style without rerunning force simulation. Canvas, SVG, PNG and PDF consume the same concrete primitives. Inspection and accessible export count each node or edge once rather than counting its label or arrow again.

## Graph inference

Use `createInferredGraphData` when relationships follow a rule. The resulting
graph works with the same `layoutGraph` and `createGraphPlot` actions.

> **Executable complete.** Use an ES module with the imports, data, and prepared resource state described in this section. Resolve these names from setup in this fragment or section; alternatives branch from the same base.

```javascript
import { chart } from 'ggaction';

const program = chart()
  .createData({ id: 'points', keyField: 'id', values: [
    { id: 'a', x: 0 }, { id: 'b', x: 1 },
    { id: 'c', x: 3 }, { id: 'd', x: 10 }
  ] })
  .createInferredGraphData({
    id: 'neighbors', nodeKey: 'id', ruleId: 'nearest',
    rule: 'knn', features: ['x'], metric: 'euclidean',
    options: { k: 1, symmetrize: 'union' }
  })
  .layoutGraph({ id: 'placement', method: 'circular' })
  .createCanvas({ width: 400, height: 300 })
  .createGraphPlot({ labels: {} });
```

The inferred edges are a–b, b–c, and c–d, with weights 1, 2, and 7. Their identities
include `ruleId` and typed endpoint keys. Changing a threshold or source value
preserves the identity of a surviving relationship. A new `ruleId` denotes a
separate inference.

| Rule | Required rule options | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `knn` | None; `k` defaults to 1 | Nearest neighbors, with `directed`, `union`, or `mutual` symmetry |
| `radius` | `radius` | Include distances at or below the radius |
| `similarity` | `threshold` | Include cosine or Jaccard similarities at or above the threshold |
| `mst` | None | Minimum spanning tree of metric distances or an explicit candidate graph |
| `group` | `fields` | Connect equal typed groups as a clique or an explicit-hub star |
| `sequence` | `orderField` | Connect each row to the row `lag` positions later within its group |

Numeric metrics accept a field array. Jaccard also accepts `features: { set:
'attributes' }` for an array-valued column. Great-circle accepts `features: {
longitude: 'longitude', latitude: 'latitude' }` and returns distances in meters.
Preprocessing defaults to `none`; numeric metrics also support `standardize` and
`minmax`. Missing features fail unless `options.missing: 'omit-node'` is explicit.
Cosine zero vectors fail unless `options.zeroVector: 'zero-similarity'` is explicit.

Group and sequence rules do not accept metric features. A candidate MST uses
`candidateGraph: 'existingGraph'` with an undirected weighted graph and omits
metric features. Disconnected candidates require `options.forest: true`.

Search defaults to exact brute force. Use `options.search: { algorithm:
'kd-tree' }` for Euclidean or Manhattan neighbor/radius queries up to eight
dimensions, or `{ algorithm: 'grid' }` for radius queries up to three dimensions.
Approximate kNN requires `{ mode: 'approximate', seed: 42 }`; it records measured
recall and fails below its `minRecall` threshold, which defaults to 0.95. It never
silently substitutes approximate results for exact search.

`editInferredGraphData({ target: 'neighbors', definition: { options: { k: 2 } } })`
replaces the rule options and refreshes dependent layouts and plots. A different
rule requires its new `ruleId` and applicable definition. Source revisions also
refresh dependent inferred graphs; layout, canvas, and paint edits preserve the
topology. `candidateGraph: null` removes a candidate input, so provide metric
features in the same edit when switching to a complete metric MST.

Inference supports the Full entry point. Resource-backed graph plots currently
reject automatic facet partitioning and mark filtering. Create an explicitly
filtered dataset and a separate inferred graph when you need recomputation.

## Outlines and shadows

Body and label styles accept `outline:{color,width}|false` and `shadow:{color,offsetX?,offsetY?,blurRadius?}|false`, including per-item overrides. Omission preserves an effect during edits; false removes it, including an inherited role effect. Effects reuse the [mark appearance contract](./api/appearance/mark-style/). An authored outline and stroke in the same style patch conflict; an existing stroke is retained underneath the outline and returns when it is removed. Each effect preserves its original item identity and source geometry. Style edits, resize, highlight replay and offline restore do not rerun the stored layout.

Graph edges accept shadow on both the path and its arrow. Edge outlines are unsupported; edit their ordinary stroke.

<!-- Source: /tutorials/graphs/ -->

# Draw an observed network

Create two node rows and one observed directed edge. A fixed layout determines positions; the plot adds circles, an arrow and readable labels. This is the canonical graph example's action flow.

```javascript
import { chart, render } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({
    "width": 300,
    "height": 240,
    "margin": 0,
    "background": "#ffffff"
  })
  .createData({
    "id": "nodes",
    "values": [
      {
        "id": "A"
      },
      {
        "id": "B"
      }
    ],
    "keyField": "id"
  })
  .createData({
    "id": "edges",
    "values": [
      {
        "source": "A",
        "target": "B"
      }
    ]
  })
  .createGraphData({
    "id": "network",
    "nodes": "nodes",
    "edges": "edges",
    "nodeKey": "id",
    "source": "source",
    "target": "target",
    "directed": true,
    "selfLoops": true
  })
  .layoutGraph({
    "id": "positions",
    "graph": "network",
    "method": "fixed",
    "options": {
      "positions": [
        {
          "key": "A",
          "x": 60,
          "y": 120
        },
        {
          "key": "B",
          "x": 240,
          "y": 120
        }
      ]
    }
  })
  .createGraphPlot({
    "id": "networkPlot",
    "layout": "positions",
    "origin": [
      0,
      0
    ],
    "nodes": {
      "radius": 10
    },
    "edges": {
      "stroke": "#64748b",
      "strokeWidth": 2,
      "parallelGap": 90,
      "loopRadius": 32
    },
    "labels": {
      "offset": [
        0,
        24
      ],
      "fontSize": 14
    }
  });
render(program, document.querySelector("#chart").getContext("2d"));
```

## Preserve separate connections

The parallel example contains two observed edges with the same endpoints. Both survive as distinct paths and selections. The self-loop example retains an edge whose endpoints name the same node. Neither view infers new connections from position.

## Revise the view

Continue from `program` with `program.editGraphPlot({target:"networkPlot",nodes:{radius:14}})` to change node size. Use `editLayout` to change fixed positions, or create a separate circular/force layout and explicitly rebind the plot. Source revisions update dependent layouts and plots together. The original program remains available.

See [Graph plots](./api/graphs/) for full defaults, typed overrides, label attributes, selection and output behavior.

# Partition plots

## Shared contract

The Full entry point draws stored `layoutHierarchy({method:"partition"})` intervals as Cartesian rectangles or polar sectors. The hierarchy and layout contracts, typed key/path targets, label content, exact resource refs, source revision closure, facets and removal rules are owned by [Hierarchy resources and plots](./api/hierarchy/). These actions require the Full entry point. Renderers consume the same concrete rect/path/text output; restore validates stored intervals, view and mapping without running a layout algorithm.

A view changes projection, never hierarchy values or layout order. Focus is `null` (the current root), `{key:scalar}` for flat/nested input or `{path:scalar[]}` for grouped input. Focus must exist. `rootVisible:true` and `prunedSelection:"keep-hidden"` are defaults. A hidden root consumes no depth band. A synthetic forest root remains non-drawable. Zero totals retain node metadata and empty-value diagnostics; no equal-share area is invented. Inclusive residuals remain blank tails, not synthetic leaves.

All real nodes retain stable logical keys, original source lineage, fields and navigation metadata. `getMarkItems` reports visible geometry and `navigation` (parent, firstChild, sibling keys and root). Inspection reports focus, breadcrumb keys and diagnostics. Nonvisible nodes have no graphic or hit candidate. Label thresholds hide ink but retain the accessible name. Existing selection predicates remain active with keep-hidden; node-key/field predicates therefore retain selected hidden nodes and reappear on zoom-out. Property and aggregate selection predicates retain their existing reevaluation semantics. Explicit `drop` intersects the previous membership with visible node keys and stores the result through `editMarkSelection`; a later zoom-out does not resurrect those members.

A source revision which deletes explicit focus recovers the nearest surviving ancestor using the prior parent chain. If none survives, focus becomes the new root, or empty for an empty model. Inspection records the previous key and `ancestor`, `root` or `empty` reason. Explicit focus editing clears that diagnostic. Every dependent plot is preflighted before revision; a failure preserves the input program and trace.

Cartesian orientation is horizontal (value along x, depth along y) or vertical (value along y, depth along x). `reverseU` and `reverseV` reverse value/depth directions. Polar mapping uses degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock by default, `startAngle:0`, `sweep:360`, `direction:"clockwise"`, `innerRadius:0`, `outerRadius:"auto"`, `radiusPolicy:"equal-depth"`. Counterclockwise and equal-depth-area bands are explicit alternatives. Mapping follows the bound coordinate's effective frame and polarFrame; radii must fit the resolved available radius. Mapping fields remain stored when switching coordinate family. Coordinate/Canvas edits rematerialize that intent.

`padding` defaults to `[0,0]`; a scalar applies to both sibling and depth gaps. Values are nonnegative screen pixels. Cartesian gaps inset each side by half a gap; polar angular gaps use the local band mid-radius and radial gaps use pixels. Oversized gaps yield no ink, never negative geometry. `clip:false` is default. Cells and labels use the hierarchy style owner, including solid, linear gradient, pattern and radial gradient fills. Labels default to false; enabling `{}` uses total values. `minWidth:0` and `minArcLength:0` are nonnegative pixel thresholds. Cell overrides and label text use exact typed node targets.

## createPartitionPlot

```typescript
createPartitionPlot(options?: TargetedOptions<PartitionPlotOptions>): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Draw an icicle or sunburst from stored partition intervals. The first omitted ID is `partitionPlot`; another plot requires an explicit ID. Layout and coordinate use current eligible context, then a unique candidate; ambiguous state requires an explicit ID. With no coordinate, a Cartesian `main` coordinate is created. The complete proposed output is checked before changes.

## editPartitionPlot

```typescript
editPartitionPlot(options: TargetedOptions<EditPartitionPlotOptions>): ChartProgram
```

Chart authoring. Edit focus, mapping, cells, labels or a partition layout binding. Target uses current eligible context, then a unique partition plot. A nonempty patch is required. Omission preserves intent; `focus:null` returns to the root, `outerRadius:"auto"` follows the coordinate, and `labels:false` removes labels. A new layout must contain any retained explicit focus. Invalid edits leave the earlier chart unchanged.

See the [partition tutorial](./tutorials/partition/) for the maintained executable flow.

## Outlines and shadows

Body and label styles accept `outline:{color,width}|false` and `shadow:{color,offsetX?,offsetY?,blurRadius?}|false`, including per-item overrides. Omission preserves an effect during edits; false removes it, including an inherited role effect. Effects reuse the [mark appearance contract](./api/appearance/mark-style/). An authored outline and stroke in the same style patch conflict; an existing stroke is retained underneath the outline and returns when it is removed. Each effect preserves its original item identity and source geometry. Style edits, resize, highlight replay and offline restore do not rerun the stored layout.

# Partition tutorial

A partition assigns each node one normalized interval. Rectangular and radial views share its values, order and typed identity. The maintained program is [examples/partition-layouts/program.js](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/tree/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/partition-layouts/program.js); the example, tutorial and render tests consume that same program.

## Run the icicle

Use the Getting Started browser module setup with a canvas whose id is `chart`.

## Focus and return

Continue from `icicle` above. `icicle.editPartitionPlot({focus:{key:"A"}})` expands A and its descendants into the same frame. `focus:null` returns to the current root. `rootVisible:false` removes the focus node's band while retaining its descendants. Selection by node key or source field retains hidden members; choose `prunedSelection:"drop"` to discard hidden membership explicitly. A source revision that deletes the focused node recovers its nearest surviving ancestor and reports that recovery in inspection.

## Share intervals with a sunburst

The sunburst variant in the same maintained program binds a polar coordinate and uses `innerRadius:20`, `outerRadius:120` and two-pixel gaps. `radiusPolicy:"equal-depth-area"` makes equal squared-radius bands; `direction:"counterclockwise"` changes angular direction. These mappings preserve the partition values and layout resource.

Zero values retain metadata without artificial area. Inclusive parent residuals remain blank space. Tiny labels may be suppressed with `minWidth` or `minArcLength` while their names remain accessible. See [Partition plots](./api/partition/) for all defaults, coordinate rules, selection semantics and atomic errors.

# Flow data and Sankey layouts

Use explicit node and edge tables to show how quantities move between named
entities. Build a flow graph, store a layout, then draw links and nodes as
separate marks. These actions are available from the Full `ggaction` entry point.

The [flow tutorial](./tutorials/flows/) uses the same executable program as the
browser example and renderer tests. All renderers consume the same concrete
rectangles, text and closed ribbons.

## `createFlowData`

**Chart authoring.**

```typescript
createFlowData(options: CreateFlowDataOptions): ChartProgram;
```

Required options are `id`, `nodes`, `edges`, `nodeKey`, `source`, `target` and
`value`. The node and edge options name existing materialized datasets. Key and
endpoint columns accept a string or an array of column names for a compound key.
Numeric `1` and string `"1"` remain different keys. `target` names the edge's
endpoint column; create the resource inside its child chart before composing it.

Every endpoint must exist. `value` names one finite, nonnegative numeric column.
Zero-valued links and isolated nodes remain in the resource. Optional `edgeKey`
selects a unique typed edge key. Without it, parallel edges retain their source
row identities. Optional `attributes` selects node columns to retain in the
model. The graph is always directed.

Defaults are `balance: "allow"`, `selfLoops: false`, `maxNodes: 10000` and
`maxEdges: 10000`. `balance: "strict"` requires incoming and outgoing totals to
agree at internal nodes that have both incoming and outgoing edges. Sources and
sinks can have a net flow. The relative tolerance is `1e-12` of the larger total.
Overflow, missing endpoints, invalid values and exceeded work limits are errors.

Each node records incoming, outgoing, throughput and imbalance. Throughput is the
larger total; imbalance is incoming minus outgoing. Creating flow data produces
no graphics.

## `editFlowData`

**Chart authoring.**

```typescript
editFlowData(options: TargetedOptions<EditFlowDataOptions>): ChartProgram;
```

Use `{ target?, nodes?, edges?, definition? }`. Omitted values preserve the stored
source roles and definition; `definition` patches the creation options. A
nonempty edit increments the graph revision and updates dependent layouts,
node/link marks, labels and selections. A source `reviseData` follows the same
path. An invalid endpoint, balance, cycle or label field rejects the entire edit
and leaves the earlier program and trace unchanged.

Choose a flow explicitly with `target`, or rely on the current eligible flow and
then the only eligible flow. Ambiguous choices are errors. `editGraphData` is for
ordinary observed graphs; use `editFlowData` to retain flow semantics.

## `layoutFlow`

**Chart authoring.**

```typescript
layoutFlow(options: TargetedOptions<LayoutFlowOptions>): ChartProgram;
```

Use `{ id, graph?, method, options? }`. Choose `method: "dag"` for an acyclic
flow or `"cyclic"` to preserve feedback and self-loop links. DAG mode rejects
cycles even when their value is zero. Cyclic mode groups strongly connected
nodes and routes their internal links through separate outside lanes; it never
deletes an edge. It accepts any directed graph with finite nonnegative weights.
General graph layouts use the separate `layoutGraph` action.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`, `height` | `600`, `400` | Positive finite layout dimensions |
| `nodeWidth` | `16` | Positive node extent along the flow direction |
| `nodePadding` | `8` | Nonnegative gap between nodes in a column |
| `align` | `"justify"` | `"left"`, `"right"`, `"center"`, or `"justify"` |
| `order` | `"input"` | Input order, `"barycentric"`, or an explicit complete typed-key array |
| `iterations` | `6` | Deterministic relaxation passes, integer from 0 through 1000 |
| `laneGap` | `8` | Nonnegative spacing reserved for feedback lanes |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal"` | `"horizontal"` or `"vertical"` |
| `maxNodes`, `maxEdges` | `10000`, `10000` | Positive integer resource limits |

Left alignment follows longest-path ranks. Right alignment works back from
sinks. Justify moves sinks to the last column. Center keeps internal ranks and
places sources immediately before their first consumer. Input and explicit
orders preserve the order within each column. Barycentric order allows stable
reordering as centers relax.

All columns use one common value-to-thickness ratio. Node thickness represents
throughput; link thickness represents its value. All-zero input uses zero
thickness. Padding that cannot fit is an error. Vertical orientation transposes
the same geometry. Stored layout dimensions stay independent of Canvas size.

Use `editLayout({ target, options: { ... } })` to patch these options while
retaining the method. Existing marks update together. Snapshot restoration
validates the stored geometry and its source bindings without running the
placement solver again.

## `createFlowNodes`

**Chart authoring.**

```typescript
createFlowNodes(options?: TargetedOptions<FlowNodesOptions>): ChartProgram;
```

Use `{ id?, layout?, coordinate?, clip?, nodes?, labels? }`. The default mark ID
is `flowNodes` when available. The layout must be a DAG or cyclic flow layout.
Select a Cartesian coordinate explicitly, reuse the current/only eligible one,
or let the first mark create `main`. The entire layout, including feedback lanes,
is fitted uniformly into its frame. `clip` defaults to `true`.

`nodes` accepts `fill`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `opacity` and `overrides`.
Defaults are blue `#2563eb`, white stroke, width `1`, opacity `1`. Fill accepts
[structured paints](./api/appearance/). An override is `{ key, ...paint }` and uses an
existing original typed node key. Opacity zero remains a valid visible-item
identity.

Labels default to disabled. `labels: {}` enables keys; `content: "value"` shows
throughput and `content: { field: "name" }` reads a node source column. Missing
fields are errors. Label styles are `fill`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`
and `offset: [x, y]`. Defaults are `#0f172a`, `sans-serif`, `12`, `normal` and
`[0, 0]`. Label overrides accept `{ key, text?, ...paint }`.

Source edits retain an override whose key disappears and report it as an orphan
style. New override assignments must reference existing keys.

## `editFlowNodes`

**Chart authoring.**

```typescript
editFlowNodes(options: TargetedOptions<EditFlowNodesOptions>): ChartProgram;
```

Use `{ target?, layout?, coordinate?, clip?, nodes?, labels? }`. Omitted options
preserve existing values. Styles patch existing styles; an `overrides` array
replaces the whole array. `labels: false` removes labels and their placement
configuration. Empty edits are rejected.

## `createFlowLinks`

**Chart authoring.**

```typescript
createFlowLinks(options?: TargetedOptions<FlowLinksOptions>): ChartProgram;
```

Use `{ id?, layout?, coordinate?, clip?, links? }`. The default ID is `flowLinks`.
Layout and coordinate inference match node marks. Link styles accept the same
body paint fields as nodes, with defaults `#64748b`, stroke `"none"`, width `0`,
opacity `0.45`. Link overrides require an explicit `edgeKey` in the graph;
automatic occurrence IDs are not authored typed keys. Links do not own labels.

Create links before nodes to draw node bodies above their attachments. Forward
links use closed cubic ribbons. Feedback and loop links use closed lane ribbons.
Canvas, SVG, PNG and PDF read these same primitives.

## `editFlowLinks`

**Chart authoring.**

```typescript
editFlowLinks(options: TargetedOptions<EditFlowLinksOptions>): ChartProgram;
```

Use `{ target?, layout?, coordinate?, clip?, links? }`. A nonempty edit patches
styles or changes the exact layout/coordinate binding after validating the full
result. Invalid edits preserve the earlier program.

## Consumers and lifecycle

Flow marks support item inspection, source-row lineage, selection/highlighting,
Canvas and coordinate rematerialization, snapshots, and composition with other
charts through `hconcat` and `vconcat`, including exact child-target edits.
Automatic `facet` and `repeatCharts` partitioning is incompatible with flow marks:
the node and edge tables require coordinated partition rules, so these actions
reject the input without changing it. Node items expose `key`, `value`, `incoming`, `outgoing` and `imbalance`;
link items expose `source`, `target` and `value` alongside unique source fields.

Position, node thickness and link thickness belong to the flow layout. Ordinary
position/size encodings and automatic axes/legends do not apply to these marks.
Use typed style overrides for body appearance and selection/highlighting for
emphasis. Remove marks with `removeMark` before removing their layout or graph
with `removeResource`; live consumers are protected by dependency checks.
Highlight strokes apply to node and link bodies. Node labels share highlight
fill, opacity and offset while retaining their text appearance.

Every action returns an immutable program. Unknown options, explicit
`undefined`, invalid keys and ambiguous omitted references are rejected.

## Outlines and shadows

Body and label styles accept `outline:{color,width}|false` and `shadow:{color,offsetX?,offsetY?,blurRadius?}|false`, including per-item overrides. Omission preserves an effect during edits; false removes it, including an inherited role effect. Effects reuse the [mark appearance contract](./api/appearance/mark-style/). An authored outline and stroke in the same style patch conflict; an existing stroke is retained underneath the outline and returns when it is removed. Each effect preserves its original item identity and source geometry. Style edits, resize, highlight replay and offline restore do not rerun the stored layout.

<!-- Source: /tutorials/flows/ -->

# Draw conserved flows

Start with a node table and an edge table whose values have one shared unit.
A flow graph validates the endpoints and values, a layout stores their positions,
and two marks draw the ribbons and nodes.

This runnable Full example sends six units from one source and four from another
to a total of ten. The layout preserves a common thickness scale.

```javascript

  .createCanvas({

      }
    ],

    "id": "edges",
    "values": [
      {
        "id": "a",
        "from": "Supply A",
        "to": "Total",
        "value": 6
      },
      {
        "id": "b",
        "from": "Supply B",
        "to": "Total",
        "value": 4
      }
    ],
    "keyField": "id"
  })

    "id": "flow",
    "nodes": "nodes",
    "edges": "edges",
    "nodeKey": "id",
    "source": "from",
    "target": "to",
    "edgeKey": "id",
    "value": "value",
    "balance": "strict"
  })
  .layoutFlow({
    "id": "layout",
    "method": "dag",
    "options": {
      "width": 400,

  .createFlowLinks({
    "links": {
      "opacity": 0.55,
      "overrides": [
        {
          "key": "a",
          "fill": "#2563eb"

          "fill": "#f59e0b"
        }
      ]
    }
  })
  .createFlowNodes({
    "nodes": {
      "overrides": [
        {
          "key": "Supply A",
          "fill": "#2563eb"
        },
        {
          "key": "Supply B",
          "fill": "#f59e0b"
        },
        {
          "key": "Total",
          "fill": "#0d9488"
        }
      ]
    },
    "labels": {
      "content": "value",
      "fill": "#ffffff",
      "fontSize": 14,
      "fontWeight": 600
    }
  })
  .createTitle({
    "text": "Flow · two sources, one total",
    "subtitle": "Ribbon thickness preserves the explicit source values",
    "align": "left",
    "alongOffset": 0,
    "offset": 2,
    "gap": 8,
    "titleStyle": {
      "color": "#0f172a",
      "fontSize": 20,
      "fontFamily": "sans-serif",
      "fontWeight": 600
    },
    "subtitleStyle": {
      "color": "#64748b",
      "fontSize": 12,
      "fontFamily": "sans-serif",
      "fontWeight": 400
    }
  });
```

Draw links first so node bodies cover the attachments. `balance: "strict"`
checks internal nodes; sources and sinks may have a net flow. A source revision
updates the graph, layout and both marks together, or rejects the entire change
if it would invalidate an endpoint or conservation rule.

For feedback, select `method: "cyclic"`. All edges remain represented, including
self-loops when the flow graph explicitly enables them. Outside lanes are part
of the stored bounds, so fitting and clipping include their full extent.

The [shared example source](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/7cc2977f4cc083d091c7c69046ac9b52da9f2b9d/examples/flow-layouts/program.js)
also demonstrates vertical flow and typed per-item colors. The browser example,
primitive comparisons and generated figures use that one program.
See [Flow Data and Sankey Layouts](./api/flows/) for exact options, selection
fields, defaults and lifecycle behavior.
